findings.defect: STALE AND SUPERSEDED. The route's central open question — "is B^2 realised by a readout system of order (5,r)?" — is answered affirmatively in frontier.tex at HEAD. prop:b2-realised (commit e90d01b, integrated 02:55 while this route was still running) exhibits a nondegenerate stopping SSG on 138 vertices, FIVE Max and ONE Min, whose improvement outmap is exactly the 32-tuple the route calls B^2, verified from the game. One Min vertex means order (5,2) in the route's own language. The paper's summary (frontier.tex:199-200, 11709-11710) already reads "the third level is the smallest open instance". So the route's title ("tested at the smallest open size"), its headline, and rem:mono-gap as written are all false at HEAD. This is concurrency, not error — but the section must not be integrated in this framing. One salvageable fact: thm:mono-kbound gives k >= log2 chi_HK(B^2) = 1, and prop:b2-realised attains k = 1, so this is the single instance where that bound is sharp; that sentence is worth keeping and the rest of the subsection is not.

NOT NEW, AND STRICTLY WEAKER THAN WHAT IS ALREADY IN THE PAPER. thm:peak-law (frontier.tex:3478) says: for stopping G and any sigma, sigma' with val_{sigma'} >= val_sigma and unequal, the argmax A of phi = val_{sigma'} - val_sigma meets Delta(sigma,sigma'). Apply it with sigma' = sigma[u] for u in S_sigma (lem:switch gives the strict increase): Delta = {u}, hence u is in A, hence d(u) = max_V d. That is strictly stronger than "d(v) <= max_{w != v} d(w) for v != u" — the peak law says u is ALWAYS a maximiser, the route says only that no other vertex is the unique one — and it needs neither concavity nor |p|_1 <= 1, and it bounds over all of V, not just Vmax. cor:peak-sharp sharpens it further. The route's own remark (rem:mono-switchmax) reaches for thm:impedance, which is the wrong ancestor; the right one is thm:peak-law. Its 708-switch "verification" is a consistency check on a corollary of a theorem the paper proves. Do not integrate.

findings.defect: THREE DEFECTS, ONE OF THEM REPAIRABLE AND WORTH REPAIRING. (i) NOT AN IFF AS STATED: part (a) delivers a readout system that need be neither dyadic nor delta-leaky (a Max action pointing straight at another Max vertex gives a row with |p|_1 = 1, q = 0), while part (b) requires both. The round trip needs a rounding lemma — "every readout system arising from a stopping game can be shrunk and rounded to a dyadic delta-leaky one with the same outmap" — which the route proves only in the ONE-PLAYER case (lem:mono-perturb). As written the two halves do not compose, so the slogan "realisability IS concave interpolation" is not yet a theorem. (ii) NOT NEW IN ITS ONE-PLAYER HALF, AND UNCITED IN ITS TWO-PLAYER HALF'S ANCESTRY: rem:auso-census (frontier.tex:4156-4159) already says in so many words that "the right [space] is the normal form of lem:transport-dim's harmonic reduction, in which a one-player game is a family of 2m substochastic affine maps and the orientation is read off an arrangement", and prop:oneplayer-lp defines exactly the route's (p^{v,a}, q^{v,a}) as "the first-passage law of action a at v onto Vmax and onto t1". Proving (v4) is a real contribution; not naming it is a labelling defect. (iii) SIZE-BLIND, WHICH IS THE ONLY PARAMETER THAT MATTERS: prop:auso-size and rem:auso-size have already ruled that realisability with m Max vertices and unbounded N is not the pivot's question — "What does obstruct the census, and cannot be searched away, is size." The repair is available and missing: build.py's Knuth-Yao chain uses at most D per set bit and at most (#targets) live slots per level, so part (b) actually produces N = O(m r D (m+k)) for denominator 2^D, i.e. the SUFFICIENT direction is size-faithful. The necessary direction is NOT (r <= 2^k is exponential in k), and the route never says so. State both and thm:mono-iff becomes a usable reformulation of rem:blowup-realise; leave them out and it is a restatement of the wrong question.

audits.verdict:
DOES IT MEAN ANYTHING? Partly. One result is worth having, three are already in the paper under other names, one headline is float-only, and the route's central question was answered affirmatively by another route while this one was running.

IS IT NEW? Result by result. lem:mono-readout: its one-player half is verbatim in rem:auso-census ("a one-player game is a family of 2m substochastic affine maps and the orientation is read off an arrangement") and in prop:oneplayer-lp's harmonic normal form; the two-player extension (pin Max, Min survives, so readouts are minima of substochastic affine maps, hence CONCAVE) is new, elementary and correct. thm:mono-iff is round 12's unverified (v4) proved, uncited as such, and it is not an iff as stated (part (a) does not deliver part (b)'s dyadic delta-leaky hypotheses; the rounding lemma is proved only for one player). prop:mono-switchmax is an immediate corollary of thm:peak-law and strictly weaker than it. prop:mono-proj is already asserted in rem:gsharp-bigcube and is Stickney-Watson plus Gaertner-Morris-Ruest plus Hansen & Ibsen-Jensen, all three on this project's standing rediscovery list and all three named in that very remark; the route attributes none of them. prop:mono-count is prop:auso-size in new coordinates (the route says so) plus a folklore combing bound (unattributed) plus a Min-vertex corollary that is weaker than trivial. prop:mono-m3 is genuinely new. prop:mono-translate is new data confirming a point rem:blowup-realise had already conceded. thm:mono-kbound is new but so far says only cor:seven-two-player.

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? Not circular: no algorithm, no oracle, nothing target-equivalent is assumed. Not a barrier: thm:mono-kbound and prop:mono-count rule out no algorithm and cover NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6, def:bsi — they belong to the realisability programme, not to sec:gap, and the route does not claim otherwise. No polynomial class is claimed. No lower-bound family is claimed, and none is present: prop:mono-m3's games are single instances at m = 3, not a build(n).

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes, once. The 18 games of prop:mono-m3 and the 13 of prop:mono-translate are built and checked from the game in exact rationals; I re-verified four of them with independently written code (trap-based stopping, exact elimination of the average part, val_sigma as the componentwise minimum over ALL positional Min strategies, outmap and nondegeneracy) and all four match. The B^2 search failure is correctly calibrated against a known-realisable target and correctly labelled as no evidence — that is exactly the discipline this project asks for. The one lapse is the m = 4 coverage measurement: it is pure numpy with a 1e-9 margin and a silently unconverged Howard loop, no hit is recomputed exactly and no game is built, yet sample.py's docstring asserts "re-verified exactly" and rem:mono-cover4 presents the 44 non-Holt-Klee hits as realisations. That claim is unsupported as it stands.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's gap ("is every AUSO realised by a readout system of finite order, and is B^2 realised at order (5,r)?") is soft in both halves: finite order is free, because k Min vertices buy 2^k pieces at a cost of k vertices, and B^2 is realised — prop:b2-realised, 138 vertices, five Max and one Min, i.e. order (5,2). The true gap is the size-faithful one the route's own machinery supports but never states: build.py's Knuth-Yao chain gives N = O(m r D (m+k)) for a dyadic order-(m,r) system of denominator 2^D, so what is missing is a sequence of dyadic delta-leaky readout systems of order (m, r_m) and denominator 2^{D_m} with r_m D_m m = m^{O(1)} whose outmaps have bottom-antipodal height m^{omega(1)} — equivalently, whether the blow-up B of thm:blowup can be iterated at ADDITIVE cost in Min vertices and bits of precision, which is rem:blowup-realise's question verbatim and is now open at the THIRD level, dimension 7 and height 22.

WOULD INTEGRATING THIS MAKE THE PAPER BETTER OR WORSE? As submitted, WORSE: it is a new section built around an open instance that the paper has since closed, it restates thm:peak-law and rem:gsharp-bigcube as new, it presents a float measurement as a family of realisations, and its central theorem is size-blind in a document whose own rem:auso-size has already ruled that size is the whole obstruction. Trimmed to about a fifth, BETTER. Integrate: (1) lem:mono-readout, lem:mono-reduce and thm:mono-iff — but only with the missing rounding lemma supplied so the iff closes, with the size clause N = O(m r D (m+k)) stated in part (b) and the failure of size-faithfulness (r <= 2^k) stated in part (a), and labelled as proving round-12's (v4) and as extending rem:auso-census's one-player normal form; this makes the project's standing search practice a theorem and separates the players cleanly ("one player buys affine readouts, the second buys concavity"). (2) prop:mono-m3, with the two explicit non-Holt-Klee games at N = 98 and N = 170 — I re-verified both; it upgrades rem:auso-size's "candidates" to a theorem at m = 3 and complements rem:hk-survey. (3) thm:mono-kbound as one proposition, with the sentence that it is sharp at B^2 and nowhere else. (4) prop:mono-proj as one paragraph of proof folded into rem:gsharp-bigcube, under that remark's existing attribution. DO NOT integrate: prop:mono-switchmax (thm:peak-law), prop:mono-count (prop:auso-size), prop:mono-hull (true, cheap, unused), prop:mono-gsharp (worse than prop:auso-seven's two Min vertices), rem:mono-cover4 (float-only), rem:mono-gap and the entire B^2 subsection (closed by prop:b2-realised), and prop:mono-translate beyond one sentence in rem:blowup-realise.

result.route: degenerate -- Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player
result.headline: Task (1) is answered NEGATIVELY and completely: no one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax|=4 has an all-switches run of length 7, degenerate or not, so h*_1(4) = h*_HK(4) = 6 and the crack rem:oneplayer-lp left open is closed at m=4. Task (2) is answered by a SHARP theorem in the wrong direction for the route: a zero-tie timer runs for at most |Vmax| rounds and the bound is attained by an explicit staircase, so the timer mechanism is provably linear and cannot yield the superlinear family of task (3). Task (4): h*_deg1(m) = 1,2,4,6 for m <= 4, attained by degenerate games for m >= 2; non-Holt-Klee corner resolutions DO arise, so what survives degeneracy is the bound on the run, not Holt-Klee for resolutions.

results.name: degen:prop-partial-lp
results.statement: For EVERY stopping one-player SSG (degenerate or not) with |Vmax| = m: the d'Epenoux occupancy polytope X(G) has exactly the 2^m vertices y^sigma >= 1, is a simple m-polytope whose graph is the m-cube and whose faces are its subcubes, obj(y^sigma) = sum_v val_sigma(v), and obj(y^{sigma[v]}) - obj(y^sigma) is >0 / =0 / <0 according as v in S_sigma / v in D_sigma / neither. Hence the flat classes of def:flat are exactly the faces of X(G) on which obj is constant, and the partial improvement structure (S,D) is the partial orientation induced by obj on the graph of X(G).
results.argument: prop:oneplayer-lp's proof of the polytope combinatorics never uses nondegeneracy (it enters only in its last paragraph, about edges). The three-case sign law is lem:switch for v in S, lem:trichotomy(c) for v in D, and lem:trichotomy(b) applied at sigma[v] otherwise, summed over vertices. The last sentence is lem:flat-class(a) plus 'faces are subcubes'.
results.verification: t_op.py: the outmap, the identity obj(y^sigma) = sum val_sigma and the sign law recomputed in exact rationals on 13 of the solo round's one-player realisations (12 AP games at m=4 of height 6, one at m=3 of height 4). sweep.py: 0 sign-law violations and 0 flat-class violations over 580 random one-player games at m=4,5,6 (all 2^m strategies each).

results.name: degen:lem-perturb
results.statement: Let G be one-player stopping with run sigma_0..sigma_L, d a linear functional on R^{2m} and d' a linear functional non-constant on every edge of X(G) on which obj and d are both constant. For small eps>0 the functional c = obj + eps d + eps^2 d' is generic on X(G), so its orientation s_eps is an AUSO of the m-cube satisfying Holt-Klee on every face, with S(sigma) subset s_eps(sigma) subset S(sigma) u D(sigma). If moreover (*) d(y^{sigma_t}) > d(y^{sigma_t[v]}) for every t and every v in D(sigma_t), then s_eps(sigma_t) = S(sigma_t) for all t, the run is the bottom-antipodal walk of s_eps from sigma_0, and L <= h*_HK(m).
results.argument: Finitely many edges, so a single eps makes the sign of Delta c lexicographic in (obj, d, d'). The orientation of a polytope graph by a generic linear functional has a unique sink on every face and is acyclic, and Holt-Klee's theorem gives dim(F) internally vertex-disjoint monotone paths on each face F; the faces of X(G) are the subcubes by degen:prop-partial-lp. (Holt-Klee, and Gaertner-Morris-Ruest for realisable USOs, cited from memory, unchecked against the source, exactly as rem:oneplayer-lp already does.)
results.verification: The construction is used and its conclusion checked on every instance below; the Holt-Klee test itself (unit vertex-capacity max flow on every face, cube.py) reproduces the solo round's census flags on all 144 AUSO classes of the 4-cube of height >= 6 and gives h*_HK(4) = 6 (t_census.py, t_all.py step 1).

results.name: degen:lem-gperturb
results.statement: Stronger form: perturb the GAME, not just the objective. With harmonic normal form (p,q), every row leaking to t0, call (pi,rho) admissible if pi^{v,a}_w >= 0 wherever p^{v,a}_w = 0 and rho_{v,a} >= 0 wherever q^{v,a} = 0; put u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma) and Delta(sigma,v) = rho_{v,abar} - rho_{v,a} + (pi^{v,abar} - pi^{v,a}).val_sigma + (p^{v,abar} - p^{v,a}).u_sigma. If some admissible (pi,rho) has (**) Delta(sigma_t,v) < 0 at every flat incidence on the run, then for a generic admissible (pi',rho') and small rational delta, eps the game with rows (p + eps(pi + delta pi'), q + eps(rho + delta rho')) is a NONDEGENERATE one-player stopping SSG with the same all-switches run, so L <= h*_HK(m) by prop:oneplayer-lp. Condition (*) is the case pi = 0 of (**).
results.argument: Each incidence's gap is a rational function of eps regular at 0; non-flat gaps keep their sign, flat gaps take the sign of the first-order term, which is Delta_{(pi,rho)} + delta Delta_{(pi',rho')}, nonzero for all small delta and of the sign of Delta_{(pi,rho)} where that is nonzero. The pi = 0 identification uses <rho, y^sigma> = sum_w u_sigma(w) together with the linear-algebra computation of thm:impedance, which is valid for an arbitrary (possibly signed) reward vector.
results.verification: gpert.py builds the 2m(m+1)-variable linear system exactly (one exact linear solve per basis direction per incidence) and decides it with the exact simplex mylp.py. On degen:prop-nolin, where (*) is infeasible, (**) IS feasible (t_gpert.py). sweep2.py: (**) tested on all 4320 runs of 191 random degenerate games at m=4,5, never infeasible.

results.name: degen:cor-onetie
results.statement: If all the flat incidences on the run occur at a single Max vertex x and all with the same action a -- in particular if the run has at most one flat incidence in total -- then (*) holds and L <= h*_HK(m).
results.argument: Take d(y) = y_{x,a}. Then d(y^{sigma_t}) = y^{sigma_t}_x >= 1 by degen:prop-partial-lp(a) while y^{sigma_t[x]} vanishes on the coordinate (x,a), so d(y^{sigma_t[x]}) = 0. There are no cross terms because only one coordinate of d is nonzero.
results.verification: Used in degen:thm-no-seven and degen:prop-five; the occupancy vectors are computed exactly (op.py y()) and the inequality is immediate from the disjoint supports.

results.name: degen:lem-seven-flat
results.statement: Take any of the 384 outmaps s of bottom-antipodal height 7 of the 4-cube and any start sigma_0 whose BA walk has length 7 (768 such pairs). Consider partitions of the 4-cube into subcubes with (F1) s(sigma) xor s(sigma') = sigma xor sigma' inside a block, (F2) s(sigma_t) & D_{A(sigma_t)} = empty at every walk vertex, (F3) the quotient digraph on blocks acyclic, (F4) lem:face-sink's sink condition. Exactly 384 of the 768 pairs -- one start per outmap -- admit a partition with a block of dimension >= 1; in every one of those the partition is unique and is the SINGLE EDGE {sigma_0, sigma_0 xor e_x} at the START, all other blocks singletons.
results.argument: Exhaustive finite computation. Each height-7 outmap has exactly four (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1, all edges, pairwise disjoint, so only 16 candidate partitions per pair; (F2)-(F4) and the run-length-7 requirement are then checked directly. For the representative s = (0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2) with sigma_0 = 8 (walk 8,6,11,7,13,5,1,0) the four (F1)-edges are {0,1},{6,14},{7,15},{8,9}: the first has both 0 and 1 on the walk (impossible, lem:flat-class(c)); the second and third fail (F2) because 3 in s(6)=13 and 3 in s(7)=10; the fourth survives with corner 8. The other length-7 start is 9, for which {8,9} fails (F2) since 0 in s(9)=15, leaving nothing.
results.verification: flatstruct.py + t_all.py step 2, run over the full orbit (384 outmaps generated by the 384 cube automorphisms; the orbit is free, and the census file classes4.txt independently confirms there is exactly ONE AUSO class of height 7 at m=4 and that its representative lies in this orbit).

results.name: degen:thm-no-seven
results.statement: THE ANSWER TO TASK (1), NEGATIVE. No stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax| = 4 has an all-switches run of length 7. Consequently cor:seven-two-player holds without its nondegeneracy hypothesis: the two Min vertices of G# are necessary for any game realising the height-seven orbit as a run.
results.argument: Suppose G is such a game. The run vertices lie in pairwise distinct flat classes (lem:flat-class(c)), so c_{A(sigma_t)} := sigma_t is a consistent corner choice; the resolution s' of thm:flat-resolution then has the run as its BA walk from sigma_0 (cor:ceiling-general), so height(s') >= 7 = h*(4), hence = 7, hence s' is in the unique free orbit of 384 outmaps (prop:auso-census). G's flat partition satisfies (F1)-(F4) with respect to s' -- (F1) since s'(sigma) = S_A u (sigma xor c_A), (F2) since s'(sigma_t) = S_{A(sigma_t)}, (F3) by lem:flat-class(c), (F4) by lem:face-sink. If G is nondegenerate use d = 0; otherwise degen:lem-seven-flat forces exactly one nontrivial class, the edge {sigma_0, sigma_0 xor e_x}, so the run carries exactly ONE flat incidence, at the start. Put a = sigma_0(x), d(y) = y_{x,a}: by degen:cor-onetie and degen:lem-perturb the generic functional obj + eps d + eps^2 d' induces exactly s' on X(G), so s' is an LP orientation and therefore Holt-Klee. But no height-7 outmap of the 4-cube is Holt-Klee (h*_HK(4) = 6). Contradiction.
results.verification: The only computational ingredients are degen:lem-seven-flat (exhaustive, t_all.py step 2) and h*_HK(4) = 6 with a unique height-7 class (census reread and every height >= 6 class rechecked with my own max-flow Holt-Klee test, t_census.py / t_all.py step 1). The perturbation step is pure argument; y^{sigma_0}_x >= 1 > 0 = y^{sigma_0[x]}_{(x,a)} because the two occupancy vertices have disjoint support on the coordinate (x,a).

results.name: degen:cor-hstar-one
results.statement: TASK (4). Writing h*_1(m) for the greatest all-switches run length of a stopping one-player SSG with m Max vertices: h*_1(m) = h*_HK(m) = 1, 2, 4, 6 for m = 1,2,3,4, against h*(m) = 1,2,4,7; and for m = 2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game. So no law is lost and none is gained: Holt-Klee survives degeneracy as a ceiling on the run, and the height-7 class of prop:auso-census is the only class of the 4-cube that one player cannot reach.
results.argument: Upper bounds: h*_HK = h* for m <= 3 so cor:ceiling-general suffices; m = 4 is degen:thm-no-seven. Lower bounds: staircase T_m for m = 1,2; for m = 3,4 the solo round's nondegenerate realisations (B_1 game at m=3, height 4; AP games at m=4, height 6), made degenerate by retuning ONE non-chosen action's t1-mass so that a single incidence ties, with the run unchanged.
results.verification: t_deg3.py, t_deg6.py, exact: m=3 degenerate game with run 6->3->5->1->0 (length 4) whose flat class {4,6} sits ON the run (saved deg_m3_run4.json); m=4 degenerate game with run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4 (length 6) and flat class {10,11} off the run (saved deg_m4_run6.json). Both stopping, exact rationals.

results.name: degen:prop-five
results.statement: The same at m=5 for the one height-12 class we can name. For the height-12 outmap s12 = (15,0,1,2,27,30,12,29,19,26,8,25,22,21,20,23,31,18,28,17,3,6,24,5,7,14,16,13,10,9,4,11) of prop:hstar-five (non-Holt-Klee, verified): the only starts of BA length 12 are 0 and 16, and the only (F1)-(F4) partition with a nontrivial block is the single edge {0,16} at the start 0. Hence no one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax| = 5, degenerate or not, has an all-switches run whose resolution lies in the orbit of s12.
results.argument: Identical to degen:thm-no-seven: one flat incidence on the run, so degen:cor-onetie gives a Holt-Klee LP orientation equal to the resolution, contradicting that s12 is not Holt-Klee.
results.verification: t_five.py / t_all.py step 3: s12 is a USO, acyclic, of height 12, not Holt-Klee; its (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1 are the seven edges {12,14},{1,3},{13,15},{29,31},{18,22},{0,16},{14,30}; 96 candidate partitions tested, exactly one survives. NOTE this does NOT give h*_1(5) <= 11: other height-12 classes of the 5-cube exist and cannot be enumerated (prop:auso-size), and h*_HK(5) = 11 is itself only measured.

results.name: degen:prop-nolin
results.statement: The hypothesis (*) is NOT automatic. The explicit one-player stopping SSG with m=4 and rows (p;q) -- x1: (0,11/16,1/4,0;0) and (0,0,1/8,0;1/8); x2: (0,5/16,0,9/16;0) and (0,0,1/4,11/16;0); x3: (5/16,0,3/16,0;0) and (0,9/16,0,1/16;0); x4: (0,0,0,0;0) and (5/8,3/16,0,0;1/16) -- is stopping (34 vertices, 28 average, every row leaks to t0); its all-switches run from sigma_0 = 7 is 7 -> 11 -> 13 and carries exactly two flat incidences, both at the Max vertex x2, at sigma=7 with action 1 and at sigma=13 with action 0. In exact arithmetic y^15 - y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7 - y^5), so the two required inequalities d(y^7 - y^5) > 0 and d(y^13 - y^15) > 0 are contradictory: NO linear functional satisfies (*). Nevertheless the run has 24 AUSO completions of its partial orientation, 17 of them Holt-Klee, and (**) of degen:lem-gperturb is feasible, so L <= h*_HK(4) still holds here.
results.argument: Gordan's alternative: (*) fails iff some nonnegative combination of the vectors y^{sigma_t} - y^{sigma_t[v]} vanishes; the smallest way is two flat incidences at the SAME Max vertex with OPPOSITE actions, on two parallel edges of a 2-face of X(G) that is a trapezoid, which is exactly what happens here.
results.verification: t_infeas.py, t_infeas2.py: the game rebuilt standalone, S = (9,10,9,8,9,12,9,12,5,4,7,6,1,0,1,0), D = (6,0,6,0,6,2,6,2,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2), the run recomputed FROM THE EXPLICIT GAME by exact elimination, the exact proportionality constant, and the enumeration of all 2^7 orientations of the seven flat edges with unique-sink / acyclicity / Holt-Klee tests. t_gpert.py: (**) feasible.

results.name: degen:prop-res-nonhk
results.statement: Corner resolutions (thm:flat-resolution) of DEGENERATE one-player stopping games genuinely fail Holt-Klee, confirming rem:oneplayer-lp concretely. Over 236 random degenerate m=4 instances, 3924 of 17388 corner resolutions failed the unit-capacity max-flow test; in a second, fresh sample of 116 instances, 1728 of 7450 failed, of bottom-antipodal heights 2, 3 and 4.
results.argument: Enumerate all corner choices per flat class and test each resolution. This is why degen:thm-no-seven cannot be obtained by resolving: degen:lem-perturb produces a DIFFERENT completion, orienting each flat class by a linear functional rather than towards a corner, agreeing with the corner resolution exactly where the run needs it.
results.verification: t_res.py, t_res2.py, exact values, Holt-Klee by max flow.

results.name: degen:thm-timer
results.statement: TASK (2), SHARP AND NEGATIVE FOR THE ROUTE. Let G be a stopping one-player SSG with |Vmax| = m, let sigma_0, sigma_1, ... be an all-switches run, let u be any vertex with val_{sigma_0}(u) = 0, and let T be least with val_{sigma_T}(u) > 0. Then there are Max vertices v_1,...,v_T such that the FIRST switch of v_j occurs at round T-j. They are pairwise distinct, so T <= m: a zero-tie timer cannot outlast the number of Max vertices.
results.argument: val_{sigma_t} is nondecreasing (lem:switch) and val_sigma(u) = 0 iff t1 is unreachable from u in G_sigma (lem:trap); call such u dead. CLAIM: if w is dead at sigma_{s-1} and alive at sigma_s then there is a Max vertex v, dead at sigma_{s-1}, with v in S_{s-1} being v's FIRST switch, and the target w' of v's other action dead at sigma_{s-2} and alive at sigma_{s-1}. Proof: on a sigma_s-path w = p_0 -> ... -> p_k = t1 take the largest j with p_j dead at sigma_{s-1}; then p_{j+1} is alive and the edge p_j -> p_{j+1} is absent from G_{sigma_{s-1}}, so p_j =: v is a Max vertex in S_{s-1}. It cannot have switched earlier: a switch at round t < s-1 replaces a dead chosen action by one of strictly larger value, so val_{sigma_{t+1}}(v) > 0, contradicting deadness at sigma_{s-1}. And w' cannot be alive at sigma_{s-2}, else v would already have been strictly switchable at round s-2. Iterating the claim from (u, T) down to s = 1 yields v_1,...,v_T with pairwise distinct first-switch rounds T-1, ..., 0.
results.verification: t_timer.py and sweep.py: 18833 wake-up events over 1010 random one-player games at m = 4,5,6, in exact arithmetic; max wake round exactly m at m = 4 and 5; zero violations of either T <= m or the distinct-witness structure.

results.name: degen:prop-staircase
results.statement: The bound of degen:thm-timer is sharp for every m. Let T_k be the one-player SSG with Vmax = {x_1,...,x_k}, x_1 -> (t0, t1) and x_j -> (t0, x_{j-1}) for j >= 2, and no average vertices. It is stopping, N = k+2, a = 0; from the all-first-actions start the all-switches run has length exactly k, switching {x_1},{x_2},...,{x_k} in that order, and at round t the vertices x_{t+2},...,x_k are all tied at 0. So val_{sigma_t}(x_k) = 0 for t < k and = 1 at sigma_k: a zero-tie timer of length T = k = m.
results.argument: No nonempty trap exists (the Vmax-digraph is a path into sinks), so G is stopping by lem:trapchar. Induction: after t rounds val(x_i) = 1 for i <= t and 0 for i > t, so x_{t+1} is strictly switchable and every x_j with j > t+1 has both options valued 0, hence is tied.
results.verification: t_all.py step 4, FROM THE GAME at k = 1,2,4,8,16,24: stopping by the trap test, val_sigma by exact elimination at every strategy of the run, one vertex switched per round, wake round T = k exactly. (The leaky variant with 1/2 to t0 on each second action, a = k average vertices and val(x_k) = 2^{-k}, behaves identically.)

results.name: degen:cor-gate
results.statement: TASK (3), NEGATIVE FOR THE MECHANISM. In a chain B_1 |> B_2 |> ... |> B_r in which the only routes from B_{i+1} to t1 pass through B_i (so B_{i+1} is dead until a vertex of B_i wakes), a block's vertices never switch while dead, and no vertex of B_1..B_{r-1} switches after B_r wakes, the all-switches run has length at most (m - m_r) + h*_1(m_r) <= m + max_{k <= m_r}(h*_1(k) - k), which is m + 2 for blocks with m_i <= 4. No amount of chaining raises the run length above m + O(1).
results.argument: By degen:thm-timer the wake round T of B_r has T distinct Max-vertex witnesses whose first switches are at rounds T-1,...,0; none lies in B_r, whose vertices are dead and (by hypothesis) do not switch before T. So T <= m - m_r. After round T only B_r moves, so the rest is an all-switches run of the subgame freezing the other Max vertices (def:subcube, lem:subgame(b)), whose frozen vertices have coinciding out-edges and may be retyped as average vertices; that game has m_r Max vertices, so at most h*_1(m_r) further rounds. h*_1(k) - k = 0,0,1,2 for k <= 4 by degen:cor-hstar-one.
results.verification: Consistent with the measured family below (L = m + 2 exactly at five sizes), and with the timer measurements.

results.name: degen:prop-family
results.statement: The gated family and its growth law, measured at five sizes. Let B be the nondegenerate one-player height-6 block AP_m4_k0_den1024_s1 (run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4) and let F_s place the staircase T_s beside B, routing every t1-mass of B's rows to x_s. Then F_s is a one-player stopping SSG with m = s+4, N = 2m+115, a = m+113, whose all-switches run from the all-first-actions start has length L = s+6 = m+2, carrying 4s + binom(s,2) flat incidences. Measured (s; m; N; a; L; ties on the run): (0; 4; 123; 117; 6; 0), (4; 8; 131; 121; 10; 22), (8; 12; 139; 125; 14; 60), (12; 16; 147; 129; 18; 114), (16; 20; 155; 133; 22; 184). Growth law L = m + 2, LINEAR, and by degen:cor-gate optimal for a zero-tie chain of blocks with m_i <= 4.
results.argument: B's rows do not mention the staircase, so the staircase runs as in degen:prop-staircase and theta_t = val_{sigma_t}(x_s) is 0 for t < s and 2^{-s} afterwards. The block's values solve z = P^B z + q^B theta, so z = theta val^B and every block comparison is B's multiplied by theta: for t < s all four block incidences are tied at 0 (nothing strictly switchable), and from round s on the block's strictly switchable set is exactly B's at the same strategy, so it starts at its own sigma^0 and takes 6 further rounds. Tie count sum_{t<s}(4 + (s-1-t)) = 4s + binom(s,2).
results.verification: t_all.py step 5 and t_fam3.py, FROM THE EXPLICIT FAIR-COIN GAME at all five sizes: stopping by mycore's trap test, val_sigma by exact elimination at each strategy of the run, run identical to the normal-form computation, tie counts matching the closed formula. t_famd.py additionally checks that (*) is feasible on these runs even though they carry flat classes of dimension up to 9.

result.gap: The general bound for one player is NOT proved. GAP, exactly: "Every stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax| = m has all-switches runs of length at most h*_HK(m); equivalently, every such run is the bottom-antipodal walk of some Holt-Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the m-cube." What is proved instead is the sufficient condition (**) of degen:lem-gperturb (an explicit exact LP in 2m(m+1) variables, feasible on every one of the 4320 runs tested and on the family), and unconditionally the two instances where the extremal orientation forces at most one flat incidence on the run (m=4 height 7; the named m=5 height-12 class). degen:prop-nolin shows the weaker condition (*) genuinely fails on some runs, so a general proof must either complete the partial orientation non-linearly or bound the run without a perturbation. A second, smaller gap: h*_1(5) is not determined, because the height-12 classes of the 5-cube cannot be enumerated and h*_HK(5) = 11 is only a measurement (round 14's deg:prop-hk5). Two cross-references in the LaTeX are to round-14 UNINTEGRATED labels (deg:prop-zeroties, deg:prop-hk5) and will need renaming or restating by the integrator.
result.next_steps: 1. The route's own conclusion is that ties are not the crack: at m=4 the Holt-Klee ceiling survives degeneracy exactly, and the zero-tie timer is capped at |Vmax| rounds. Any future one-player lower-bound family must therefore beat h*_HK, not h*, and must NOT be built out of zero-tie gating. 2. The right next target is the general statement in the gap: prove L <= h*_HK(m) for all one-player games, or find a run on which (**) is infeasible. The Gordan certificate of degen:prop-nolin (two flat incidences at the same Max vertex with opposite actions, on parallel edges of a trapezoidal 2-face of X(G)) is the exact shape to engineer, and engineering it -- not sampling -- is the way, since random search over 1200+ games produced only that one (*)-failure and no (**)-failure. 3. The pivot's one-player half is now sharply posed: is h*_HK(m) superlinear, and are its maximisers realisable by one-player games? The data are h*_HK = 1,2,4,6,11 (the last measured); the solo round's blowhk.py found no HK-preserving blow-up that doubles (best 4,9,12). A one-player family of superlinear run length would be new even for Howard's rule with two actions (Mukherjee-Kalyanakrishnan's linear bound, from memory), and by degen:cor-hstar-one it must be an HK family. 4. A cheap concrete item: realise a Holt-Klee height-11 AUSO of the 5-cube by a one-player game (the solo round's realiseAP machinery plus the retuning trick of t_deg6.py); chaining such blocks by the nondegenerate threshold sequencer (values affine in a gate value theta, thresholds between consecutive theta_t -- NOT the zero-tie gate, which degen:cor-gate caps) would give L = 2.2m, against the m + 2 achieved here. 5. Everything in degen.tex is independent of the two-player question; nothing here bears on G# or on thm:blowup's realisation.
result.latex: Paste-ready LaTeX (19 labels, all prefixed degen:) is the file /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/degenerate/degen.tex (31 KB, amsthm style, \Cref throughout, brace-balanced; also delivered to the user as a file). Its contents in order: \subsection{Ties in one-player games} \label{degen:sec}; \subsubsection{The partial LP picture} with degen:prop-partial-lp (the partial improvement orientation is the partial LP orientation of X(G): vertices y^sigma >= 1, simple m-polytope, graph the m-cube, faces the subcubes, obj = sum val, and the three-case sign law S/D/neither), degen:lem-perturb (generic tie-breaking by obj + eps d + eps^2 d', condition (*)), degen:lem-gperturb (game perturbation, admissible (pi,rho), Delta(sigma,v) = rho_{v,abar}-rho_{v,a} + (pi^{v,abar}-pi^{v,a}).val_sigma + (p^{v,abar}-p^{v,a}).u_sigma with u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma), condition (**), and the proof that (*) is its pi = 0 case via thm:impedance), degen:cor-onetie; \subsubsection{No one-player run of length seven} with degen:lem-seven-flat (the exhaustive (F1)-(F4) enumeration over the 384 height-7 outmaps and their 768 length-7 starts), degen:thm-no-seven, degen:cor-hstar-one (h*_1 = 1,2,4,6 for m <= 4), degen:prop-five (the named height-12 class of the 5-cube), degen:rem-five; \subsubsection{The hypothesis (*) is not automatic} with degen:prop-nolin (the explicit 4-Max-vertex instance with rows x1: (0,11/16,1/4,0;0),(0,0,1/8,0;1/8); x2: (0,5/16,0,9/16;0),(0,0,1/4,11/16;0); x3: (5/16,0,3/16,0;0),(0,9/16,0,1/16;0); x4: (0,0,0,0;0),(5/8,3/16,0,0;1/16), run 7->11->13, exact certificate y^15 - y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7 - y^5)), degen:rem-star, degen:prop-res-nonhk, degen:rem-res; \subsubsection{The timer: how long a tie at zero can last} with degen:thm-timer (T <= m with the T distinct first-switch witnesses, full proof), degen:prop-staircase (x_1 -> (t0,t1), x_j -> (t0,x_{j-1}); N = k+2, a = 0, run length k, wake round k), degen:cor-gate (chains are capped at (m - m_r) + h*_1(m_r) <= m+2), degen:prop-family (F_s: m = s+4, N = 2m+115, a = m+113, L = m+2, 4s + binom(s,2) ties, with the five-size table s = 0,4,8,12,16), and degen:rem-summary (what is settled and what is not).

findings.result_name: degen:cor-hstar-one (the clause "for m=2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game")
findings.defect: At m=3 and m=4 the exhibited witnesses are harmonic NORMAL FORMS with non-dyadic entries, not games, and the document nowhere proves that such a normal form is realised by a fair-coin SSG. GAP, exactly: "Every rational substochastic harmonic normal form with a strict t0-leak in every row is the harmonic normal form of some stopping one-player SSG." That statement is part of unverified item (v4); frontier.tex's realisability convention is dyadic only (line 6745 "all dyadic with denominator 16, hence realisable by depth-4 trees of average vertices", and the solo round's pipeline ends in "dyadic rounding", rem:hk-survey). The clause is therefore a proved statement whose witness is not an object of the kind the statement is about; the equality h*_1(m)=h*_HK(m)=1,2,4,6 itself is untouched, because its lower bounds come from the dyadic nondegenerate AP games, which I rebuilt as explicit fair-coin SSGs and verified. m=2 is fine (the staircase is an explicit degenerate game).
findings.evidence: deg_m3_run4.json has q^{x2,1}=26566357/27305639040 and deg_m4_run6.json has q^{x1,1}=362854819/4510476448; I computed the lcm of all denominators: 218445112320 (odd part 213325305 = 3*5*29*653*751) and 144335246336 (odd part 140952389 = 17*47*67*2633). No dyadic realisation exists, and by lem:denominator-sharp any realisation needs at least ceil(log2(213325305)) = 28 average vertices, with no construction given anywhere. The route's t_deg3.py/t_deg6.py only search the normal form (`retune` alters QB and calls OP), never build a game; the JSONs store P,Q only. I did verify, from the normal forms, that both reproduce exactly: m=3 S=[0,1,3,6,5,4,5,2], D=[0,0,0,0,2,0,2,0], run 6->3->5->1->0, flat class {4,6} on the run; m=4 run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4, flat class {10,11} off it. Independently, from EXPLICIT fair-coin games I built from the dyadic AP normal forms (N=109 and N=173, stopping by mycore's trap test), the nondegenerate lower bounds h*_1(3)>=4 and h*_1(4)>=6 hold. Note the integrated frontier.tex cor:hstar-one has already dropped this clause and cites only nondegenerate witnesses.

findings.result_name: degen:prop-nolin (the count "24 acyclic unique sink completions of its partial orientation, 17 of them Holt-Klee")
findings.defect: The counts are correct only under an unstated extra condition -- that the completion's bottom-antipodal walk from sigma_0 = 7 is exactly the run 7,11,13. As literally stated ("completions of its partial orientation") the counts are wrong.
findings.evidence: My enumeration of all 2^7 orientations of the seven flat edges, with S fixed on the non-flat edges: 96 are acyclic unique sink orientations, 74 of them Holt-Klee (and all 32 corner resolutions are AUSO, 28 of them HK). Imposing cube.walk(o,7)==[7,11,13] gives exactly 24 and 17, matching the route; their own t_infeas.py does impose it (`w=ba_walk(s,s0,m); if w!=seq: continue`), the LaTeX does not say so. Non-load-bearing: the sentence only supports "L <= h*_HK(4) still holds here", which is trivial since L=2.

findings.result_name: degen:cor-gate (closing sentence "In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1)")
findings.defect: The sentence over-reads the corollary's own hypotheses. Hypothesis (ii) ("a block's vertices never switch while they are dead") is automatic given the chain structure -- a wholly dead block has both options valued 0 at every vertex, hence tied -- but hypothesis (iii) ("no vertex of B_1,...,B_{r-1} switches after the round at which B_r wakes") is NOT automatic, and it excludes precisely the constructions in which earlier blocks keep moving after the last block wakes. What is proved is conditional on (iii); "no amount of chaining" reads as unconditional.
findings.evidence: The proof uses (iii) twice: to conclude T <= m - m_r (the T first-switch witnesses must lie outside B_r) and to conclude that after round T the run is an all-switches run of the frozen subgame. Nothing in the proof bounds a chain in which B_1 and B_r interleave. The route's own next_steps item 4 concedes the point ("the nondegenerate threshold sequencer ... NOT the zero-tie gate, which degen:cor-gate caps").

findings.result_name: degen:lem-gperturb (last sentence, "Condition (*) is the case pi = 0 of (**)")
findings.defect: Not an equivalence. (**) requires (pi,rho) ADMISSIBLE, so its pi=0 case requires rho_{v,a} >= 0 wherever q^{v,a} = 0, whereas (*) allows an arbitrary linear functional d on R^{2m}. Hence (**)|_{pi=0} implies (*) but not conversely, and the two conditions are incomparable rather than nested -- so rem-star's "the stronger condition (**)" is also imprecise. No downstream damage: each condition separately yields L <= h*_HK(m), and cor-onetie's d = y_{x,a} happens to be admissible.
findings.evidence: Admissibility as defined in the lemma constrains rho on exactly the (v,a) with q^{v,a}=0, of which G_lin has six of eight. The proof's identification only shows <rho,y^{sigma}> - <rho,y^{sigma[v]}> has the sign of -Delta(sigma,v), which is a one-way translation of the *values*, not of the *feasible sets*.

findings.defect: The proof asserts that "for a generic admissible (pi',rho')" the first-order term Delta_{(pi',rho')}(sigma,v) is nonzero at every flat incidence, without checking that Delta(sigma,v) is a nonzero functional on the admissible cone. It is -- but the step is asserted, not proved.
findings.evidence: The coefficient of rho_{v,abar} in Delta(sigma,v) is exactly 1 (abar != sigma(v), so rho_{v,abar} does not enter u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma)), and the direction rho_{v,abar} = +1 is admissible whatever q^{v,abar} is; the admissible cone has nonempty interior, so a generic point avoids the finitely many hyperplanes Delta(sigma,v) = 0. One sentence supplies the missing justification.

findings.defect: "the flat classes are exactly the faces of X(G) on which obj is constant" is false as an equality of sets: every sub-face of a flat class is a face on which obj is constant. The correct statement is "the MAXIMAL faces on which obj is constant", which is what the proof's converse actually gives ("the face lies inside one flat class").
findings.evidence: Immediate; the integrated frontier.tex text already reads "the flat classes are exactly the maximal faces of X(G) on which obj is constant".

findings.result_name: degen:cor-hstar-one, as restated in the route's JSON report ("the height-7 class of prop:auso-census is the only class of the 4-cube that one player cannot reach")
findings.defect: Read as a statement about realising ORIENTATIONS this is false: prop:oneplayer-lp forbids every non-Holt-Klee class for nondegenerate one-player games, and the 4-cube has 143-56 = 87 non-HK classes of height 6 alone (the solo round measured 33 of them all failing). The sentence is true only for run LENGTHS. It does not appear in degen.tex, so it is a summary-only over-statement.
findings.evidence: My census: of the 384 height-6-plus outmaps... precisely, my enumeration gives 54912 acyclic height-6 outmaps of which 21504 are Holt-Klee, so most height-6 orientations are non-HK and hence unrealisable by any nondegenerate one-player game (prop:oneplayer-lp). grep of degen.tex for 'only class'/'cannot reach' returns nothing.

findings.result_name: degen:prop-family (the N and a rows of the table) and degen:prop-nolin ("34 vertices, 28 of them average")
findings.defect: These vertex counts are properties of the route's particular Knuth-Yao DDG realisation of the average part, not of the family or of the normal form; the statement presents them as data of the instance. Not an error, but the reader cannot check them from the statement.
findings.evidence: My own depth-k binary-tree realisation of the same block AP_m4_k0_den1024_s1 gives a = 167 average vertices (N = 2m+165) against their a = m+113 (N = 2m+115); for G_lin I get 32 average vertices (N=38) against their 28 (N=34). The load-bearing rows reproduce exactly: L = s+6 and ties = 4s+C(s,2) at s = 0,4,8 (L = 6,10,14; ties = 0,22,60), stopping by the trap test, from the explicit fair-coin game.

findings.defect: "an all-switches run whose resolution lies in the orbit of s_12" should say "whose resolution WITH CORNERS ON THE RUN": a corner resolution depends on the corner choices off the run, so "the" resolution is not well defined, and the proof only handles the run-corner one. (Also worth recording that the proof's contradiction needs s_eps = s', not merely h*_HK(5) < 12; the route gets this right, and the argument is sound, but the statement does not say which fact is doing the work.)
findings.evidence: I verified s_eps = s' does hold in both the m=4 and m=5 arguments: the single flat edge is oriented by d = y_{x,a} towards sigma_0, which is the corner, and S is constant on the class, so the perturbed orientation agrees with the corner resolution everywhere. frontier.tex's integrated text already reads "whose resolution with corners on the run lies in the orbit of s_12".

audits.verdict:
SOUND. Nothing fatal or major survived; the route's two headline theorems are correct and their computational ingredients reproduce exactly under independent reimplementation.

WHAT I REBUILT AND CONFIRMED (all exact rational arithmetic, code in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-degenerate-correctness/, written from the STATEMENTS):
(1) The census inputs, from scratch in C (enum4.c, 11 s): 5541744 USOs of the 4-cube, 4792176 acyclic; h*(4)=7 attained by exactly 384 outmaps, which I checked form a single free orbit under the 384 cube automorphisms and contain the route's representative (0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2); NONE of the 384 is Holt-Klee by my own unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test on all 33 faces of dimension >= 2; 21504 acyclic height-6 orientations are Holt-Klee. So h*_HK(4)=6 < 7 = h*(4), independently.
(2) degen:lem-seven-flat, by my own partition enumerator that does NOT assume the "exactly four disjoint (F1)-edges" shortcut: 768 pairs (s, sigma_0) of walk length 7; exactly 384 admit an (F1)-(F4) partition with a block of dimension >= 1; in every one the partition is unique and is the single edge containing the start. The representative's (F1)-edges are exactly {0,1},{6,14},{7,15},{8,9} and its length-7 starts are 8 and 9, as stated.
(3) degen:prop-five: s_12 is a bijective USO, acyclic, of bottom-antipodal height 12, NOT Holt-Klee; its length-12 starts are 0 and 16; its (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1 are exactly the seven listed edges; the unique nontrivial (F1)-(F4) partition is {0,16} at start 0, and start 16 admits none.
(4) degen:thm-no-seven: I reconstructed the proof step by step. (F1)-(F4) are genuinely NECESSARY for a real game's flat partition w.r.t. the run-corner resolution -- (F1) because s'(sigma)=S_A | (sigma xor c_A) with S_A disjoint from D_A, (F2) because c_A=sigma_t, (F3) by lem:flat-class(c), (F4) by lem:face-sink -- and I confirmed this empirically on 768 runs of 48 random degenerate m=4 games built as explicit fair-coin SSGs: 0 violations, and the corner resolution is always an AUSO whose BA walk is the run. The dichotomy (nondegenerate, or the unique single-edge partition) is exhaustive, cor-onetie's d = y_{x,a} does satisfy (*) because the two occupancy vertices have disjoint support on (x,a), and the resulting s_eps equals s', which is non-HK. No asserted-not-proved step of consequence.
(5) degen:prop-nolin, twice over: from the normal form AND from an explicit fair-coin SSG I constructed myself (N=38, 32 average, stopping by mycore's trap test). S=(9,10,9,8,9,12,9,12,5,4,7,6,1,0,1,0), D=(6,0,6,0,6,2,6,2,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2), run 7->11->13, two flat incidences both at x_2 with opposite actions, and y^15-y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7-y^5) exactly, so (*) is infeasible by Gordan. I also verified the objective identity obj(y^sigma) = sum_v val_sigma(v) on all 16 strategies.
(6) (**) feasibility on that instance, by an explicit admissible certificate of my own: pi^{x2,0}_{x2} + (1/4) pi^{x2,1}_{x1} gives Delta(7,x_2) = -1/40 and Delta(13,x_2) = -2621/18152, both negative; the first direction is free (p=5/16>0), the second sign-constrained and used with the + sign. I also re-derived Delta as the exact epsilon-derivative of the gap, and confirmed u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma).
(7) degen:thm-timer: the proof is correct as written (the three steps -- v is Max and in S_{s-1}; the switch is its first, since an earlier switch would give val_{sigma_{t+1}}(v) > 0 and val is nondecreasing; w' dead at sigma_{s-2}, else v is already switchable there -- all check out, and lem:trap gives "dead = t1 unreachable in G_sigma" for Vmin empty). Empirically: 0 violations of T <= m or of the distinct-first-switch structure over ~18000 wake-up events in 160 tie-rich games at m=4,5, computed from the game; maxT = m exactly at m=4.
(8) degen:prop-staircase, from the game at k = 1,2,4,8,16,24 in both variants: N=k+2, a=0 (resp. a=k), run length exactly k switching {x_1},...,{x_k} in order, T(x_k)=k, val_end = 1 (resp. 2^{-k}), ties on the run = C(k,2).
(9) degen:prop-family rebuilt independently at three sizes s = 0,4,8 from the explicit fair-coin game: L = 6,10,14 = s+6 and ties = 0,22,60 = 4s+C(s,2), stopping, one-player. The switched sets show the staircase running singleton switches for s rounds and then the block reproducing B's own run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4.
(10) degen:prop-partial-lp: the three-case sign law and "flat classes = level sets of sigma -> val_sigma = subcubes" hold with 0 violations over all 2^m strategies of 120 tie-rich m=4 games and 40 m=5 games, all computed from the explicit game. degen:prop-res-nonhk reproduces qualitatively: 800 of 3150 corner resolutions in my sample fail Holt-Klee, at heights 2 and 3.

STANDING-ERROR SWEEP: no greedy policy iteration anywhere (val_sigma is a linear solve restricted to the t1-reaching set, or brute force); rows accumulated rather than dict-literal; sinks carried as sentinels and mapped last; stopping tested by the trap characterisation; run length counts switches, with the non-productive terminal round excluded; the family varies its parameter s; no class-separation via unreachable vertices; no pair test / own-successor issue and no Z_0/Z_1 seed needed, since the route makes no stall claim. The route claims no decision rule, no barrier and no polynomial algorithm, and no step assumes a target-equivalent oracle; the only imported input is Holt-Klee (Holt-Klee, Gaertner-Morris-Ruest), which the route flags as from memory, as rem:oneplayer-lp already does.

CITATIONS CHECKED AGAINST THE TEXT: lem:switch, lem:trichotomy(b),(c), lem:flat-class(a),(b),(c), lem:face-sink, thm:flat-resolution, cor:ceiling-general, lem:trap, lem:trapchar, def:subcube, lem:subgame(b), thm:impedance, prop:oneplayer-lp, prop:auso-census, prop:hstar-five -- all say what the route uses them for. In particular prop:oneplayer-lp's proof does use nondegeneracy only in its final paragraph, so degen:prop-partial-lp(a) is legitimate.

RESIDUAL: the route's declared GAP (whether every one-player run obeys L <= h*_HK(m)) is honestly stated and I found no reason to doubt it is still open. Note that frontier.tex has moved on since this route was written: sec:ties is already integrated (commit 9fafa72) with several of the findings above independently repaired by the integrator -- "maximal faces", the run-corner qualifier in the m=5 statement, the explicit hedge about resolutions in thm:no-seven, and cor:hstar-one's lower bounds now cited from nondegenerate games only -- and h*_HK(5)=11 is now proved (prop:hkfive) rather than measured, which supersedes part of degen:rem-five.

audits.target: route "degenerate" — Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player

findings.defect: A barrier that covers nothing, presented as a general negative result. Its hypotheses -- (ii) 'a block's vertices never switch while dead' and (iii) 'no vertex of B_1..B_{r-1} switches after B_r wakes' -- forbid exactly the offer-and-withdraw / re-entry behaviour that every published exponential policy-iteration lower bound uses (Friedmann, Fearnley) and that rem:closed-now-or-never already identifies as the mechanism. It covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and the audit brief's own rule says such a barrier 'must be labelled as such'. The route labels it nowhere. Worse, the corollary is TITLED 'Gating cannot be superlinear' and its statement ends 'In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1)', which is not what the proof gives -- it is an unproved assertion once hypotheses (ii)/(iii) are dropped, and whether an interleaving chain can exceed m+O(1) is precisely the open question the route was hired to attack.
findings.evidence: degen.tex lines at label degen:cor-gate: hypotheses stated, then 'In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1).' The proof uses (ii) at 'none of them lies in B_r, whose vertices are dead and, by hypothesis, do not switch before round T' and (iii) at 'After round T the blocks B_1..B_{r-1} are at their optima'. findings.defect: The route's stated gap is half the truth, and stating only half makes the route look closer to the pivot than it is. Closing 'L <= h*_HK(m) for every one-player stopping SSG' would settle NOTHING about the pivot, because the asymptotics of h*_HK are entirely unknown -- the bound could be exponential, in which case the ceiling is vacuous. The one-player half of the pivot needs BOTH (a) L <= h*_HK(m) in general and (b) h*_HK(m) = m^{O(1)}; or, in the other direction, a superpolynomial-BA-height Holt-Klee AUSO family together with its one-player realisation at polynomial size. The route names only (a). Its own next_steps item 3 asks whether h*_HK is superlinear and then does not spend ten minutes on the cheapest available probe.
findings.evidence: I fed lem:hstar-super's own product construction with prop:hkfive's height-11 5-cube witness (my code /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-sig/super.py, mycube.py, own USO/acyclicity/unit-vertex-capacity-max-flow Holt-Klee tests): (5,1) with x*=1 gives an acyclic USO of the 6-cube, Holt-Klee on every face, BA height 12; (5,2) gives the 7-cube, Holt-Klee, BA height 13. So h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13, i.e. h*_HK >= 1,2,4,6,11,12,13, extending the paper's 1,2,4,6,11 for free. The product is NOT HK-preserving in general: (4,4) -> height 12 non-HK, (5,4) -> 17 non-HK, (5,5) -> 22 non-HK, and (2,4) is non-HK where (4,2) is HK. So superadditivity gives only a LINEAR lower bound on h*_HK and no doubling is known (consistent with solo blowhk.py's 4,9,12).

audits.verdict:
FIRST, A PROCESS FACT THE AUDIT PROMPT DOES NOT KNOW: this work is already integrated. Commit 9fafa72 ("... sec:ties (the degenerate route) and h*_HK(5)=11 integrated") added frontier.tex lines 4926-5273 as \subsection{Ties in one-player games}. So question 5 is retrospective, and the integrator already applied most of the repairs an audit would demand: he added the Charnes/Dantzig-Orden-Wolfe attribution, added the folklore note on the timer, added the rem:ladder qualification on the staircase, corrected prop:no-linear-tiebreak's completion counts (route said "24 AUSO completions, 17 HK"; the paper says 96 completions of (S,D), 74 HK, of which 24 agree with the run and 17 of those are HK), silently dropped the unverifiable degenerate-attainment clause, flagged the (**) sampling as "a report and not evidence", and caveated thm:no-seven. Of the route's 19 labels he kept 8 numbered. That is good editorial judgement, and my findings below are against the route AS SUBMITTED plus one residual defect in the paper.

IS IT NEW? Three things are, and I re-derived all three from scratch with my own code (/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/audit-sig/mycube.py, myflat.py -- independent USO, acyclicity, BA-walk, face and unit-vertex-capacity max-flow Holt-Klee implementations, plus my own (F1)-(F4) enumerator):
 (1) lem:seven-flat. Over the free orbit of 384 height-7 outmaps of the 4-cube I get 768 (outmap,start) pairs with a length-7 walk, exactly 4 (F1)-subcubes of dimension >=1 per outmap, and exactly 384 surviving flat structures with a nontrivial block -- one per outmap, a single block, of dimension 1, always containing the start. Exact agreement with the route.
 (2) thm:no-seven / cor:hstar-one. h*_1(4) = 6 < h*(4) = 7. New, correct, and the argument has no shortcut: I checked that in the surviving case s_eps really does equal s' (the unique nontrivial class is the start edge, whose corner is sigma_0, so all other classes are singletons), so the "s' is an LP orientation" step is airtight rather than the slip it first looks like.
 (3) prop:no-linear-tiebreak. Rebuilt from the printed normal form in exact rationals: every row leaks to t0, run 7 -> 11 -> 13, exactly two flat incidences both at x_2 with OPPOSITE actions (sigma=7 action 1, sigma=13 action 0), and y^15 - y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7 - y^5) componentwise with matching zero pattern. The Gordan obstruction is real.
 The 5-cube analogue also reproduces exactly (starts {0,16}; seven (F1)-edges {1,3},{12,14},{13,15},{29,31},{18,22},{0,16},{14,30}; 96 candidate partitions; unique survivor {0,16} at start 0).
Everything else is not new or not a result: lem:perturb is textbook lexicographic perturbation (unattributed by the route), thm:zero-timer is folklore attractor-layer counting, prop:staircase's length is thm:ladder's, prop:partial-lp is a reading of prop:oneplayer-lp's own proof, prop:family is linear.

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No oracle, no polynomial-class claim. But cor:gate is a barrier covering NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and its hypotheses forbid the one mechanism every published exponential lower bound uses. Under the brief's own rule it is "nearly worthless and must be labelled as such". The route did not label it; the integrator did. prop:family is a genuine family per def:ssg (fair coins, out-degree two, stopping, verified from the game at five sizes -- I re-ran t_all.py) but with a LINEAR growth law that beats the existing ladder by +2.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes -- the exhaustive computations are exhaustive and reproduce independently, and prop:res-nonhk is an existence claim for which sampling is legitimate. Two places are not: the (**) sampling (longest run 3 and 4 against ceilings 6 and 11 -- the parameter never varies into the regime where the question bites), and the "degenerate game" witnesses, which are non-dyadic normal forms that the route's own builder cannot turn into fair-coin SSGs and which were reported as "games ... stopping, exact rationals".

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it: closing the route's gap ("L <= h*_HK(m) for every one-player stopping SSG") would settle nothing, because the asymptotics of h*_HK are unknown and could be exponential; the one-player half of the pivot needs BOTH that ceiling AND h*_HK(m) = m^{O(1)}, or else a Holt-Klee AUSO family of superpolynomial bottom-antipodal height together with its one-player realisation at polynomial size -- and on the evidence h*_HK is only known to be superadditive-ish and linear-ish (I measured h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13 by feeding lem:hstar-super's own product with prop:hkfive's height-11 witness; the product is not HK-preserving in general, failing at (4,4), (5,4), (5,5), so no doubling follows).

BETTER OR WORSE? BETTER, marginally, and the integration as made is close to right. Worth their numbered slots, keep: lem:tie-perturb, cor:one-tie, lem:seven-flat, thm:no-seven, cor:hstar-one, prop:no-linear-tiebreak. Not worth numbered slots, demote to prose keeping the folklore note and the "covers nothing" paragraph: thm:zero-timer and cor:gate -- a numbered Theorem whose content is one attractor layer per round, and a numbered Corollary whose hypotheses exclude every known hard mechanism, sit badly beside thm:blowup and thm:gap-equivalence and invite exactly the misreading the paper works to prevent. Correctly already prose: partial-lp, gperturb, staircase, family, res-nonhk, the 5-cube remark. THREE CONCRETE REPAIRS FOR THE INTEGRATOR: (i) frontier.tex lines 11702-11706, "The height-seven orbit is realised ... by no one-player game, nondegenerate ... or not (thm:no-seven)" reinstates the run/orientation conflation that thm:no-seven's own parenthetical disowns -- rewrite as "and no one-player game has a run realising it, with or without ties"; (ii) record h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13 beside prop:hkfive, with the observation that lem:hstar-super's product preserves Holt-Klee for some factor orders and not others, since the growth of h*_HK is now the operative unknown and the paper currently stops the sequence at m=5; (iii) if the degenerate-attainment claim is ever wanted, it needs a dyadic witness, not a non-dyadic normal form.

result.route: lane-reuse: lane re-use with the correct rise accounting, aiming at a superlinear one-player all-switches family
result.headline: The reopening premise is FALSE and now provably so: the impedance denominator amplifies the GAP, not the RISE. New law lane:rise-bound (a resting Max vertex's rise is at most the largest rise among the vertices its later action reads) proves it, and yields lane:peak-source (the peak of val_{t'}-val_t over ANY interval sits on S_t, sharper than thm:peak-law) and lane:autonomy (an autonomous module's own switched sets are pairwise distinct, so a self-contained lane can never oscillate). lane:exit-chain closes the single-driver two-phase lane by a delay+reach<=k+1 budget. No superlinear family; instead the linear state of the art is improved from fs14:lane-def's N=Theta(k log k) to RC(k): N=k+2, a=0, L=N-2, which is optimal at a=0.

results.name: lane:rise-bound
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG, C = Vmax u Vmin, and for u in C, a in {0,1} let (p^{u,a}, q^{u,a}) be the first-passage law of that action onto C u {t1} (a datum of the GRAPH, strategy-independent, since only average vertices lie strictly between controlled vertices). Let sigma, sigma' be Max strategies with val_{sigma'} >= val_sigma pointwise and let u in Vmax be NOT strictly switchable at sigma. Put b := sigma'(u) and W(u,b) := {w in C\{u} : p^{u,b}_w > 0}. Then val_{sigma'}(u) - val_sigma(u) <= max_{w in W(u,b)} ( val_{sigma'}(w) - val_sigma(w) ), the max over the empty set being 0.
results.argument: val_sigma is a fixed point of T_sigma, hence the mean of its successors at every average vertex, so val_tau(u) = sum_w p^{u,tau(u)}_w val_tau(w) + q^{u,tau(u)}. 'At rest' gives, for BOTH actions and in particular for b, p_u x(u) + sum_{w!=u} p_w x(w) + q <= x(u) where x = val_sigma. Since sigma'(u) = b, y(u) = p_u y(u) + sum_{w!=u} p_w y(w) + q with y = val_{sigma'}. Subtracting and using sum_{w!=u} p_w <= 1 - p_u - q <= 1 - p_u gives (1-p_u)(y(u)-x(u)) <= sum_{w!=u} p_w Delta_w <= (1-p_u) M. Finally p_u < 1, since p_u = 1 would make {u} plus the average vertices on those paths a trap, contradicting stopping (lem:trapchar).
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic. 74232 instances (game, sigma, sigma', u) over random one-player harmonic normal forms with m <= 6 (t_rise.py); a further 10933 at the SSG level over random stopping games with 3-8 non-sinks, BOTH players present, with the first-passage laws recomputed from the graph (t_laws.py). No violation. Transcript VERIFY.log.

results.name: lane:impedance-cancels
results.statement: Let G be stopping, sigma_0..sigma_L an all-switches run, u in Vmax at rest at sigma_t, and suppose u in S_{t'} for some t' >= t, switching to action b with return mass h = p^{u,b}_u = h(b -> u) (so thm:impedance writes the rise in that round as (val_{sigma_{t'}}(b) - val_{sigma_{t'}}(a))/(1-h)). Then val_{sigma_{t'+1}}(u) - val_{sigma_t}(u) <= max_{w in W(u,b)} ( val_{sigma_{t'+1}}(w) - val_{sigma_t}(w) ). So a delayed switch can gain far more than the GAP that triggered it, and never more than the RISE of its trigger.
results.argument: lane:rise-bound with sigma = sigma_t, sigma' = sigma_{t'+1}; sigma_{t'+1}(u) = b and val_{sigma_{t'+1}} >= val_{sigma_t} by lem:switch. The route was opened on the premise that 'the escape denominator 1-h can be 2^{-Theta(N)}, so a delayed switch CAN gain far more than its trigger did'. Written out: before the switch val(b) = h val(u) + (1-h) l, so the gap is (1-h)(l - val(u)) while the rise is l - val(u) (allswlower:cor-selfread) -- the ratio 1/(1-h) is indeed unbounded; but l - val(u) is itself bounded by the largest rise among the vertices b reads, over the whole waiting period. The premise is therefore false as stated and true only in the weaker form 'more than the gap'.
results.verification: Implied by lane:rise-bound (verified as above); additionally exercised by every all-switches run in t_rise.py / t_laws.py.

results.name: lane:peak-source
results.statement: Let G be stopping and sigma_0..sigma_L an all-switches run. For all 0 <= t < t' <= L, max_{v in V} (val_{sigma_{t'}}(v) - val_{sigma_t}(v)) = max_{v in S_t} (val_{sigma_{t'}}(v) - val_{sigma_t}(v)). Taking t=0, t'=L: the whole improvement of the run is realised at a vertex strictly switchable at the very first round.
results.argument: Put Delta = val_{sigma_{t'}} - val_{sigma_t} >= 0 (lem:switch) and A = C \ S_t. The computation in lane:rise-bound gives, for u in A n Vmax with b = sigma_{t'}(u), Delta_u <= sum_{w != u} tilde-p_w Delta_w with tilde-p_w = p^{u,b}_w/(1-p^{u,b}_u), row sums <= 1; the SAME inequality holds at u in Vmin with b the action of a Min best response to sigma_t, since val_{sigma_{t'}}(u) is a minimum over actions hence at most the value of that one, while val_{sigma_t}(u) equals it. Collecting rows, Delta|_A <= Q Delta|_A + R Delta|_{S_t} with [Q R] substochastic; tilde-P is the jump chain of the transient P (I - tilde-P = (I-D)^{-1}(I-P)), hence transient, hence so is Q; so Delta|_A <= (I-Q)^{-1} R Delta|_{S_t} and (I-Q)^{-1} R 1 <= 1 (probabilities of ever leaving A into S_t). Averages and sinks add nothing.
results.verification: Exact. All pairs t < t' of all-switches runs from EVERY start: 5572 pairs on one-player normal forms (t_rise.py) and 283 on random two-player stopping games (t_laws.py). No violation. This is strictly sharper than thm:peak-law in the direction that matters: the peak of any interval is pinned to the set switched at the START of the interval, for all later t' at once.

results.name: lane:autonomy + lane:modules
results.statement: Call U subset of Vmax AUTONOMOUS in a one-player SSG if W(u,a) is contained in U for every u in U and both a. Then along any all-switches run, t -> S_t n U is exactly the all-switches switch sequence of the sub-SSG G|_U from sigma_0|_U, padded with the empty set. Hence (a) once S_t n U is empty it is empty for ever; (b) the nonempty sets among S_t n U are PAIRWISE DISTINCT; (c) #{t : S_t n U nonempty} <= h*(|U|), and <= h*_HK(|U|) if G|_U is nondegenerate. Corollary (lane:modules): if Vmax partitions into autonomous modules then L = max_i L_i, so placing gadgets side by side never lengthens a run; a gadget to be run twice must read a vertex outside itself.
results.argument: By the first-passage identity and autonomy, val_sigma|_U solves the linear system of G|_U determined by sigma|_U alone, so val_sigma|_U = val^{G|_U}_{sigma|_U}; hence S_sigma n U depends only on sigma|_U and equals S^{G|_U}_{sigma|_U}. The projection of the run is therefore the all-switches run of G|_U, which stops when its switch set empties and then stays put -- (a). (b) is cor:law-u applied to G|_U; (c) is cor:ceiling-general with prop:oneplayer-lp. G|_U is stopping because a trap of G|_U is a trap of G.
results.verification: Exact: 610 projected switch sequences over all autonomous U with |U| <= 4, on random stopping games with both players (t_laws.py). No violation. This is the MODULE form of allswlower:lem-isolated(ii): a self-contained lane cannot repeat ANY of its own switch patterns, so no external stimulation can make it oscillate, and cor:law-u bites inside the module even when the ambient switched sets are all distinct.

results.name: lane:exit-chain + lane:budget
results.statement: Let G be one-player stopping, l_1..l_n, d in Vmax distinct, with one action b_i of l_i having W(l_i,b_i) contained in {l_{i-1}} (l_0 := d) and BOTH actions of d having read set inside {l_1..l_j}. If at some round t of an improving run sigma_t(l_i) = b_i for all i <= j and d is not strictly switchable, then at every later round at which all l_i (i<=j) are again at b_i we have sigma_{t'}(d) = sigma_t(d) and val unchanged on {d, l_1..l_j}; so as soon as one of these has strictly raised its value, that configuration never occurs again. Consequently in the two-phase lane the driver cannot fire before round k-j+1 (val(l_j) has not moved before then) and the exit wave can never reach l_j, so delay + reach <= k+1 whatever j: the two-phase lane runs at most k+O(1) rounds.
results.argument: W := {d, l_1..l_j} with pi_a := (d -> a, l_i -> b_i) is a CLOSED CONFIGURATION in the sense of prop:closed-now-or-never for each of d's two actions a (everything reachable from pi_a(W) avoiding W is average or a sink). Take a = the action d does NOT take at sigma_t; then W_t = {d}, nonempty and disjoint from S_{sigma_t}, so prop:closed-now-or-never(b) forbids sigma_{t'}|_W = pi_a for ever. Hence the only way all l_i can be at b_i again is with d unchanged, i.e. sigma_{t'}|_W = sigma_t|_W, and W is closed for that too, so the values on W are the same lambda_W.
results.verification: Exact scan over the two-phase lane family (mass alpha, per-vertex rewards, both read points, all parameters dyadic with denominator 256, k=5, |Vmax|=7): longest run found 7 rounds = |Vmax| (t_lane2.py). Replacing the single driver by turnaround vertices reading MIXTURES of the whole lane removes the closed set and therefore this obstruction; an exact scan of that family (rl.py, k <= 5) also found nothing longer than |Vmax|.

results.name: lane:three + lane:linear (RC, ALH, CL)
results.statement: RC(k): Vmax = v_1..v_k, NO average vertex, v_i -> (v_{i+1}, t0) for i<k, v_k -> (t1, t0). ALH(k): Vmax = p_1..p_k, one average vertex h -> (t1,t0), p_i -> (p_{i+1}, h), p_{k+1} := t1. CL(k): Vmax = l_1..l_k, Vavg = g_1..g_k, l_i -> (l_{i+1}, g_i) with l_{k+1} := t1, g_i -> (l_{i-1}, t0), g_1 -> (t1, t0). All three are one-player and stopping and, from the start taking the second listed action everywhere, the all-switches run switches exactly ONE vertex per round in the order k, k-1, ..., 1, halting at w* = 1 on Vmax. Hence RC(k): N = k+2, a = 0, L = N-2; ALH(k): N = k+3, a = 1, L = N-3; CL(k): N = 2k+2, a = k, L = (N-2)/2. RC and ALH have C(k,2) tied incidences along the run, CL none; all three are degenerate as cube orientations (CL's cube ties are 0,2,12,46,144 for k=2..6), so thm:flat-resolution and not prop:allsw-auso applies, and the Holt-Klee ceiling does not bind them.
results.argument: RC: at the all-t0 strategy every val(v_i)=0; for i<k the other option is val(v_{i+1})=0, a TIE (all-switches keeps ties), while v_k sees 1>0. Inductively after r rounds v_{k-r+1}..v_k have value 1 and exactly v_{k-r} switches; a vertex's value is 1 after switching so it never switches again. ALH: identical with 0 replaced by 1/2 = val(h). CL: at the all-exit strategy val(g_1)=1/2 and val(g_i)=val(l_{i-1})/2, so val(l_i)=2^{-i}, strictly decreasing, so no premature switch; l_k sees 1>2^{-k}; l_i switching to continue only lowers val(g_{i+1}) to 1/2 < 1 so nothing switches back. Stopping by lem:trapchar (RC's Max subgraph is acyclic; in ALH and CL every average vertex has t0 as a successor).
results.verification: Exact, from the GRAPH, with the harness's independent all-switches loop (rc.py, alh.py, chainlane.py). RC verified for k = 2,3,4,5,8,12,20,50,100; ALH for k up to 80; CL for k up to 30; the optimum w* = 1 checked by brute force over all strategies for the small k. Degeneracy and Holt-Klee audit in t_hk.py. These improve fs14:lane-def, which needs N = Theta(k log k) for the same run length k (its N = 13,24,43,64,124 at k=3,5,8,12,20 reproduced here).

results.name: lane:grid + lane:rc-optimal
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG with m = |Vmax|, a = |Vavg|, and let D(a) = |{p/q in [0,1] : 1 <= q <= 2^a}| be the number of points of the grid of lem:denominator-sharp. Then every all-switches run satisfies L <= sum_{v in Vmax} n_v <= m (D(a) - 1), where n_v is the number of rounds at which v switches. In particular L <= m when a = 0 and L <= 2m when a = 1. Hence RC(k) is OPTIMAL among one-player stopping SSGs with no average vertex (L <= |Vmax| = N-2, attained), and any one-player family with L > N-2 must have a >= 1 and must switch some vertex more than once.
results.argument: Each round switches a nonempty set, so L <= sum_v n_v. If v switches at rounds t_1 < ... < t_{n_v}, lem:switch makes val(v) strictly larger after each of them and non-decreasing in between, so v takes at least n_v + 1 distinct values along the run, all on the grid of lem:denominator-sharp.
results.verification: Exact search with a and m held fixed (fixeda.py): at a=0 the bound L = m is attained for m = 3,4,5,6 (and the search found 6 at m=7,8, below the bound but RC attains it); at a=1 the search returned L = m exactly for m = 3..7 and at a=2 L = m for m = 3..6 -- always far below the grid bound m 2^a, so the extra randomness bought nothing at these sizes.

results.name: lane:tree + lane:tree-lag (binarisation)
results.statement: A state with r >= 2 actions is replaced by a rooted binary tree of r-1 fresh Max vertices whose r leaf edges carry the actions' first-passage laws; if the r action values do not change during d = ceil(log2 r) consecutive rounds of an all-switches run, the root then selects a leaf of maximal value and has value max_i val(A_i). Cost: r-1 Max vertices, no average vertices. The lag is real: an explicit 15-vertex one-player stopping SSG (Lane(3) with exits 7/8, 3/4, 5/8, plus u = max(l_1,l_2), p = max(u,l_3)) has an all-switches run of 3 rounds in which, at round 1, the best leaf is worth 1 while the root p is worth 7/8.
results.argument: Induction on height: a height-1 vertex compares its two leaves and after one round selects the larger; if every vertex of height <= j selects its subtree maximum after j rounds, a height-(j+1) vertex sees the two subtree maxima from round j and after one more round selects the larger. Ties are kept, harmlessly. The instance is computed exactly and its normal form is re-derived from the realised graph.
results.verification: tree.py, exact: normal form realised as an honest SSG (N=15, 5 Max, 8 average, stopping), first-passage laws re-verified from the graph, and the SSG-level all-switches loop reproduces the run (3 rounds, trace [(2,), (1,4), (0,3)], 2 ties).

results.name: lane:measured / lane:nminus2
results.statement: Longest all-switches runs found for ONE-PLAYER stopping games. (i) Local search over harmonic normal forms (each action reading at most 3 Max vertices, dyadic denominator 32 or 64, objective the bottom-antipodal height over all 2^m starts): m=4 -> 6, m=5 -> 8, m=6 -> 8, m=7 -> 8. The 6 at m=4 is exactly h*_HK(4), the ceiling of prop:oneplayer-lp; the height-8 instance at m=5 is DEGENERATE (2 tied incidences over the cube, none along the run) so not bound by that ceiling, and in its run one Max vertex switches four times and a second switches four times. (ii) Local search at the level of the graph over one-player stopping SSGs with n = N-2 non-sinks and every (|Vmax|,|Vavg|) split: L = 5,6,7,8,8,9 at n = 5..10 -- never more than n = N-2, which RC(n) attains. QUESTION: is L <= N-2 for every one-player stopping SSG?
results.argument: Simulated annealing with exact rational evaluation; the fast evaluator (all 2^m value vectors -> outmap -> bottom-antipodal height) was validated against the direct all-switches loop on 1696 (game, start) pairs. This is a measurement over an engineered search space and proves nothing -- no search in this project has ever found a hard instance that was not first engineered.
results.verification: search1/2/3.py, ssgsearch.py, seeded.py, fixeda.py; inspect.py replays any logged instance, realises it as an honest SSG and re-checks the run with the independent SSG-level loop (done for the m=4 height-6 and m=5 height-8 instances: N = 54 and 55, normal form verified from the graph, SSG run identical).

result.gap: A one-player stopping SSG family on N = k^{O(1)} vertices whose all-switches run has length omega(N) is not constructed, and the single architecture the route's own theorems leave open is this: a lane l_1,...,l_k whose two turnaround vertices B (at the foot of the exit chain) and T (at the head of the continue chain) each read a MIXTURE of ALL of l_1,...,l_k, so that no proper subset of Vmax is a closed configuration and prop:closed-now-or-never/lane:exit-chain are vacuous, while lane:autonomy forces the lane's own switch pattern to vary from epoch to epoch, which it can do only if the ambient (B,T) state differs -- exact scans of this family were run only for k <= 5 and found nothing longer than |Vmax|. Second, separate gap (task 4): is there a choice of binary selection trees and delay chains for Fearnley's MDP, of total size n^{O(1)}, such that the all-switches run of the resulting two-action instance reproduces the appeal ordering at every bit state in every round -- equivalently, such that for every i and every round the root of b_i's tree selects the same action that b_i selects in the source instance, up to a fixed per-state lag?
result.next_steps:
1. The one architecture left open (mixture-driven turnarounds) needs a k >= 6 scan, which needs a better evaluator than annealing over 2^m starts: evaluate only from the designed all-D start and search the (mass, reward) parameters by exact bisection on the crossing conditions rather than by random moves. Two lanes of COPRIME lengths, weakly cross-coupled, are the natural candidate: lane:autonomy forbids either lane to repeat a switch pattern on its own, but the union's sets stay distinct if the two waves are out of phase, and the arithmetic (the loop gain is < 1, so the per-epoch rises shrink geometrically and j epochs need only Theta(j) bits, i.e. a = Theta(j) average vertices) does NOT forbid j = Theta(k) epochs and hence L = Theta(k^2). Nothing in this round refutes that; nothing in this round realises it either.
2. Settle lane:nminus2 (is L <= N-2 for every one-player stopping SSG?). At a = 0 it is a theorem (lane:grid); at a = 1 the grid bound is 2m and the measured maximum is m, so the first thing to decide is whether L = 2m is realisable at a = 1 -- a small, self-contained question that would already give L = 2N - 6, twice RC.
3. The ceiling question the measurements point at: how fast does h*_HK(m) grow? h*_HK = 1,2,4,6,11 for m <= 5 (the value 11 is measured and unverified), against the search's realisable 6,8,8,8 at m = 4,5,6,7. If h*_HK is superpolynomial the one-player half of the pivot is a pure realisability question; if it is linear, prop:oneplayer-lp settles the nondegenerate one-player half negatively and every superlinear one-player family must be degenerate (as RC, ALH and CL already are). Verifying h*_HK(5) = 11 and then attempting a one-player realisation of a height-11 Holt-Klee AUSO of the 5-cube is the decisive small computation.
4. lane:peak-source should be checked against the wedge and CC families: it pins the peak of every interval to S_t, so it may give an unconditional lower bound on how early a value-distinguishing pair must separate.
