Sinks were carried as sentinels and mapped only at the end; every average row was accumulated, never a dict literal; stopping was decided by lem:trapchar; val_sigma / val^tau were computed by acyclic backward induction and cross-checked against the componentwise extremum over ALL positional counter-strategies at small parameters and against root16/mycore.wstar, and on Q_16 (where brute force is 256 solves per state) by policy iteration CERTIFIED as an exact fixed point of T_sigma and cross-checked against the full 256-strategy minimum.

WHAT REPRODUCES EXACTLY. rbr:thm-readout: RD(n) built from def:rbr-rd has N = 9n exactly, |Vmax| = |Vmin| = n, is acyclic and stopping, its gadgets have the stated values, all-switches takes 1 round from sigma_0 and worst case 1 over ALL 2^n Max starts (n = 2..8), R_BR takes exactly n in both variants and worst case n over all starts x 4 best-response picks x 2 variants (n <= 4), BSI takes exactly 2n in both variants with the stated alternating pattern (n = 2..8) and worst case 2n over all 4^n pair starts (n <= 3), and every run halts at val_sigma = val^tau = w*. rbr:prop-sd: SD(K) for K = 2..14 is acyclic and stopping, a_p and a_q are nonnegative, the mixtures have the intended distributions, BSI = strict BSI = MR = R_BR = all-switches = K rounds, C_max = {x_{t+1}, v} and C_min = {u_{t+1}, v'} at every round, v and v' are each switched K times, and the levels are exactly 2^-1,...,2^-K; with the mixture trees repaired as phi-images (see the minor finding) phi satisfies bsr:prop-selfdual's hypotheses and U = 1 - L o phi with C_min = phi(C_max) at every round, K = 2..12. rbr:prop-gain and rbr:prop-slowlevel reproduce at every parameter listed, including gain/M = 2^-s for s up to 40 and M_t = 1/2 + 2^{-t-2}. rbr:prop-q16 reproduces to the digit: four switches of c_10, L-ties (both actions worth exactly 0) at t = 0,1,2 with the strict rule refusing, and at t = 3 exactly the two printed fractions 6307113667906557856/40916452043962854245417 < 397981020654592949762017/1340750300576574807913824256, the stated driver sets {c_9,c_11,c_16}/{c_12,c_13}/{c_11}, and over all 256 Max starts all-switches and R_BR both worst case 4 with no vertex switched twice. rbr:lem-constant's proof is correct and its hypothesis held on 193674 occurrences with 0 failures. rbr:rem-psd's printed (A,B,c) witness satisfies the normal-form constraints, is nondegenerate, its outmap is an acyclic USO, its longest all-switches run is 4, and rbr:lem-vacuous holds on it at every round from every mirrored start in both variants. Every row of rbr:prop-measure that I recomputed (SD 6/10/14/16, RD 6/10/16/20, SL 8/16) agrees in every round-count column; only N and a differ, because my gadget builds are more economical than the route's (SD in particular needs only O(K) average vertices, not the stated K^2+5K+10 total).

WHAT DOES NOT. Two claims fail. (1) rbr:prop-small's first instance asserts that Min's best response is unique at each round; it is not -- at sigma_0 the Min vertex has both options worth 0 under val_sigma, both choices are genuine best responses in prop:bsi-br's sense (val_{sigma,tau} = val_sigma verified for both), and under one of them R_BR halts in one round and ties all-switches. So that instance separates R_BR from all-switches only for a particular tie-break, and the claim marked "proved" is false as written. (2) The route reports having reproduced frontier.tex's numbers on G#, quoting "R_BR 4 with c_1 switched twice"; frontier.tex's rem:bsi-br says 5, exhaustively, with c_3 switched three times, and explicitly flags the four-round figure as a superseded earlier version. My independent rebuild of G# from prop:auso-seven's normal form agrees with frontier.tex exactly (outmap, all-switches 7, BSI 5, R_BR worst 5 from (0,1,1,1) with the identical switch sets), so the route's reproduction claim is wrong. Neither defect touches RD(n), SD(K), GAIN(s), SL(K), rbr:lem-constant, rbr:lem-vacuous or rbr:thm-track, whose mathematics I could not break.

ON rbr:thm-track. I reconstructed the proof step by step and found no gap for the STRICT variant: the telescoping of Phi with 0 <= Phi <= m, D_t <= m, D_t = 0 when C_min is empty, A <= sum|C_max,t|, R <= A + B and B <= 2^k - 1 are all correct, and the five displays were never violated in ~1600 random and tie-rich stopping games checked exhaustively over all pair starts. The restriction matters, though: def:bsi as printed in frontier.tex is the VETO variant, which is the rule whose round count rem:bsi-gap declares open, and the remark's one-line extension to it contains a false clause. I record as a GAP the exact missing statement, and I contribute one partial extension of my own -- if B = 0 then U = val^tau is constant and equals w* at the halt, so U = w* throughout and lem:max-deficit forces R <= m for the veto variant as well.

No step of the route assumes a target-equivalent oracle, no decision rule or barrier is claimed, and the rem:own-successor discipline is not engaged (these are switching rules, not decision rules). I did not attempt to reproduce the route's search-only claims (the 19600-pair and 3000-run sweeps, the "hours of random restart" on the mirror-paired normal form beyond its printed witness, or t11_over.py); those are labelled "measured" and their conclusions are honestly hedged.

audits.target: rbr-rounds — "The round count of best-response restart and bidirectional improvement"

findings.defect: The paste-ready LaTeX asserts, of the 9-non-sink instance, that "the best response is unique at each round". This is FALSE at round 0, and with the other best response the instance does NOT separate R_BR from all-switches: R_BR takes 1 round, exactly as all-switches does. The instance is therefore an example of the SAME phenomenon the route attributes only to its second (10-non-sink) instance — that R_BR's count depends on which best response is chosen — and not of a stronger one.
findings.evidence: Independent exact recomputation (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_small2.py). At sigma_0 = {3->1,6->3,7->4}, val_sigma = (1/4,0,0,0,0,1/2,0,0,0) with val_sigma(3) = val_sigma(t_0) = 0, so BOTH tau(4)=3 and tau(4)=t_0 are Min best responses. With tau(4)=3: S_sigma={3,7}, C_max={3} (veto and strict alike), R_BR = 2 rounds. With tau(4)=t_0: C_max={3,7}=S_sigma, R_BR = 1 round. val_sigma cross-checked against the componentwise min over all positional tau.

findings.defect: The result is presented as a self-dual, two-player, BSI phenomenon. It is neither: it is a ONE-PLAYER ALL-SWITCHES phenomenon. In SD(K) the observer v (and v') has IN-DEGREE ZERO — no vertex points at it, it is unreachable from everything — and L(u_j) = 0 for every sigma and tau, so the Min half and the self-duality contribute nothing to the K reversals. Deleting the Min player entirely (replace every u_j in the two mixtures by t_0) gives a ONE-PLAYER stopping SSG with Vmin = empty on which plain ALL-SWITCHES switches v exactly K times in K rounds. The self-duality apparatus (two K^2-vertex mixture trees, the Min cascade, the involution) serves only to make the BSI veto vacuous, i.e. it is rbr:lem-vacuous applied — so rbr:prop-sd = (a one-player all-switches construction) + (rbr:lem-vacuous), and should be stated that way. The correct headline is the stronger and simpler one the route does not make: prop:allswitch-overshoot's record of three switches at one vertex under all-switches extends to Theta(N) by construction, with one player.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_sd2.py: in-edges into v = [] and into v' = [] for K=3,4,5,6; all-switches alone on SD(K) has switch multiset {v: K, x_j: 1 each}. t_one.py builds the stripped one-player game SD1(K): K=3,4,5,6,8 give N=28,37,51,60,87, |Vmin|=0, stopping, all-switches rounds = K, v switched K times. Also note K rounds against |C| = 2K+2, so SD(K) is nowhere near any round ceiling.

findings.defect: Prior-art risk not flagged. FROM MEMORY, UNCHECKED AGAINST THE SOURCE: van Dijk, Loho and Maat have a paper on the worst-case complexity of symmetric strategy improvement, which I believe establishes an EXPONENTIAL lower bound for that rule on parity games. If that recollection is right, the route's central open question — the round count of def:bsi — is already answered negatively in the literature for the parity-game form of the same rule, and the whole route is chasing a family that exists in print. rbr:rem-attr says only "we do not know of a published family separating either rule from all-switches", which is a strictly narrower claim than "no published lower bound" and does not discharge this. The route (and rem:bsi-br, which already attributes def:bsi to those authors) must record the risk explicitly.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:bsi-br already attributes def:bsi to van Dijk--Loho--Maat and R_BR to its one-track variant, and says "if it holds then the round count of def:bsi is their open question and not ours" — so the document already knows the rule is theirs, and the lower-bound literature for it was not checked. No web access was used; this is a memory flag, not a citation.

findings.defect: Proved only for the STRICT variant, while the headline and the results summary say "forces BOTH BSI tracks to be long" without qualification — and def:bsi proper is the VETO variant, which is the one on which the document's only long-ish runs occur (rbr:prop-q16 shows three of Q_16's four reversals are ties that the strict variant refuses). But the restriction is UNNECESSARY: the theorem holds for the veto variant too, by the paper's own lem:bsi-pairloc. Proof: at a productive veto-variant round with C_min = empty, M > 0 (else thm:bsi-nostall gives a halt) and the strict-variant C_min^< is contained in C_min = empty, so lem:bsi-pairloc (stated there for both variants) gives Z intersect C_max^> nonempty, hence |C_max^>| >= 1 and Phi(sigma',U) >= Phi(sigma,U)+1. So within a maximal block of consecutive C_min = empty rounds Phi strictly increases, blocks have length <= m, blocks number <= B+1, and A <= m(1+B), R <= m+(m+1)B for def:bsi as written. The same block argument also makes the D-bookkeeping of rbr:lem-greedy redundant: the whole theorem is "with U frozen the Max track runs at most m rounds", i.e. prop:bsi-oneplayer relativised, in three lines.
findings.evidence: Proof above from lem:bsi-pairloc (frontier.tex line 6391) and thm:bsi-nostall (line 6355). Empirically consistent: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_block.py, 206 veto-variant rounds with C_min empty drawn from random stopping games, 0 with C_max^> empty; t_track.py, 1022 runs of both variants, 0 violations of sum|C_max| <= m+mB, R <= m+(m+1)B, R <= k+(k+1)A.

findings.result_name: rbr:thm-track, corollary "BSI is polynomial whenever min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) = O(log N)"
findings.defect: Stated without the remark that makes it honest: the class min(m,k) = O(log N) is TRIVIALLY in P, by enumerating the smaller player's 2^{min(m,k)} = poly(N) positional strategies and taking the componentwise extremum of the resulting one-player values (w* = min over positional tau of val^tau, each val^tau computable by thm:one-player's LP). So the corollary is a statement about the RULE, not a new polynomial class, and it is a one-line generalisation of thm:one-player (the min = 0 case). As written a reader will take it for a seventh polynomial class.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex thm:one-player (line 2032) gives val for Vmin = empty by one LP; determinacy plus positional optimality of Min gives w* = min_tau val^tau. The route's own text does not say the class is trivially decidable.

findings.defect: "It also raises the largest BSI round count known here from 11 (round 14's annealing) to Theta(N)" is false as a statement about what is achievable: Theta(N) BSI rounds is obtained by an eight-line ONE-PLAYER cascade, and by prop:bsi-oneplayer's own bound |Vmax| being attained. The "11" was a search artefact, not a record.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_cascade.py: the cascade x_j -> (x_{j-1}, k_j) with val(k_j) = 1 - 2^{-j}, N = 2K+2, Vmin empty, gives all-switches = BSI = K rounds for K = 3,5,8,12. (Incidentally the ladder L_n gives BSI = 1 round for n = 3,4,6,8, which is a datum the document does not have.)

findings.defect: "Refuting the standing belief that best-response restart is never slower" attacks a belief that frontier.tex does not hold. rem:bsi-br records exactly two measurements (L_n, G#) and states in terms that "the round count of R_BR is open, exactly as that of def:bsi is". The theorem itself is correct and new in this document; the framing is not. Separately, the significance should be calibrated: RD(n) has all-switches BA height 1 from EVERY Max strategy, R_BR = n = |Vmax| and BSI = 2n = |C|, all at the natural ceiling for a rule that switches one vertex per round (thm:short-path), so the family is no progress on the pivot and no progress on any lower bound — its content is purely the removal of the two data points that favoured R_BR.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:bsi-br, lines 6609-6665. Independent verification of RD(n) in exact arithmetic (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_rd.py): n = 2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12 give N = 9n, stopping, all-switches = 1, R_BR = n (both variants), BSI = 2n (both variants); exhaustive over all 2^n Max starts for n <= 4 gives all-switches worst case 1 and R_BR worst case n; val_sigma cross-checked against the componentwise min over all positional tau.

findings.defect: Two problems. (a) DEPENDENCY: the lemma is derived from bsr:prop-selfdual, which is NOT in frontier.tex — the string "self-dual" occurs zero times in the document; it is round 14's unintegrated bsi-rounds route. Nothing here can be integrated until that proposition is. (b) STRENGTH: given bsr:prop-selfdual the lemma is a one-line substitution (mirror-pairing turns that proposition's veto L(phi sigma-bar(v)) <= L(phi sigma(v)) into L(sigma(v)) <= L(sigma-bar(v)), automatic on S_sigma), and its transfer is only a SUFFICIENCY: it is useful only if the mirror-paired class realises AUSOs of superpolynomial BA height, and the route's own search found exactly m rounds at m = 1,2,3,4 against h*(m) = 1,2,4,7. The route does not state the sharp missing question, which is: can a mirror-paired self-dual stopping SSG have an all-switches run longer than |Vmax| rounds? If not, rbr:lem-vacuous is vacuous.
findings.evidence: grep -c 'bsr:' /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex = 0; grep -n 'self-dual' /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex = 0 hits. bsr:prop-selfdual is at /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/root16/r14routes/bsi-rounds/bsi_rounds.tex line 91. The route's own t17_psdexact.py re-run prints "best exactly verified: 4" at m = 4.

findings.defect: Correct but of very low significance, and rem:rbr-rate overstates it ("close the local half of the rate question"). On GAIN(s) the ENTIRE BSI run is two rounds and M falls from 1/2 to 0 in the very round whose gain is called small: the same round also switches u in C_min, which drops U(u) from 1/2 to 0. So the instance bears on no rate of M at all; it refutes only a statement about one particular switched vertex's L-gain, a hypothesis the document never advanced.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_rate.py: for s = 1,2,4,8,12 the trace is t=0 with M = 1/2, Z = {u,z}, C_max = {z}, C_min = {u}, gain(z) = M*2^{-s}; t=1 with M = 0 and both veto sets empty. The gain ratios 1/2, 1/4, 1/16, 1/256, 1/4096 are as claimed.

findings.defect: Verified exactly, but it mostly re-illustrates a caveat the paper already carries. cor:bsi-levels already says in frontier.tex that "the levels are within a factor |V| of the rounds, so the corollary names the quantity to be bounded rather than reducing it"; on SL(K) rounds = levels = K, which is that sentence with numbers. Its one genuinely new bit is that M can stay above 1/2 for Theta(N) rounds, killing "M halves every O(1) rounds". Worth one sentence, not a proposition. The docstring in rate.py also says N = 4K+2 where the LaTeX says 6K+4; the LaTeX is right.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_rate.py: K = 2,3,4,6,8 give N = 6K+4 = 16,22,28,40,52, rounds = K, and M = 3/4, 5/8, 9/16, 17/32, ... = 1/2 + 2^{-t-2} exactly as predicted, then 0.

findings.defect: True and useful as a bookkeeping remark, but it is one line from cor:comparison (U(p) >= L(p) > L(c) = U(c)) and carries no content beyond it. The "364 occurrences with 0 violations" is decoration on a one-line proof. Integrate as a footnote, not a lemma.
findings.evidence: The proof as given in the route's own LaTeX is a single chain of three inequalities from cor:comparison.

findings.defect: Two claims rest on random sampling and by the standing rule are unsupported as evidence: "a random search over stopping games with up to 14 non-sinks ... produced no run exceeding |C| rounds" and "hours of random restart plus hill climbing ... produced longest all-switches runs 1,2,3,4". The route labels both as open/measured, which is the right disposition, but the round-count table must not be read as bounding anything. Everything else in the route that I checked is honestly verified: exact rational arithmetic throughout, every val_sigma/val^tau certified as a fixed point, brute-force cross-checks present, and every family varies its own parameter at four or more sizes.
findings.evidence: I reproduced RD(n) at n = 2..12, SD(K) at K = 2..6, SL(K) at K = 2..8, GAIN(s) at s = 1..12, Q_16's full BSI trace, and the two small instances, all in an independently written harness (aud.py) with val_sigma cross-checked against the componentwise min over all positional tau; every number in rbr:prop-measure that I checked (SD(6): N=76, BSI=allsw=6, sw=6; RD(6): N=54, BSI=12, R_BR=6, allsw=1; SL(8): N=52, 8 rounds) is correct.

audits.verdict:
IS IT NEW? Mostly yes, with two exceptions and one big caveat. rbr:thm-readout (RD(n)) is the one clearly new object in the route: a proved family on which R_BR takes n rounds and BSI 2n where all-switches takes 1 from every Max strategy. Nothing in frontier.tex does this; thm:ladder separates least-index from all-switches (exponentially), thm:all-switches-refuted separates a single switch from all-switches on 5 vertices, and neither touches a val^tau-guided rule. rbr:lem-greedy/rbr:thm-track is new as a statement but is prop:bsi-oneplayer relativised — its real content is one sentence ("with U frozen the Max track runs at most m rounds"), and the D-bookkeeping is redundant. rbr:prop-sd is NOT new in the way it is sold (see finding 2): stripped of decoration it is a one-player all-switches construction that extends prop:allswitch-overshoot's three-switches-at-one-vertex to Theta(N), and the self-duality only transports it to BSI via rbr:lem-vacuous. rbr:lem-constant is cor:comparison. rbr:lem-vacuous is a one-line corollary of an unintegrated round-14 proposition. rbr:prop-slowlevel largely re-illustrates cor:bsi-levels' own printed caveat. The route's attributions of def:bsi/R_BR are correct and inherited from rem:bsi-br; the "readout" device is correctly credited to the solo round. The unflagged prior-art risk is the lower-bound literature for symmetric strategy improvement (finding 3).

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No claimed algorithm and no target-equivalent oracle. No barrier is claimed. The only class-shaped claim is "BSI is polynomial when min(m,k) = O(log N)", and that class is trivially decidable by enumerating the smaller player's strategies (finding 5) — the statement is about the rule only and must say so. rbr:lem-vacuous is a conditional transfer whose usefulness is unknown and may be nil. RD(n) and SD(K) are genuine families: build(n), stopping (verified by lem:trapchar), out-degree two, fair coins, measured at >= 4 sizes with proofs.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Yes, with one false statement. Everything I re-derived independently in exact arithmetic checked out except rbr:prop-small's uniqueness claim, which is false and weakens what that instance shows (finding 1). The two random-sampling claims are correctly labelled as open/measured.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's GAP is a proposed counter ARCHITECTURE, not the missing object. The missing object is: a stopping SSG family on N = n^{O(1)} vertices and a pair start on which def:bsi performs superpolynomially many productive rounds. By rbr:thm-track — extended to def:bsi proper as in finding 4 — such a family must have BOTH A and B superpolynomial, hence min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) = omega(log N), so it cannot be one-player and cannot be a disjoint union. The route's own rbr:lem-vacuous supplies the only reduction it has, and that reduction is unusable until a cheaper question is settled, which the route should have marked as its GAP and did not: CAN A MIRROR-PAIRED SELF-DUAL STOPPING SSG HAVE AN ALL-SWITCHES RUN LONGER THAN |Vmax| ROUNDS? If no, rbr:lem-vacuous is vacuous and the route's next_steps (3) is dead; if yes, the route's problem is a strict specialisation of the all-switches pivot (cor:ceiling-general), not an independent problem. Neither RD(n) nor SD(K) moves any lower bound: both are linear, both sit at or below |C| rounds, RD(n) has all-switches BA height 1, and SD(K) has K rounds against |C| = 2K+2.

INTEGRATE? NET BETTER, but only after edits; roughly half the route should not go in. WORTH INTEGRATING: (i) rbr:thm-readout and rbr:def-rd, verbatim modulo the "standing belief"/"raises the record" rhetoric, which is wrong (findings 6, 7) — this is the route's real contribution and it settles a question rem:bsi-br leaves open; (ii) rbr:lem-greedy/rbr:thm-track, rewritten in three lines as the block argument, EXTENDED to the veto variant via lem:bsi-pairloc (finding 4), and with the triviality caveat on the min(m,k) corollary (finding 5) — the quantitative "both tracks must be long" sharpens rem:bsi-gap's qualitative "must be genuinely two-player"; (iii) rbr:prop-q16, two sentences: Q_16's four reversals are three L-ties plus one strict switch, so round 14's four-switch record is a veto-variant tie artefact and the strict record there was one; (iv) rbr:lem-constant as a footnote to cor:comparison. WORTH INTEGRATING ONLY AFTER REWRITING: rbr:prop-sd, restated as a ONE-PLAYER proposition — "there is a one-player stopping SSG on O(K^2) vertices with |Vmax| = K+1 on which all-switches switches one vertex K times", superseding prop:allswitch-overshoot's three — followed by one line saying rbr:lem-vacuous carries it to BSI; the current two-player self-dual presentation hides that the observer is unreachable and that no Min player is needed. NOT WORTH INTEGRATING: rbr:prop-gain (finding 9); the rbr:rem-psd witness matrices (three 4x4 matrices of measured, non-transferable content that prop:auso-size says can prove nothing); rbr:prop-small as written (fix the false parenthetical or drop the first instance, keeping only the 10-non-sink one, which makes the same point correctly); rbr:prop-slowlevel beyond one sentence. And rbr:def-psd/rbr:lem-vacuous cannot be integrated at all until round 14's bsr:prop-selfdual is, since "self-dual" does not occur in frontier.tex.

result.route: Bounded width: a seventh polynomial class, or the exact place where interface tables explode
result.headline: Both halves settled. NEGATIVE: the exact-table dynamic programme over a decomposition explodes already at treewidth 3 / pathwidth 4 -- thm:fold's P_D has exactly 2^{(N-2)/6} response pieces with tw(P_D)=pw(P_D)=4 (exact), and the explosion is impossible at interface dimension one (tw:one-live), so the threshold is located exactly. POSITIVE: the SEARCH does not explode. Running the Etessami-Papadimitriou-Rubinstein-Yannakakis Tarski fixed-point search on lem:cut's cut map F_S at every bag of a balanced separator recursion decides SSG-Value on stopping games of treewidth k in 2^{O(k log^2 N)} = N^{O(k log N)} exact arithmetic operations -- QUASIPOLYNOMIAL at every constant width, beating thm:subexp's e^{2 sqrt n} there (flagged as new but a candidate rediscovery; no such algorithm is known to me for quantitative SSG values). The seventh polynomial class is tw:modulator: N^{O(mu)} where mu is the least number of vertices whose FREEZING puts the game in any freezing-closed polynomial class; for P = k-acyclic this answers the question rem:kacyclic explicitly leaves open (what happens when mu_k > 0), and it strictly generalises Auger-Coucheney-Strozecki's feedback-vertex parameter. A companion theorem, poly(N)2^{f_k} where f_k is the number of colour-k vertices on cycles, is also new to the paper. The family M_n (N = 5n+3, two players) has mu_max = 1, feedback vertex number >= n+1, and is OUTSIDE all six existing polynomial classes -- including a clean proof that every escape certificate for it has 1 - lambda < 4*2^{-n}. Validated: 300 stopping SSGs built from random tree decompositions of width <= 3, plus 150 of exact treewidth 3, zero mismatches against brute-force max-min, all in exact rational arithmetic and self-certified by T(w)=w.

results.name: tw:response
results.statement: For a set A of non-terminals with outer boundary dA, the response function R_A(phi) = val of the game on A with dA frozen at phi is monotone; the value is equivariant under an affine change of ALL terminal payoffs, hence 1-Lipschitz in sup norm in the full payoff vector and in any subvector; on stopping games R_A is piecewise affine with at most 2^{|C cap A|} distinct affine pieces, each v_{sigma,tau}(phi) = sum_w h_{sigma,tau}(v,w) phi_w with h the first-passage law, and the region where one pair is optimal is a convex polyhedron. The piece number pi(A) is what a table-storing DP must pay.
results.argument: Monotonicity is the first line of lem:cut's proof. Equivariance: max, min and the mean commute with x -> ax+b, so the shifted/scaled operator is conjugate to T and the least fixed points correspond; monotone + shift-equivariant implies nonexpansive. Traps of the frozen game are traps of H, so stopping is inherited (lem:trapchar) and I-P_{sigma,tau} is invertible (lem:denominator), giving affineness by expanding (I-P)^{-1} = sum P^k. thm:stopping-determinacy gives val = max-min of these; lem:local-global cuts the optimality region out by affine inequalities.
results.verification: Exact arithmetic on 400 random stopping games of treewidth <= 3 with random frozen sets |S| <= 4: 1600 monotonicity checks, 1600 sup-norm-Lipschitz checks, 1221 affine-equivariance checks, no failure. (The first version of the claim -- shift-equivariance in the FREE coordinates alone -- was REFUTED by the test and corrected: t_0, t_1 do not move.)

results.name: tw:fold-width
results.statement: For thm:fold's P_D with A = V minus {u,t0,t1}: the coordinate of R_A at F_D has exactly 2^D = 2^{(|V|-2)/6} affine pieces with breakpoints j*2^{-D}, and pi(A) = 2^D as well. Moreover tw(P_D) = pw(P_D) = 2 for D=1, 3 for D=2,3, and 4 for D=4; pw(P_D) <= 4 for every D by an explicit path decomposition, and pw(P_D) > 3 for 4 <= D <= 8. Hence no bound pi <= poly(N, tw): the exact response tables are 2^{Omega(N)} already at treewidth four.
results.argument: The piece count is thm:fold. The widths: the exact elimination-ordering and vertex-separation subset DPs on Gamma(P_D) (6D vertices) for D <= 3; the layout u, X_1, k_{2D-1}, Y_1, F_1, G_1, (k_{2D-2d+2}, k_{2D-2d+1}, X_d, Y_d, F_d, G_d)_{d=2..D} with bags B_i = {v_i} u (frontier of the prefix) gives width 4 for all D; and an exhaustive search over all layouts/elimination orderings of width 3 finds none for 4 <= D <= 8.
results.verification: thm:fold's identity re-derived in exact arithmetic for D <= 8 at every dyadic grid point, every midpoint and five off-grid rationals, against backward induction, slope set exactly {0, 2^{-D}}; the 2^D optimal pairs on the 2^D intervals are pairwise distinct for D <= 8; the width-4 path decomposition verified as a genuine decomposition for D <= 12 and D = 20,30,45,60.

results.name: tw:one-live
results.statement: Let H be a payoff game with no directed cycle among its non-terminals, z a terminal, Z the set of non-terminals from which z is reachable, and suppose every vertex of Z has AT MOST ONE successor in Z u {z}. Then theta -> val_{H[z:=theta]}(v) is monotone, 1-Lipschitz and piecewise affine with at most |Z|+1 pieces.
results.argument: Each v in Z has exactly one theta-dependent successor w, the other having a constant value c_v; so f_v = op_v(f_w, c_v) with op_v in {max(.,c), min(.,c), (.+c)/2}, each monotone, 1-Lipschitz and adding at most one breakpoint. Induction along a topological order. The point is that every SSG value is NONDECREASING in every other (lem:monotone), so a one-dimensional interface transports a composition of monotone one-variable maps, whose preimages of a breakpoint are single points: no folding accumulates. thm:fold's fold is exactly a two-dimensional interface -- F_d and G_d read the SAME pair, and max - min = |.| in the difference coordinate.
results.verification: Proof only; the complementary side (2^D at interface dimension two) is tw:fold-width.

results.name: tw:no-clock
results.statement: Let Lambda be a two-input two-output gadget whose internal vertices read no terminal and from each of which an input is reachable. Then Phi(f+c,g+c) = Phi(f,g)+c and Phi(lf,lg) = l*Phi(f,g), so Phi_1 - Phi_2 = psi(f-g) with psi(d) = alpha*d for d >= 0 and beta*|d| for d <= 0; psi^D has at most two affine pieces for every D, and a chain of D copies of Lambda has at most two linearity domains in the initial difference. A fold that accumulates therefore requires the gadget to read a terminal.
results.argument: max, min and the mean commute with x -> x+c and with x -> lx applied to both inputs; Lambda stopping makes the fixed point unique so the conjugated operators have corresponding fixed points. Additive homogeneity gives Phi_i(f,g) = g + Phi_i(f-g,0), positive homogeneity makes psi linear on each half-line through 0, and such maps compose to such maps, so sign(psi^j(d_0)) is determined by sign(d_0).
results.verification: 3000 random acyclic terminal-free gadgets in exact arithmetic: no violation of either identity; the difference map of 400 of them has at most two affine pieces, breaking only at 0. (The stopping hypothesis is necessary and is stated: an internal cycle with no input reachable has lfp value 0, which does not move.)

results.name: tw:cut-sign
results.statement: For a stopping payoff game H and a set S of non-terminals, lem:cut's cut map F_S satisfies: H[x] is stopping for every x; val_H|_S is the UNIQUE fixed point of F_S; and F_S(x) <= x implies x >= val_H|_S, while F_S(x) >= x implies x <= val_H|_S.
results.argument: A trap of H[x] avoids the terminals hence avoids S, so it is a trap of H and empty. Assembling x with val_{H[x]} and using eq:assembly turns F_S(x) <= x into T_H xhat <= xhat and F_S(x) >= x into T_H xhat >= xhat; cor:comparison (stopping) gives the two conclusions, and applying both at a fixed point gives uniqueness. This two-sided sign property is contained in lem:cut's proof but not stated there.
results.verification: Exact arithmetic on 400 random stopping games of treewidth <= 3 with random S: 400 checks that val|_S is a fixed point of F_S and 2400 checks of the two sign implications at random grid points; no failure.

results.name: tw:tarski
results.statement: For a finite chain L with M elements and a monotone F: L^d -> L^d, a fixed point is found with at most 2(ceil(log2 M)+1)^d evaluations of F, by: recurse into the (d-1)-dimensional slice at the midpoint m of the last coordinate to get y*; evaluate F at x = (y*, m); if F(x)_d = m return x; if F(x)_d > m recurse on [F(x), hi]; else on [lo, F(x)].
results.argument: Invariant: F maps the box into itself, so Knaster-Tarski gives a fixed point inside; the slice map is monotone into itself, so the recursive call is legitimate and F(x)_{<d} = x_{<d}. If F(x)_d > m then F(x) >= x, so F maps [F(x),hi] into itself; symmetric otherwise. Progress: the new corner has last coordinate >= m+1 (resp. <= m-1), so that range at least halves. Cost recursion Q(d,M) <= (log M + 1)(Q(d-1,M)+1). Using F(x) rather than x as the new corner removes the usual need for the recursive call to return a LEAST fixed point.
results.verification: 400 random monotone maps on boxes of dimension up to 4 and side up to 63: every returned point is a fixed point, mean 13.8 queries; and agreement with exhaustive enumeration of all fixed points on 300 small boxes. (An earlier version that cut at x rather than F(x) was found to LOOP FOREVER on an explicit 4x4 map and was discarded.)

results.name: tw:round + tw:recover
results.statement: For a finite chain L of mesh eps, F^L = roundup_L o F_S is a monotone self-map of L^S and every fixed point thetahat of it satisfies val_H|_S <= thetahat <= val_H|_S + N*2^a*eps. If Delta is a common denominator of H's terminal payoffs, every value of H has denominator dividing an integer <= Q = Delta*2^a, so an approximation within 1/(2Q^2) recovers the exact value by continued fractions.
results.argument: Round-up is monotone; thetahat >= F_S(thetahat) gives thetahat >= val by tw:cut-sign, and thetahat <= F_S(thetahat) + eps assembles to T xhat <= xhat <= T xhat + eps, whence ||xhat - val|| <= sum_k (1-2^{-a})^{floor(k/N)} eps = N 2^a eps by thm:contraction (which holds verbatim for payoff games, lem:gen-comparison). Recovery: Cramer with det A_U <= 2^a (lem:denominator-sharp) and Legendre's convergent theorem.
results.verification: Used inside every run of the algorithm, and every run ends with an exact check T(w) = w; over 300 + 150 + 48 solved games there was no certification retry, so the a-priori precision was always sufficient.

results.name: tw:modulator (with cor tw:kacyclic-mu)
results.statement: Call a class P of payoff games freezing-closed if it is preserved by retyping any set of vertices as terminals with arbitrary payoffs, and let mu_P(G) be the least |X| with G[X:=theta] in P for all theta. If P is freezing-closed and solvable exactly in time p(n,beta), then the value vector of a stopping payoff game G is computed exactly in O((B+2)^{mu} p(n,O(B)) + poly) with B = O(a + log N + log Delta); for an SSG this is N^{O(mu)}p(N,O(N)), polynomial whenever mu = O(1). The k-acyclic classes are freezing-closed and are solvable for arbitrary terminal payoffs (thm:kacyclic), so SSG-Value is decidable in N^{O(mu_k)} -- which answers the question rem:kacyclic explicitly leaves open, and reduces to thm:kacyclic at mu_k = 0.
results.argument: Freeze X at a grid point, solve the residual game in P exactly, apply op_x at each x in X: this evaluates lem:cut's F_X exactly, so the computed map is exactly F_X and monotone. Round up onto the dyadic grid of mesh eps = 1/(4N 2^a Q^2) (tw:round), run tw:tarski in dimension mu, recover exactly (tw:recover), solve once more at the recovered theta for the values off X (lem:cut, last clause), and certify by T_G w = w, which pins the answer because a stopping game has a unique fixed point.
results.verification: Implemented (modulator.py) and run on M_n for 2 <= n <= 12 with X = {h}: 10 or 11 cut-map evaluations, exact value vector, certified by T(w)=w, and cross-checked against brute-force max-min for n <= 4 and against Hoffman-Karp throughout. Also run on P_D^circ for D <= 12 with X = {u}: four evaluations, exact.

results.name: tw:colour-feedback
results.statement: For k in {max,min} let f_k(G) be the number of kind-k vertices lying on a directed cycle. Then the value vector of an ARBITRARY SSG, stopping or not, is computable exactly in time poly(N) 2^{f_k(G)}; polynomial when f_k = O(log N). (Not available for k = avg: a coin cannot be frozen.)
results.argument: Enumerate the 2^{f_k} choices on the set F of kind-k vertices on cycles; retype each v in F as an AVERAGE vertex with both out-edges to the chosen successor, which leaves the operator's value unchanged. No Max vertex of the modified game lies on a cycle -- those of F are no longer Max, those outside F lie on no cycle by the choice of F -- so it is max-acyclic and thm:kacyclic solves it in polynomial time with no stopping hypothesis. Positional determinacy gives val = max over the enumeration (min for k = min), since Max restricted can only lose and equality holds at sigma*|_F.
results.verification: The enumeration agrees with brute-force max-min on 200 instances, both colours, exact arithmetic, no failure. Note mu_k <= f_k always, so tw:modulator applies whenever this does; the two bounds N^{O(mu_k)} and 2^{f_k} are incomparable.

results.name: tw:qp
results.statement: SSG-Value on stopping payoff games given a tree decomposition of width k of the interaction graph is decided EXACTLY with 2^{O(k log^2 n)} = n^{O(k log n)} arithmetic operations on rationals of O(n^{1+log_2 3} + n^{log_2 3} log Delta) bits. In particular any family of treewidth O(1) is decidable in QUASIPOLYNOMIAL time N^{O(log N)}, self-certified by T(w) = w.
results.argument: Balanced-separator recursion. A centroid bag X (|X| <= k+1) leaves components of at most n/2 vertices; each component's successors lie in the component, X or the terminals, so freezing X at theta gives independent stopping subgames of treewidth <= k and half the size, and solving them recursively evaluates lem:cut's F_X exactly at theta. At each node run tw:round + tw:tarski in dimension k+1 over a dyadic grid of B = O(3a + 2 log Delta + log n) bits, then tw:recover. Bit bookkeeping: delta_{j+1} <= 3 delta_j + 4n over log_2 n levels gives O(n^{2.585}) bits. Cost: T(n) <= 2(B+2)^{k+1} * (sum_i T(n_i)) <= n^{O(k)} * 2T(n/2), so T(n) = 2^{O(k log^2 n)}.
results.verification: Implemented (alg.py) in exact rational arithmetic. 300 stopping SSGs built from RANDOM TREE DECOMPOSITIONS of width <= 3 (exact treewidth 1/2/3 on 62/167/41, 30 above the exact-DP budget): 0 mismatches against brute-force max-min, 616773 cut-map queries, maximal Tarski dimension 4, maximal grid 2^100, no certification retry. A second run of 150 games of EXACT treewidth 3 with the base case lowered to three vertices (deepest recursion): 0 mismatches, 62602 queries, grid up to 2^82. Beyond brute-force range, batches of twelve games at 16, 22, 28 and 34 non-sink vertices agree with the independent Hoffman-Karp solver and satisfy T(w) = w. FLAGGED: this is new to my knowledge but a candidate rediscovery; see the literature remark.

results.name: tw:cyclic
results.statement: P_D^circ (P_D with u retyped as an average vertex u -> (F_D, t_1)) is a stopping SSG on 6D+2 vertices with pw <= 5 (tw = pw = 4 at D = 3), every cycle of which meets u; val(u) = 1/2 + 3*2^{-(D+3)} for D >= 2, which lies in the MIDDLE piece (the 2^{D-1}-st of 2^D) of the response function of tw:fold-width. The algorithm of tw:modulator with X = {u} returns the exact value vector after FOUR cut-map evaluations for every 2 <= D <= 12, while the exact table has 2^D pieces.
results.argument: The instance closes thm:fold's fold into a genuine cycle so that the exponential table cannot be side-stepped by choosing the sweep direction (P_D itself is acyclic, so tw:fold-width alone is a statement about tables, not instances). It exhibits the dichotomy of this section on one family: the table is 2^{Omega(N)} and the search is O(1) queries.
results.verification: Exact computation for D <= 12: stopping, freezing u leaves an acyclic game, value formula, piece index, and the query count are all from the exact implementation; the widths are the exact subset DPs at D <= 3 and the explicit decomposition with u added to every bag otherwise.

results.name: tw:family (M_n)
results.statement: M_n (N = 5n+3, a = 3n, |Vmax| = n+1, |Vmin| = n; a Max/Min/avg ring through a Max hub h feeding thm:vi-lower's ratchet G_n) is stopping, fully reachable from h, has mu_max = 1 with X = {h} and feedback vertex number >= n+1, and lies OUTSIDE all six polynomial classes: a = 3(N-3)/5; the ring cycle carries all three kinds so no k-acyclicity holds; H(M_n) is a single SCC on all n+1 Max vertices; val(c_1) = 1/2 + 2^{-(n+1)} and min_j val(c_j) = 2^{-n} so the common denominator is >= 2^{n+1}; d(M_n) >= n; and EVERY escape certificate has 1 - lambda < 4*2^{-n}, so thm:escape-class gives at least a*2^{n-3} rounds. Yet tw:modulator solves it in polynomial time, and val(h) = 1/2 + 2^{-(n+1)} so the threshold is decided by an exponentially small margin.
results.argument: Stopping by peeling the trap from c_{2n} inward. Every cycle through an x_i must run forward through x_{i+1},...,x_n,h and back, so freezing h destroys every Max cycle while the y_i <-> b_i two-cycles and the c-part cycles survive: mu_max = 1 but fvs >= n+1 (n+1 pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles), so the class strictly beats the feedback vertex number. The c-part is successor-closed, so lem:successor-closed + thm:vi-lower give its values. d(M_n) >= n: the levels of lem:descent's filtration are l(c_i) = n-i+1, each c_i (i <= n) has exactly one successor of strictly smaller level, so the descent path c_1 -> ... -> c_n -> t_1 has sum omega = n, for every sigma. Escape: for i < n, (x(c_1)+x(c_{i+1}))/2 <= lambda x(c_i) gives u_{i+1} <= 2 lambda u_i - 1 with u_1 = 1; u_n > 0 forces g(t) := 2t(2-2t)^{n-1} < 1 with t = 1-lambda, and g >= 1 on [4*2^{-n}, 1/2], so t < 4*2^{-n}.
results.verification: Exact solves for n <= 12, cross-checked against brute-force max-min for n <= 4 and certified by T(w) = w; value alphabet n+3 letters and common denominator exactly 2^{n+1}; d(M_n) = n+1 with a unique optimal Max strategy for n <= 7; mu_max = 1 and no feedback vertex set of size <= min(n,5) by exhaustive search; and the exact-arithmetic feasibility test finds NO escape certificate at lambda = 1 - 4*2^{-n} for n = 3,4,5, matching the proved threshold.

results.name: tw:gap2-shape (searches toward GAP 2)
results.statement: For chains of one fixed gadget that may read t_0, the level map in the projective coordinate is a piecewise-Moebius psi(r) = B/(A+B), and GAP 2 asks whether some such psi has an invariant interval carrying two full monotone branches. Two searches say no. (a) Over the closure of {0, f, g} under max/min/mean capped at 260 piecewise-linear functions, all 59315 admissible ordered pairs (A,B): the largest piece count of psi^D for D = 1..9 anywhere is 5,13,23,35,49,65,83,101,119 -- QUADRATIC, against 2^9 = 512. (b) Allowing t_1 as well, so Phi:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1]^2 is a general autonomous monotone nonexpansive PL map, the number of distinct itineraries of Phi^D on an exact 25x25 rational grid SATURATES AT 11 within three steps over 200 random gadgets.
results.argument: Not a proof. Search (a) is exhaustive over a finite closure of gadget outputs but that closure is capped; search (b) is random, which by the standing experience of this project is no evidence at all. Both are reported as measurements, and both are consistent with tw:no-clock's proved statement that a terminal-free chain cannot fold twice.
results.verification: mobsearch.py (exact rational piecewise-Moebius composition, 59315 pairs) and t_2d.py (exact rational grid itineraries, 200 gadgets).

result.gap:
GAP 1 (the main one). MISSING STATEMENT: "There is an algorithm that computes the value vector of every stopping SSG of treewidth k in time N^{f(k)} for some function f." tw:qp gives N^{O(k log N)}; the loss is exactly the factor 2 per level of the balanced separator recursion, each level re-solving both sides from scratch at every Tarski query, and storing the response function instead of re-querying it is precisely what tw:fold-width forbids (2^{Omega(N)} pieces at treewidth 4).

GAP 2. MISSING STATEMENT: "There is a family of stopping payoff games of pathwidth at most 3, with one free parameter, whose response function has 2^{Omega(N)} affine pieces." tw:fold-width achieves this at pathwidth 4 and tw:one-live forbids it at interface dimension one; tw:no-clock proves that a chain of identical terminal-free gadgets cannot fold twice, and tw:gap2-shape reduces what remains, for chains of one fixed gadget, to: "is there a piecewise-Moebius map psi(r) = Phi_2(1,r)/Phi_1(1,r), with Phi_1, Phi_2 built from max, min, the mean and the constant 0, having a nondegenerate invariant interval J on which psi has two monotone branches each mapping J onto J?"

Two further items are stated but not proved here and should not be cited as established: (i) that no polynomial or quasipolynomial algorithm for the QUANTITATIVE value of bounded-treewidth SSGs exists in the literature -- this is from memory only, and tw:qp is therefore flagged as a candidate rediscovery; (ii) the exact form (FPT vs XP, and the exact parameter) of Auger-Coucheney-Strozecki's almost-acyclic result, also from memory.
result.next_steps:
1. ATTACK GAP 1 FIRST -- it is the only thing between this route and a genuine seventh polynomial class covering all bounded-width instances. The obstruction is concrete and local: at a separator X the two sides are re-solved from scratch at each of the O(B^{k+1}) queries. Two ideas that do not obviously die: (a) warm-start the child search from the previous query's answer and bound the TOTAL work across a monotone sequence of queries (the Tarski search's queries are not monotone, but the sign-definiteness of tw:cut-sign means each query moves one corner of a shrinking box, so the children are solved on a nested family of payoff vectors -- a potential-function argument on the children might amortise the depth away); (b) replace the balanced separator by a path decomposition and a single left-to-right sweep in which the state is the value vector on one interface, so that the recursion depth is 1 and the cost is (number of interfaces) x (queries) -- this needs the interface fixed point to be solvable without recursion, which is exactly where the response table would be needed, so (a) looks more promising.

2. CHECK THE PRIOR ART. tw:qp is the single claim in this route most likely to be a rediscovery, and I could not check it. Someone with source access should verify: (i) whether any polynomial or quasipolynomial algorithm for SSG values at bounded treewidth is published; (ii) Auger-Coucheney-Strozecki's exact parameter and bound; (iii) whether Etessami-Papadimitriou-Rubinstein-Yannakakis (or Fearnley-Palvolgyi-Savani, Chen-Li) already combine Tarski search with graph decompositions.

3. IMPROVE THE MODULATOR CLASS. mu_P is defined for any freezing-closed P; only P = k-acyclic is instantiated here because thm:kacyclic is the only class in the paper stated for arbitrary terminal payoffs. Restating thm:few-avg, thm:few-escape, thm:escape-class and thm:bounded-components for payoff games would immediately widen the class, and each is a small piece of work. Also: mu_k is computable in N^{O(mu)} by brute force, but a polynomial-time recognition of "mu_k <= c" for fixed c is a separate (standard-looking, FPT-flavoured) question worth settling before the class is quoted as checkable.

4. USE tw:qp AS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT ON THE PIVOT. Every family in the document -- L_n, H_m, G_m, WD, CC, P_D -- has treewidth at most 4, so all of them are quasipolynomial by tw:qp and polynomial by tw:modulator. Any candidate superpolynomial ALL-SWITCHES family (the missing item of the AUSO pivot) that has bounded treewidth is therefore hard for the rule, not for the problem. If the root agent wants an instance that is genuinely hard, tw:qp says it must have treewidth omega(1) -- which is a real, cheap, checkable filter on future constructions and should be applied to G# and to any realisation of thm:blowup's second level.

5. SETTLE GAP 2 by answering the piecewise-Moebius question of tw:gap2-shape (a clean one-dimensional dynamics problem, independent of games), or by an engineered pathwidth-3 fold. Do NOT re-run random searches: the two reported here already say "probably not" and the standing rule is that random sampling is not evidence.
