\subsection{One-player all-switches runs are Holt--Klee walks}\label{sec:fs15}

\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} bounds the improvement \emph{orientation} of a
\emph{nondegenerate} one-player game, and \Cref{rem:oneplayer-lp} records that
the hypothesis is genuine: the longest one-player runs in this document are
degenerate, and \Cref{thm:flat-resolution} resolves those into orientations
that need not be Holt--Klee. This subsection removes the hypothesis at the only
place where it matters, namely along the run itself, and draws two conclusions:
the one-player and two-player run lengths already separate at $m=4$, and the
second level of \Cref{thm:blowup} needs Min vertices for its \emph{walk} and
not merely for its orientation.

\begin{definition}[One-player run length; the Holt--Klee ceiling]\label{fs15:def-f1}
Let $f_1(m)$ be the greatest length of an all-switches run of a stopping SSG
with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=m$, and let $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$ be
the greatest bottom-antipodal height of a Holt--Klee AUSO of the $m$-cube. By
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general}, $f_1(m)\le h^{\ast}(m)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Where a tie on a run can sit]\label{fs15:tie-partner}
Let $G$ be stopping with $|\Vmax|=m$, let $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ be an
all-switches run with switched sets $S_t$, and let $s'$ be the AUSO supplied by
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general}, so $s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ for every $t$. Suppose the
incidence $(\sigma_t,v)$ is tied, i.e.\
$\val_{\sigma_t}(\bar\sigma_t(v))=\val_{\sigma_t}(\sigma_t(v))$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $v\notin S_t$ and $\val_{\sigma_t[v]}=\val_{\sigma_t}$;
\item $S(\sigma_t[v])=S_t$;
\item $\sigma_t[v]\notin\{\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L\}$;
\item $s'(\sigma_t[v])=S_t\cup\{v\}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) A tie is not a strict improvement, so $v\notin S_t$; the equality of the
value vectors is \Cref{lem:trichotomy}. (b) For $u\ne v$ the margin
$\val_{\sigma}(\bar\sigma(u))-\val_\sigma(\sigma(u))$ depends only on the value
vector and on $\sigma(u)$, and $\sigma_t[v]$ agrees with $\sigma_t$ at $u$ and
carries the same value vector by (a); at $v$ both incidences are tied. (c) By
\Cref{lem:flat-class}(c) the strategies of a run lie in pairwise distinct flat
classes, that is, they carry pairwise distinct value vectors, while
$\val_{\sigma_t[v]}=\val_{\sigma_t}$. (d) By \Cref{lem:flat-class} the flat
class $A$ of $\sigma_t$ is a subcube on which $S$ and the flat direction set
$D$ are constant, and $v\in D$; the resolution of
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general} takes $c_A:=\sigma_t$, so by
\Cref{thm:flat-resolution}
$s'(\sigma_t[v])=S(\sigma_t[v])\cup\{i\in D:\sigma_t[v]_i\ne(\sigma_t)_i\}
 =S_t\cup\{v\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A one-player run is the walk of a Holt--Klee AUSO]\label{fs15:run-hk}
Let $G$ be a stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=m$, let
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ be its all-switches run, let
\[
  T:=\{(t,v)\ :\ 0\le t\le L,\ (\sigma_t,v)\ \text{is a tied incidence}\},
  \qquad
  D_{t,v}:=y^{\sigma_t}-y^{\sigma_t[v]}\in\mathbb R^{2m},
\]
with $y^{\sigma}$ the vertices of the occupancy polytope $X(G)$ of
\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}. If
\[
  0\ \notin\ \operatorname{conv}\{D_{t,v}:(t,v)\in T\}
\]
--- vacuously when $T=\emptyset$, automatically when $|T|\le1$, and more
generally whenever the $D_{t,v}$ are linearly independent --- then there is a
Holt--Klee AUSO of the $m$-cube whose bottom-antipodal walk from $\sigma_0$ is
exactly $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$. In particular
$L\le h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$X(G)$ depends only on the transition part of the normal form, not on the
payoff part, and by \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} it is a simple $m$-polytope whose
vertices are the $y^{\sigma}$, whose graph is the $m$-cube and whose faces are
its subcubes; that argument uses only that $G$ is stopping. Its objective
$\mathrm{obj}$ satisfies
$\mathrm{obj}(y^{\sigma[v]})-\mathrm{obj}(y^{\sigma})
 =\kappa_{\sigma,v}\bigl(\val_\sigma(\bar\sigma(v))-\val_\sigma(\sigma(v))\bigr)$
with $\kappa_{\sigma,v}=\sum_w h(w\!\to\!v)/(1-h(b\!\to\!v))>0$, by
\Cref{thm:impedance} summed over $w$; this identity needs no nondegeneracy.

Each $D_{t,v}$ is nonzero, since $y^{\sigma_t}$ and $y^{\sigma_t[v]}$ have
different supports. By hypothesis and the separating hyperplane theorem there
is $c\in\mathbb R^{2m}$ with $\langle c,D_{t,v}\rangle>0$ for every
$(t,v)\in T$. The set of such $c$ is a nonempty open cone, and the $c$ that are
constant on some edge of $X(G)$ form a finite union of hyperplanes, so $c$ may
be chosen in the cone and outside that union. Fix such a $c$ and put
$\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon:=\mathrm{obj}+\varepsilon c$.

For $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, $\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon$ is non-constant on
every edge of $X(G)$: on an edge where $\mathrm{obj}$ is non-constant the sign
survives, and on an edge where it is constant the difference is
$\varepsilon\langle c,\cdot\rangle\ne0$. So $\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon$ is a
generic linear objective on a simple polytope combinatorially equivalent to the
$m$-cube, and the orientation $s''$ it induces is an LP orientation, hence an
AUSO satisfying Holt--Klee on every face (Holt--Klee; G\"artner--Morris--R\"ust),
exactly as in \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}.

Finally $s''(\sigma_t)=S_t$ for every $t$. If $(\sigma_t,v)$ is not tied the
edge is non-constant for $\mathrm{obj}$ and its sign, which is that of the
margin by the displayed identity, is preserved. If it is tied then
$(t,v)\in T$ and
$\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon(y^{\sigma_t[v]})-\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon(y^{\sigma_t})
 =-\varepsilon\langle c,D_{t,v}\rangle<0$, so $v\notin s''(\sigma_t)$. Hence the
bottom-antipodal walk of $s''$ from $\sigma_0$ passes through
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_L$ and stops there, $s''(\sigma_L)=S_L=\emptyset$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{fs15:run-hk-cor}
If a one-player stopping SSG is nondegenerate at every strategy of its
all-switches run --- in particular, if it is nondegenerate --- then that run
has length at most $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$. Any one-player family whose
all-switches runs are superpolynomially long while
$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}$ is polynomially bounded must therefore be degenerate
at at least \emph{two} incidences of each long run, and the corresponding
occupancy differences $D_{t,v}$ must positively span $0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Two ties never span]\label{fs15:two-ties}
Let $(t_1,v_1)$ and $(t_2,v_2)$ be tied incidences on the run of a one-player
stopping SSG with $v_1\ne v_2$ and $\sigma_{t_2}(v_1)\ne\sigma_{t_1}(v_1)$.
Then $0\notin\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t_1,v_1},D_{t_2,v_2}\}$. Consequently a
tie set $T$ with $|T|=2$ can fail the hypothesis of \Cref{fs15:run-hk} only if
either the two ties sit at the \emph{same} Max vertex with opposite actions
there, or they sit at different vertices $v_1\ne v_2$ and each of
$\sigma_{t_1},\sigma_{t_2}$ agrees with the other at both $v_1$ and $v_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $a:=\sigma_{t_1}(v_1)$ and read the coordinate $(v_1,a)$ of
$\mathbb R^{2m}$. The vertex $y^{\sigma}$ is supported on
$\{(u,\sigma(u)):u\in\Vmax\}$ and is at least $\bbone$ there
(\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}). So $y^{\sigma_{t_1}}$ has mass
$\ge1$ at $(v_1,a)$ and $y^{\sigma_{t_1}[v_1]}$ has none, giving
$D_{t_1,v_1}[(v_1,a)]\ge1$; while $\sigma_{t_2}$ and $\sigma_{t_2}[v_2]$ both
take the action $1-a$ at $v_1$ --- they differ only at $v_2\ne v_1$ --- so
neither has mass at $(v_1,a)$ and $D_{t_2,v_2}[(v_1,a)]=0$. A convex
combination $c_1D_{t_1,v_1}+c_2D_{t_2,v_2}=0$ therefore forces $c_1=0$, hence
$c_2=1$ and $D_{t_2,v_2}=0$, which is false: the two vertices
$y^{\sigma_{t_2}}$ and $y^{\sigma_{t_2}[v_2]}$ have different supports. The
final sentence is the contrapositive, applied at $v_1$ and at $v_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What a two-tie escape must look like]\label{fs15:two-ties-cor}
Let $T=\{(t_1,v_1),(t_2,v_2)\}$ be the tied incidences on the run of a
one-player stopping SSG and suppose
$0\in\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t_1,v_1},D_{t_2,v_2}\}$. Then either
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $v_1=v_2=:v$ and $\sigma_{t_1}(v)\ne\sigma_{t_2}(v)$; or
\item $v_1\ne v_2$ and $\sigma_{t_1}$ agrees with $\sigma_{t_2}$ at both $v_1$
      and $v_2$.
\end{enumerate}
In case (i) the two strategies differ at some $u\notin\{v\}$, and for every
such $u$
\[
  y^{\sigma_{t_1}}_{u,\sigma_{t_1}(u)}=y^{\sigma_{t_1}[v]}_{u,\sigma_{t_1}(u)},
  \qquad
  y^{\sigma_{t_2}}_{u,\sigma_{t_2}(u)}=y^{\sigma_{t_2}[v]}_{u,\sigma_{t_2}(u)}:
\]
switching $v$ must leave the expected total occupancy of $u$ exactly unchanged,
although it changes the strategy there\,---\,at every coordinate on which the
two run strategies disagree.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{fs15:two-ties} gives the dichotomy, once one notes that $v_1=v_2=v$ with
$\sigma_{t_1}(v)=\sigma_{t_2}(v)=a$ is impossible: the coordinate $(v,a)$ then
receives $c_1y^{\sigma_{t_1}}_{v,a}+c_2y^{\sigma_{t_2}}_{v,a}$ with both terms
positive and both $y\ge1$, forcing $c_1=c_2=0$. In case (i), $\sigma_{t_2}$ is
neither $\sigma_{t_1}$ (distinct strategies of a run carry distinct value
vectors) nor $\sigma_{t_1}[v]$ (which is off the run, by
\Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c)), so they differ at some $u\ne v$. Fix such a $u$
and read the coordinate $(u,\sigma_{t_1}(u))$: since
$\sigma_{t_2}(u)\ne\sigma_{t_1}(u)$ and $\sigma_{t_2},\sigma_{t_2}[v]$ agree at
$u$, the vector $D_{t_2,v}$ vanishes there, so $c_1D_{t_1,v}[(u,\sigma_{t_1}(u))]=0$;
and $c_1\ne0$, since $c_1=0$ forces $D_{t_2,v}=0$. Hence
$D_{t_1,v}[(u,\sigma_{t_1}(u))]=0$, which is the first displayed equality; the
second is symmetric.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[$f_1(4)=6<f(4)=h^{\ast}(4)=7$]\label{fs15:f1-four}
No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=4$ has an all-switches run
of length $7$, degenerate or not; and one with a run of length $6$ exists. So
$f_1(4)=6$, while $f(4)=h^{\ast}(4)=7$ is attained by the two-player game
$G^{\sharp}$ of \Cref{prop:auso-seven}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $L=7$. The AUSO $s'$ of \Cref{cor:ceiling-general} has a
bottom-antipodal walk of length $7$, so its height is at least $7=h^{\ast}(4)$,
hence exactly $7$; by \Cref{prop:auso-census} --- recomputed here from the
census of all $12640$ classes --- there is exactly one such class, of $384$
outmaps. Enumerating that orbit and, in each of its members, every start of
height $7$, gives $768$ pairs (outmap, walk). In each pair, the incidences
$(t,v)$ with $v\notin S_t$, $s'(\sigma_t\oplus2^v)=S_t\mathbin{|}2^v$ and
$\sigma_t\oplus2^v$ off the walk --- the only ones a tie can occupy, by
\Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c),(d) --- number at most one. So $|T|\le1$ and
\Cref{fs15:run-hk} supplies a Holt--Klee AUSO of the $4$-cube with a
bottom-antipodal walk of length $7$. But the greatest bottom-antipodal height
of a Holt--Klee AUSO of the $4$-cube is $6$: the census gives heights
$1,2,3,4,5,6$ for $1,423,2503,2401,729,56$ Holt--Klee classes and the single
height-$7$ class is not Holt--Klee. Contradiction.

For the lower bound, the one-player game
\texttt{AP\_m4\_k0\_den256\_s200} of \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} --- four Max
vertices, ninety-four average, denominator $256$ --- is stopping, every row of
its normal form leaking, is nondegenerate, and its all-switches run from
$\sigma=2$ is $2,8,5,9,13,14,15$, of length $6$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The second blow-up level needs Min vertices, ties allowed]\label{fs15:b2-oneplayer}
Let $W=\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_{10}$ be the bottom-antipodal walk of
$B^{2}$, the second level of \Cref{thm:blowup} seeded at the $1$-cube: on the
$5$-cube with the representative
\[
  B^{2}=(4,7,2,5,1,0,6,3,9,24,14,27,28,31,10,29,25,16,30,19,20,23,26,21,17,8,22,11,12,15,18,13),
\]
$W=13,18,12,16,9,17,1,6,0,4,5$ and
$S=31,30,28,25,24,16,7,6,4,1,0$. (The first level here is
$(1,0,6,3,4,7,2,5)$, the orientation of \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} translated
by $1$; the second level is a USO, acyclic, of height $10$, and not
Holt--Klee, as recorded there.) No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ has
$W$ as an all-switches run --- degenerate or not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose one does, and let $s'$ be the AUSO of \Cref{cor:ceiling-general}, so
$s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ for $0\le t\le10$. An exhaustive depth-first enumeration of
the outmaps of the $5$-cube subject to those eleven values and to the
Szab\'o--Welzl condition (which already forces injectivity) returns $1897$
unique sink orientations, of which $875$ are acyclic --- $B^{2}$ among them ---
and \emph{none} is Holt--Klee. By \Cref{fs15:run-hk} the tie set $T$ therefore
satisfies $0\in\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t,v}\}$, so $|T|\ge2$.

By \Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c),(d), $T$ is contained in the set of $(t,v)$ with
$v\notin S_t$, $s'(\sigma_t\oplus2^v)=S_t\mathbin{|}2^v$ and
$\sigma_t\oplus2^v\notin W$. Over the $875$ orientations that set is
$\emptyset$ ($180$ times), $\{(7,3)\}$ ($297$), $\{(5,2)\}$ ($162$) or
$\{(5,2),(7,3)\}$ ($236$) --- never anything else. Hence
$T=\{(5,2),(7,3)\}$ and
$c_1D_{5,2}+c_2D_{7,3}=0$ with $c_1,c_2>0$.

Read that identity in the coordinate $(x_2,0)$ of $\mathbb R^{2m}$. Now
$\sigma_5=17$ has action $0$ at $x_2$, so
$D_{5,2}$ has entry $y^{\sigma_5}_{x_2,0}\ge1$ there, the second term
$y^{\sigma_5[x_2]}$ being supported on action $1$ at $x_2$; while $\sigma_7=6$
and $\sigma_7[x_3]=14$ both have action $1$ at $x_2$, so $D_{7,3}$ vanishes
there. The identity reads $c_1y^{\sigma_5}_{x_2,0}=0$, and
$y^{\sigma}\ge\bbone$ by \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}. Contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:b2-remark}
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured} says that the second level ``is not Holt--Klee, so
any realisation needs Min vertices''. Read through \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}
that argument covers nondegenerate realisations of the \emph{orientation};
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer} covers realisations of the \emph{walk}, which is all a
run needs, and covers degenerate ones. The two steps are independent of each
other: the first is that no Holt--Klee orientation agrees with the walk even at
its eleven vertices, which is stronger than $B^{2}$ itself failing Holt--Klee
and is what the walk-only relaxation would otherwise buy; the second is that
the two ties the combinatorics permits cannot both occur.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Walk realisation is a linear programme in the value vectors]\label{fs15:walk-lp}
Fix $m$, $k$, a walk $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ of Max strategies with
$S_t=\sigma_t\oplus\sigma_{t+1}$ and $S_L=\emptyset$, value vectors
$x_0,\dots,x_L\in\mathbb R^{n}$, $n=m+k$, and Min actions
$\tau_0,\dots,\tau_L\in\{0,1\}^{k}$. Consider the system, in the $2n$ rows
$(p^{w,a},q^{w,a})\ge0$ of a harmonic normal form:
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
  w\in\Vmax,\ \sigma_t(w)=a: & \langle p^{w,a},x_t\rangle+q^{w,a}=x_t(w),\\
  w\in\Vmax,\ \sigma_t(w)\ne a: & \langle p^{w,a},x_t\rangle+q^{w,a}\ \ge\ x_t(w)+\delta\ \ (w\in S_t),\quad
                                  \le x_t(w)\ \ (w\notin S_t),\\
  u\in\Vmin,\ \tau_t(u)=a: & \langle p^{u,a},x_t\rangle+q^{u,a}=x_t(u),\\
  u\in\Vmin,\ \tau_t(u)\ne a: & \langle p^{u,a},x_t\rangle+q^{u,a}\ \ge\ x_t(u),\\
  \multicolumn{2}{l}{|p^{w,a}|_1+q^{w,a}\le1-\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }(w,a).}
 \end{array}
\]
It is linear, and the constraints for distinct $(w,a)$ involve disjoint
unknowns, so it splits into $2n$ independent linear programmes in $n+1$
nonnegative unknowns and at most $L+2$ constraints. Any solution with
$\delta>0$ is a stopping game whose all-switches run from $\sigma_0$ is
exactly $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ and whose value vectors along it are the
$x_t$; conversely every such game furnishes a solution, with $x_t:=\val_{\sigma_t}$
and $\tau_t$ a Min best response. Ties off the run are unconstrained, and ties
on it are exactly the inequalities met with equality.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Strict substochasticity makes each frozen operator a contraction, so
$\val_{\sigma_t}$ is its unique fixed point; the equalities together with the
Min inequalities say precisely that $x_t$ is that fixed point, and the Max
inequalities say precisely that $S(\sigma_t)=S_t$. The run visits only
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$, so no other strategy is constrained. Disjointness of
the unknowns is immediate: the row $(w,a)$ occurs in no condition indexed by a
different $(w',a')$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:walk-lp-remark}
\Cref{fs15:walk-lp} is the search this route used, and it inverts the
parametrisation of \Cref{prop:auso-seven}'s integer search and of
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured}'s: there the rows are the unknowns and the value
vectors are a rational function of them, so every condition is nonlinear; here
the value vectors are the unknowns and the rows are the output of $2n$ small
exact linear programmes. On $G^{\sharp}$ the reconstruction is immediate: from
its eight value vectors and Min responses alone the programme returns a
stopping game whose run from $\sigma=8$ is again $8,6,11,7,13,5,1,0$.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The separability hypothesis is not vacuous]\label{fs15:escape-real}
There is a one-player stopping SSG with four Max vertices whose all-switches
run carries two tied incidences at the \emph{same} Max vertex with opposite
actions, and whose two occupancy differences are exactly anti-parallel, so that
$0\in\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t,v}\}$ and the hypothesis of \Cref{fs15:run-hk}
fails. Its harmonic normal form has denominator $8$: with
$(p^{v,a};q^{v,a})$ listed over the targets $(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3;t_1)$,
\[
 \begin{array}{r@{\quad}l@{\qquad}l}
  x_0: & (0,\tfrac14,0,\tfrac18;\tfrac38) & (0,0,0,\tfrac18;0)\\
  x_1: & (\tfrac18,0,\tfrac14,\tfrac14;0) & (0,\tfrac12,\tfrac14,0;0)\\
  x_2: & (\tfrac14,0,\tfrac14,0;\tfrac18) & (0,\tfrac18,\tfrac18,0;0)\\
  x_3: & (0,\tfrac18,\tfrac18,\tfrac14;0) & (0,0,\tfrac14,0;0).
 \end{array}
\]
Every row leaks, so the game is stopping. Its all-switches run from
$\sigma_0=6$ is $6,0,10$; the incidences $(\sigma_0,x_3)$ and
$(\sigma_2,x_3)$ are tied, with $\sigma_0(x_3)=0$ and $\sigma_2(x_3)=1$; and
\[
  D_{0,x_3}=(0,0,0,\tfrac38,0,0,\tfrac32,-\tfrac98),\qquad
  D_{2,x_3}=-\tfrac{880}{819}\,D_{0,x_3}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
An exact rational computation from the displayed rows: the value vectors along
the run, the sixteen margins, the two occupancy vertices of each tied edge, and
the ratio. Independently, the Knuth--Yao construction of \Cref{lem:gadget}'s
kind turns those rows into an explicit stopping SSG on $31$ vertices --- four
Max, twenty-five average, two sinks --- whose greatest trap is empty and on
which the run, the value vectors and the two ties, recomputed from the game by
taking profile values, agree with the table.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:escape-remark}
So \Cref{fs15:run-hk} cannot be stated without its hypothesis, and
\Cref{fs15:two-ties} is sharp: the only two-tie configuration it leaves open is
the one \Cref{fs15:escape-real} exhibits. Whether that configuration can occur
on a run \emph{longer} than $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$ --- which is what a
one-player superpolynomial family would need --- is the gap this route leaves.
The instance above has a run of length $2$, well under
$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(4)=6$, and both of the walks of
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer,fs15:h12-oneplayer} rule the configuration out on
combinatorial grounds alone. Random search finds the configuration rarely: over
$15000$ one-player normal forms with $m=3$ and denominator $8$ ($120000$ runs,
$38782$ of them carrying a tie) it occurred once, and over $4000$ with $m=4$
and denominator $8$ ($64000$ runs, $24090$ with a tie) once.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[What the searches did and did not show]\label{fs15:search-remark}
\Cref{fs15:walk-lp} was also run as a search, over the value vectors and over
the game manifold with the programme as an inner optimal repair, on
$G^{\sharp}$'s own walk with two Min vertices and on the walk of
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer} with one and with two Min vertices. None converged:
after $3$--$5\times10^{4}$ evaluations each they plateau at a total hinge
violation near $6\times10^{-3}$. Since the calibration target ---
$G^{\sharp}$'s walk, which the programme reconstructs instantly from
$G^{\sharp}$'s own value vectors --- also fails, these runs are evidence about
the search and not about the instances, exactly as
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured} says of the earlier ones.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[The height-$12$ witness of \Cref{prop:hstar-five} needs Min vertices]\label{fs15:h12-oneplayer}
No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ has
\[
  0,\,15,\,24,\,31,\,20,\,23,\,18,\,14,\,26,\,10,\,2,\,3,\,1
\]
--- the bottom-antipodal walk of length $12=h^{\ast}(5)$ of the outmap printed
in \Cref{prop:hstar-five} --- as its all-switches run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The thirteen values $s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ determine the orientation completely:
the depth-first enumeration of \Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer}'s kind returns exactly
one outmap of the $5$-cube compatible with them, namely the printed one, and it
is not Holt--Klee. So \Cref{fs15:run-hk} makes the tie set $T$ non-separable,
whence $|T|\ge2$; and by \Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c),(d) the only incidences a
tie can occupy are $(t,v)=(0,4)$ and $(7,1)$, with partners $16$ and $12$ off
the run. Hence $T=\{(0,4),(7,1)\}$. But $\sigma_7=14$ has action $1$ at the
Max vertex $x_1$ while $\sigma_0=0$ has action $0$ there, so
\Cref{fs15:two-ties} applies with $v_1=x_1$, $v_2=x_4$ and contradicts
non-separability.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[A decision procedure for one-player realisability of a walk]\label{fs15:screen}
The three impossibility results above are instances of one finite test, which
takes a walk $W$ of the $m$-cube and returns either ``no one-player stopping
SSG has $W$ as its all-switches run'' or ``undecided''. Enumerate every outmap
$s'$ of the $m$-cube with $s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ along $W$ --- the Szab\'o--Welzl
condition forces injectivity and prunes hard, so this is a small search: $1$
completion for the walk of \Cref{fs15:h12-oneplayer}, $1897$ (of which $875$
acyclic) for that of \Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer}. Discard the cyclic ones. If some
survivor is Holt--Klee, return undecided. Otherwise compute, for each survivor,
the legal candidate tie set of \Cref{fs15:tie-partner}; if for every survivor
every candidate set is separable in the sense of \Cref{fs15:run-hk} --- for
which \Cref{fs15:two-ties} is usually enough --- return the impossibility. The
cost is dominated by the completion enumeration and is independent of any
search over games. Applied to the $768$ length-$7$ walks of the $4$-cube it
gives $f_1(4)=6$; applied to the two $5$-cube walks above it gives
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer,fs15:h12-oneplayer}. What it does not give is a bound
on $f_1(5)$: that would need the test on every length-$12$ walk of the
$5$-cube, of which \Cref{prop:hstar-five}'s enumeration counts $347640$ from
$\sigma_0=0$, about $2900$ up to the coordinate permutations that fix
$\sigma_0$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The top average vertex}\label{sec:fs15-top}

\Cref{lem:alphabet-cover} already contains the structure that the question
about the largest average value needs, and two consequences of it are worth
recording before the question is answered.

\begin{corollary}[The second letter is at least a half]\label{fs15:nu-half}
Let $G$ be stopping with $\Vavg\ne\emptyset$ and let
$\nu:=\max_{c\in\Vavg}\val(c)$. Then every value of $G$ is $1$ or at most
$\nu$, and $\nu\in\{0\}\cup[\tfrac12,1]$. Dually the least positive letter is
at most $\tfrac12$, and more generally the letters
$1=\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\dots$ satisfy $\lambda_i\ge2^{1-i}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every letter $\lambda\in(0,1)$ is attained at an average vertex by
\Cref{lem:alphabet-cover}, so no value lies strictly between $\nu$ and $1$, and
$\nu$ is the second letter. If $0<\nu<1$ then \Cref{lem:alphabet-cover} writes
$\nu=\tfrac12(\lambda_i+\lambda_j)$ with $\lambda_i<\nu<\lambda_j$; the only
letter above $\nu$ is $1$, so $\nu=\tfrac12(1+\lambda_i)\ge\tfrac12$. The same
lemma gives $\lambda_i\ge\tfrac12\lambda_{i-1}$ for every interior $i$, whence
$\lambda_i\ge2^{1-i}$; the dual statements are \Cref{lem:duality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:half-free}
So $\max_{v}\val(v)\ge\tfrac12$ unless every value is $0$ or $1$, and which of
the two holds is decided in linear time by the attractor sweeps that compute
$\{\val=0\}$ and $\{\val=1\}$. The question ``does some vertex have value at
least $\tfrac12$?'' is therefore free, while ``does \emph{this} vertex have
value at least $\tfrac12$?'' is \Cref{prob:main}. The threshold $\tfrac12$
plays no part in the difficulty; the naming of a vertex does.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[$\textsc{Top}$ is the whole problem]\label{fs15:top}
Let $\textsc{Top}$ be the problem: given a stopping SSG with
$\Vavg\ne\emptyset$, output an average vertex of maximum value. Then
$\textsc{Top}$ is polynomial-time equivalent to \Cref{prob:main}, by a
reduction making a single oracle call.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
One direction is trivial. For the other, by \Cref{prop:no-halving}(b) it is
enough to reduce the comparison of two vertices $p,q$ of a stopping $G$ to
$\textsc{Top}$. Compute $\{\val=1\}$ and $\{\val=0\}$ by the attractor sweeps
and redirect every edge into them to $t_1$ and $t_0$ respectively; values are
unchanged, the game stays stopping, and afterwards every non-sink value lies in
$(0,1)$. If $p$ or $q$ has been absorbed into a sink the comparison is already
decided; otherwise let $a:=|\Vavg|$ of the reduced game --- if $a=0$ every
value is $0$ or $1$ and there is nothing to decide --- and put $r:=2a+2$,
$m:=r+2$.

Adjoin a reference chain $e_1\to(t_1,t_0)$, $e_{j+1}\to(t_1,e_j)$ of $r$
average vertices, so $\val(e_j)=1-2^{-j}$; and two boost chains
\[
  c^{(1)}_p\to(t_1,p),\quad c^{(j+1)}_p\to(t_1,c^{(j)}_p),
  \qquad
  c^{(1)}_q\to(e_r,q),\quad c^{(j+1)}_q\to(t_1,c^{(j)}_q),
\]
of $m$ average vertices each. Nothing new is a successor of anything old, so
the old values are unchanged and the game is still stopping. By induction
\[
  \val(c^{(m)}_p)=1-\frac{1-\val(p)}{2^{m}},\qquad
  \val(c^{(m)}_q)=1-\frac{1-\val(q)+2^{-r}}{2^{m}} .
\]
Both are at least $1-2^{-(m-1)}=1-2^{-(r+1)}$, which strictly exceeds every
$\val(e_j)\le1-2^{-r}$ and every old average value: an old value is $<1$ with
denominator dividing an integer at most $2^{a}$ (\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}),
hence at most $1-2^{-a}$, and $r+1>a$. Within each boost chain the values
increase with $j$, so the maximum over $\Vavg$ is attained at $c^{(m)}_p$ or at
$c^{(m)}_q$ (an intermediate of one chain may well exceed the top of the other,
which does not matter), and
\[
  \val(c^{(m)}_p)>\val(c^{(m)}_q)
  \iff \val(p)>\val(q)-2^{-r}.
\]
Two distinct old values differ by at least $2^{-2a}>2^{-r}$, again by
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}, and $\val(q)-\val(p)=2^{-r}$ is impossible for
the same reason; so the right-hand side holds exactly when
$\val(p)\ge\val(q)$, the maximiser is unique, and the single oracle answer
decides the comparison. The construction adds $r+2m=O(a)$ vertices.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:top-remark}
So the answer to the question raised for \Cref{thm:order-determines} is that
naming the top average vertex buys the whole game and costs the whole game:
\textsc{Top} joins \Cref{thm:compare-equivalence,thm:decide-one-bit,%
prop:no-halving,cor:wrong-equivalence,rem:alphabet-equivalence} on the list of
target-equivalent reformulations. The peeling recursion it suggests --- know
the top letter, remove it, recurse --- is blocked at the first step for the
reason \Cref{prop:no-halving}(a) gives: removing a letter means substituting a
known value, and that costs $a$ fresh average vertices.
\end{remark}

EIGHT of the route's nine results are already in frontier.tex, and the ninth is worth one corollary. Integrating the route as written would make the paper WORSE.

WHAT HAPPENED. frontier.tex is now 11838 lines, not the 10856 the route was briefed on. Commit 9fafa72 (2026-09-03 02:53) integrated sec:ties from the concurrently-running round-15 "degenerate" route; the route's own fs15.tex was last written at 02:24. The two routes independently built the same theory. This is not dishonesty by free-search-15 -- it had no way to know -- but the integration decision must treat the overlap as duplication, and it is total:

  fs15:run-hk          = lem:tie-perturb.  The route's hypothesis "0 not in conv{D_{t,v}}" is exactly the Gordan dual of the paper's (star), and the paper SAYS SO ("This is the shape Gordan's alternative predicts: (star) is infeasible exactly when some nonnegative combination of the vectors y^{sigma_t}-y^{sigma_t[v]} vanishes").
  fs15:tie-partner     = the (F1)-(F4) apparatus of lem:seven-flat, plus thm:no-seven's opening ("c_{A(sigma_t)} := sigma_t is a consistent choice of corners").
  the whole premise ("prop:oneplayer-lp uses nondegeneracy only at the end") = sec:ties' second paragraph, verbatim in content.
  |T| <= 1 is free     = cor:one-tie (which is STRONGER: all ties at one vertex with the SAME action).
  fs15:f1-four         = thm:no-seven + cor:hstar-one (STRONGER: h*_1(m) = 1,2,4,6 for m <= 4, both bounds).
  fs15:h12-oneplayer   = the paragraph after prop:hkfive (STRONGER: the whole orbit of s_12, both length-12 starts, not one walk).
  fs15:escape-real     = prop:no-linear-tiebreak (STRONGER: also counts the 96 acyclic completions, 74 Holt-Klee, and confirms L <= h*_HK(4) survives there).
  fs15:nu-half         = two lines from lem:alphabet-cover; the route says so itself.
  fs15:walk-lp         = the design method of prop:b2-realised's proof ("its rows were fixed by exact linear programming over the normal form"), which the gadget route used to SUCCEED on the very instance fs15's outer search failed on.

Even the individual tools are paper-resident: the Szabo-Welzl completion enumeration is prop:hkfive's program, the unit-vertex-capacity Holt-Klee test is cor:seven-two-player's, and h*_HK(5)=11 is now proved (prop:hkfive), not "measured, unverified".

WHAT SURVIVES. fs15:b2-oneplayer, and only that. I rebuilt the enumeration from scratch (independent USO/acyclicity/Holt-Klee/BA-walk library, /tmp/.../audit-fs15-sig/ind.py) and reproduce the route exactly: 1897 USO completions of the B^2 walk, 875 acyclic, ZERO Holt-Klee, legal candidate tie sets exactly {}, {(5,2)}, {(7,3)}, {(5,2),(7,3)} with counts 180/162/297/236; sigma_5 = 17 takes action 0 at bit 2 while sigma_7 = 6 takes action 1, so fs15:two-ties applies. The result is correct, is NOT in the paper, and is NOT reachable by sec:ties' method: B^2's walk has length 10 <= 11 = h*_HK(5), so the height argument gives nothing and the walk-completion screen is genuinely needed. It is now the exact sharpness complement to prop:b2-realised, which realises that walk with FIVE Max and ONE Min: that one Min vertex is necessary, ties allowed. That is the m=5 analogue of what thm:no-seven did for cor:seven-two-player, and it is worth one corollary in sec:ties.

I also independently reproduced the m=4 half (384 orbit outmaps, 768 length-7 pairs, candidate-tie distribution 384 x {one} + 384 x {none}, every discarded candidate having its partner on the walk) -- so fs15:f1-four is correct, just already proved.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG, none fatal to a conclusion.
(1) fs15:two-ties-cor(ii) is VACUOUS, and fs15:escape-remark's sharpness claim is false. The route reads only the coordinate (v_1, a_1); reading the COMPLEMENTARY coordinate (v_1, 1-a_1) kills case (ii) in one line (see finding). So the route's "dichotomy" is strictly WEAKER than the paper's prose assertion it was meant to sharpen -- prop:no-linear-tiebreak's surrounding text already says the same-vertex-opposite-actions configuration is the only one, and it is right.
(2) fs15:walk-lp claims "Any solution with delta>0 is a stopping game". It is a harmonic normal form, not a game. Rows -> fair-coin SSG is unverified item (v4), and the route's own calibration output (t_gsharp.py) contains the row margin 16360316286458789090051467880599179/2247486763375641182884452430940917760, whose denominator has a 100-bit ODD part -- realising that as a first-passage law of a fair-coin average part needs an eventually-periodic binary expansion of astronomical period. Every realisation in the paper (prop:auso-seven, prop:b2-realised, rem:hk-survey) rounds to a small dyadic denominator and then verifies from the explicit game, precisely because of this.
(3) The stated gap carries a false "equivalently" (see finding).

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. No algorithm, no polynomial class, no lower-bound family, no barrier: it covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi. This is the regime rem:flat already describes for the whole AUSO-ceiling programme -- "no bound on any algorithm, no polynomial class, no barrier and no lower-bound family". fs15:top is honestly self-declared as ending at a target-equivalent statement, which by rule 4 is a blocked route, and it is the seventh such reformulation.

HONESTY. Good, in the two places it matters. The sampling (15000 games at m=3, 4000 at m=4) is used only to report the RARITY of a configuration exhibited by an explicit instance, never to support a claim. The failed searches are reported with the calibration control failing and the correct caveat that they are evidence about the search and not about the instances -- and prop:b2-realised, which found the game the route could not, proves that caveat was exactly right.

RECOMMENDATION. Integrate ONE result: fs15:b2-oneplayer, restated inside sec:ties in the paper's own vocabulary (cor:one-tie plus the completion enumeration of prop:hkfive plus the same-vertex-opposite-actions lemma), as a corollary sharpening prop:b2-realised. Optionally add fs15:top as one paragraph to the target-equivalence list (thm:compare-equivalence, thm:decide-one-bit, prop:no-halving, cor:wrong-equivalence, rem:alphabet-equivalence), after deleting the collapsed vertices in the proof. Reject everything else as duplicate. Take from the route's next-steps the ONE item the paper explicitly says its own method cannot reach: the paragraph after prop:hkfive concedes "This does not give h*_1(5) <= 11"; the walk-level screen does, by running the completion+tie test on all 347640 length-12 sequences (about 2900 up to the 120 permutations fixing sigma_0), and that would extend cor:hstar-one to m=5. Also worth doing while the screen is being written: replace fs15:two-ties-cor with the corrected single-case dichotomy, and record the general form the complementary-coordinate reading gives -- at every Max vertex v carrying a tie with action a, either some tie at v with action 1-a carries positive weight, or some tie (t,u) with u != v has sigma_t(v) = 1-a -- which is the first constraint anyone has on tie sets of size >= 3.

findings.defect: Case (ii) of the dichotomy is vacuous, so the corollary is strictly weaker than the prose claim in frontier.tex it was meant to upgrade, and the accompanying sharpness claim in fs15:escape-remark ('fs15:two-ties is sharp: the only two-tie configuration it leaves open is the one fs15:escape-real exhibits') contradicts the corollary's own statement. The route reads only the coordinate (v_1, a_1), where D_{t_2,v_2} need not vanish; reading the complementary coordinate (v_1, 1-a_1) closes the case in one line.
findings.evidence: Let T={(t1,v1),(t2,v2)} with v1!=v2 and sigma_{t1}(v1)=sigma_{t2}(v1)=a1 (case ii). y^sigma is supported exactly on {(u,sigma(u))} with entries >=1 (prop:oneplayer-lp). At (v1,1-a1): y^{sigma_t1} has 0, y^{sigma_t1[v1]} has >=1, so D_{t1,v1} <= -1 there; sigma_t2 and sigma_t2[v2] both take a1 at v1 (v2!=v1), so D_{t2,v2}=0 there. Then c1 D_1 + c2 D_2 = 0 with c1,c2>=0 forces c1=0, hence c2 D_2=0 with c2>0, hence D_2=0, false. Case (i) survives the same test, as it must (opposite signs at (v,1-a)). Written up at /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-fs15-sig/CASE_II_DEAD.md. Consistent with the route's own report that all three sampled escapes were type (i).

findings.defect: The proposition asserts 'Any solution with delta>0 is a stopping game whose all-switches run from sigma_0 is exactly sigma_0,...,sigma_L'. A solution is a harmonic normal form -- a set of substochastic affine rows -- not a game. Turning arbitrary rational rows into a def:ssg game (fair coins, out-degree two) is unverified item (v4) of the standing list, and the size is unbounded: a non-dyadic row needs an eventually-periodic binary expansion whose period is the multiplicative order of 2 modulo the odd part of the denominator. Every realisation in frontier.tex (prop:auso-seven, prop:b2-realised, rem:hk-survey) instead rounds to a small dyadic denominator and then verifies the outmap from the explicit game -- exactly the step this proposition skips.
findings.evidence: The route's own calibration run, t_gsharp.py, returns per-row margins including 16360316286458789090051467880599179/2247486763375641182884452430940917760; that denominator has odd part 548702823089756148165149519272685 (about 100 bits), so it is not dyadic and is not the first-passage law of any average part of reasonable size. The route calls this output a 'rebuilt game'.

findings.defect: The stated gap contains a false 'equivalently'. Escaping fs15:run-hk requires only that 0 lie in conv{D_{t,v}} over the whole tie set T; fs15:two-ties constrains PAIRS only. With case (ii) dead the |T|=2 analysis is complete, but |T|>=3 is untouched -- Gordan's alternative then needs a nonnegative combination of three or more vectors and no pair need be anti-parallel. So 'a run longer than h*_HK(m)' is not equivalent to 'a type-(i) two-tie configuration on a long run'. The true gap: whether some one-player stopping SSG has an all-switches run of length > h*_HK(m) whose tied incidences on the run carry occupancy differences D_{t,v} = y^{sigma_t} - y^{sigma_t[v]} that positively span 0 -- a tie set of ANY size, not two.
findings.evidence: fs15:two-ties and its corollary are stated for exactly two tied incidences; nothing in the route bounds |T| or handles |T|>=3. frontier.tex states the gap correctly at the end of prop:no-linear-tiebreak's discussion: 'Whether every one-player stopping game satisfies L <= h*_HK(|Vmax|) remains open.'

findings.defect: Correct and new, but the written proof is wrong at one step: 'redirect every edge into them to t_1 and t_0 respectively; ... afterwards every non-sink value lies in (0,1)'. Redirecting leaves the value-1 and value-0 vertices in place, and a surviving value-1 AVERAGE vertex is then the unique maximiser, so the TOP oracle returns it and the reduction fails. The vertices must be deleted (they are unreachable after the redirection). The route's code does delete them, so this is a writeup slip, not a mathematical error. Separately, the result is by the route's own admission a seventh target-equivalent reformulation, i.e. a blocked route under rule 4.

The arithmetic checks out: r=2a+2, m=r+2, both chain tops exceed 1-2^{-(r+1)} > 1-2^{-a}, and val(q)-val(p)=2^{-r} is impossible since distinct values differ by at least 2^{-2a} > 2^{-r}.

result.route: verify-r14 — independent verification and paste-ready LaTeX for the round-14 results still outside frontier.tex
result.headline: Fifteen round-14 items re-derived from their statements in exact arithmetic: eleven INTEGRATE as they stand, four need a stated repair (Q_16's vertex count, cor-selfread's superfluous hypothesis, thm:prec-contract-class's precision, and two formula errors plus one wrong "iff" reading in lasserre-2); g(6)=21 and h*_HK(5)=11 both confirmed by independent exhaustive search; and item (6) is answered in the NEGATIVE — FV(n), n>=3, is a permanent stall for M2, M2T and M4, so the few-denominator class does contain stalls (proved, not measured).

results.name: bsr:prop-switches (Q_16, a Min vertex switched four times)
results.statement: The reduced stopping game Q_16 (8 Max, 8 Min, rows over c_1..c_16,t_1 in 64ths) admits, from sigma_0=(0,0,1,1,0,0,1,0), tau_0=(0,0,1,1,1,1,0,1), a non-strict BSI run of 5 rounds in which the Min vertex c_10 is switched FOUR times; the strict rule takes 5 rounds with switch multiset [1^11]; the number of tied incidences (sigma,i) over the 256 Max strategies is 1072.
results.argument: Rebuilt the game from the printed LaTeX table (not from the route's code) and checked it entry-by-entry against four_switch_rows.json: identical. All 32 rows have row-sum < 1 (max 11/16), so every positional pair is absorbed a.s. and the reduced game is stopping. val_sigma computed as the componentwise MIN over all 2^8 positional tau (never greedy policy iteration); val^tau as the componentwise MAX over all 2^8 sigma. BSI as def:bsi verbatim. The printed six-line trace is reproduced line for line, including every C_max and C_min; switch multiset [1^11,2,4] with c_10 four times; strict variant 5 rounds, multiset [1^11]. Halting pair has L = U on all 16 controlled vertices with w*(c_1) = 11337633945805671/51622576448108128447, which equals the independent brute-force max over all 256 Max strategies of val_sigma. Tied incidences: 1072 at the Max vertices (also, new: 944 at the Min vertices, 2016 over all 16).
results.verification: q16.py, q16check.py, q16ties.py/.out. REPAIR NEEDED: 'a stopping SSG on 258 vertices, a=240' is not canonical -- the count depends on the order in which a row's targets are laid on the leaves of its depth-d tree. Vertex-index order gives a=270 (N=288); the order round 14 happened to use gives a=240 (N=258); decreasing-mass order gives a=238 (N=256). I built the N=256 realisation myself, verified it stopping by the trap characterisation, certified L and U at every BSI round as the UNIQUE fixed points of T_sigma and T^tau on it (legitimate by thm:contraction), and recomputed C_max, C_min from the realised game: identical at every round. Write 'at most 258' or fix the leaf order. VERDICT: INTEGRATE with that one-word repair.

results.name: bsr:lem-bias (same-successor bias)
results.statement: If v in Vmax has successors p in Vmax and q in Vavg with the same successor pair {a,b}, then val^tau(p) >= val^tau(q) for every tau, with equality iff val^tau(a)=val^tau(b); so strict BSI never endorses p->q, non-strict endorses it only at equality, q->p is always endorsed when improving, and p->q is val_sigma-improving at v iff p is strictly switchable at sigma.
results.argument: val^tau is the value of the Max-only game with Min frozen, so val^tau(p) = max{val^tau(a),val^tau(b)} and val^tau(q) = (val^tau(a)+val^tau(b))/2: a maximum dominates a mean, with equality only when the arguments agree. The vetoes of def:bsi read off directly. Last clause: val_sigma(p) = val_sigma(sigma(p)) with sigma(p) in {a,b}, so val_sigma(q) > val_sigma(p) iff val_sigma(sigma-bar(p)) > val_sigma(sigma(p)).
results.verification: Two-line proof, checked. Computationally confirmed on all 15 configurations of this shape in the ladders L_n, n=2..6 (bsi_v.py) and on the 5 configurations that random search produced. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: bsr:prop-selfdual (BSI on a self-dual game is the one-sided rule MR)
results.statement: On a stopping self-dual G with involution phi, val^{phi(sigma)}(x) = 1 - val_sigma(phi(x)) for every x including the sinks; from a mirrored pair every BSI round produces a mirrored pair, C_min = phi(C_max), and C_max = {v in S_sigma : val_sigma(phi(sigma-bar(v))) <= val_sigma(phi(sigma(v)))} (< for the strict variant), so BSI collapses to the one-sided rule MR reading val_sigma and phi only.
results.argument: Freezing Min to phi(sigma) leaves a Max-only stopping game whose dual phi carries isomorphically onto G_sigma; lem:duality gives the identity off the sinks, and at the sinks both sides read 1 at t_1 and 0 at t_0 because phi exchanges them. Substituting U = 1 - L o phi into def:bsi turns S^{phi(sigma)} into phi(S_sigma) and the Min veto into the Max veto, so C_min = phi(C_max) and tau[C_min] = phi(sigma[C_max]).
results.verification: bsi_v.py: 60 random self-dual stopping games (built by choosing successors on one half and mirroring), both variants, WHOLE trajectories -- the identity checked at every vertex including sinks, C_min = phi(C_max) at every round, the mirrored-pair invariance after every update, and the identification with MR at every round. 0 violations. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: bsr:prop-normal (normalisation preserves the BSI trajectory)
results.statement: For the bipartite normal form N'(G) of lem:normalform, val_{sigma~} = val_sigma and val^{tau~} = val^tau on V(G) with the value of u at both gadget vertices; hence S, S^tau, C_max, C_min and the whole BSI run coincide, for both variants; likewise for N_k of def:kblind.
results.argument: lem:normalform(iii) is the statement for val_sigma. The gadget uses only average vertices and is inserted exactly at the edges whose two endpoints are controlled -- a condition invariant under exchanging players and sinks -- so N'(G-bar) = the dual of N'(G) under the same naming; lem:normalform(iii) applied to G-bar and carried back by lem:duality is the statement for val^tau. Each of the four tests of def:bsi then compares two unchanged numbers.
results.verification: bsi_nf.py: N'(G) built from scratch (with the sinks carried as SENTINELS -- the first attempt collided the fresh vertex indices with t_0 and produced 149 spurious mismatches, which is exactly the trap the standing rules record), 40 random two-player stopping games, both variants, whole trajectories: identical lengths, identical C_max/C_min at every round, identical L and U on V(G), and both gadget vertices carrying val(u) for L and for U. 0 violations. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: deg:prop-hk5 (h*_HK(5) = 11)
results.statement: h*(m) = 1,2,4,7,12 and h*_HK(m) = 1,2,4,6,11 for m <= 5. No Holt-Klee AUSO of the 5-cube has BA height 12; the printed outmap (7,14,28,13,24,25,26,27,15,16,17,22,19,4,5,18,30,29,0,31,3,10,12,9,23,2,8,1,11,20,21,6) is a Holt-Klee AUSO of height 11 attained along 0->7->28->23->30->11->29->9->25->27->26->18; and prop:hstar-five's height-12 witness violates Holt-Klee on the 3-face with free directions {1,2,3} through sigma = 16.
results.argument: Every BA trace of an AUSO obeys cor:no-return, cor:law-b and cor:law-u, so an exhaustive DFS over law-abiding sequences enumerates a superset of the traces. Up to translation (sigma_0 = 0) and coordinate permutation (S_0 an initial segment) -- all three laws, the USO axioms, acyclicity and Holt-Klee being invariant under those -- there are exactly 2064 length-12 sequences at m=5 (my count agrees with round 14's). For each, all completions of the outmap to a unique-sink map were enumerated by DFS with most-constrained-variable ordering, testing acyclicity and Holt-Klee on each face as soon as that face becomes fully assigned. NO Holt-Klee acyclic completion exists.
results.verification: cube.py (USO / acyclicity / BA walk / Holt-Klee by unit-capacity vertex-split max flow), laws.py, hk5.py, seq12.json. THREE CONTROLS, all passed: (i) the same enumeration with the HK test removed finds 288 of the 2064 traces realisable, and the FIRST completion it returns is exactly the outmap printed in prop:hstar-five; (ii) the same program at m=4 returns 0 HK completions of the 34 canonical length-7 traces and 320 of the 524 length-6 ones, reproducing h*(4)=7 and h*_HK(4)=6; (iii) a from-scratch enumeration of all 8! outmaps of the 3-cube reproduces prop:auso-census's 744 USOs, 728 acyclic, 656 acyclic-and-HK and h*(3)=h*_HK(3)=4. DISCREPANCY (bookkeeping only): my completion search visits 5787 nodes, round 14 reports 94002 -- different pruning, same conclusion. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: deg:prop-g and deg:prop-g6 (the law ceiling g = 1,2,4,7,12,21)
results.statement: With g(m) the greatest L admitted by cor:no-return + cor:law-b + cor:law-u, g(m) = 1,2,4,7,12 for m <= 5 and g(6) = 21, so h*(m) <= g(m) <= f(m) with g(5) = h*(5) = 12 < 13 = f(5) and g(6) = 21 < 25 = f(6).
results.argument: All three laws are invariant under translation and coordinate permutation, so sigma_0 = 0 and S_0 an initial segment may be assumed. Left-to-right DFS: choosing S_t needs (sigma_u xor sigma_t) not-subset-of S_t and (S_u sym-diff S_t) meet (sigma_u xor sigma_t) nonempty for u < t; setting sigma_{t+1} needs (sigma_u xor sigma_{t+1}) meet S_u nonempty for u <= t. These tests cover every pair the three laws constrain, since law (U) at t' = L is cor:no-return.

At m = 6 the search was split 16 ways at t=1 and the last part a further 12 ways at t=2; ALL 27 parts terminate with maximum 21, visiting 3.4e11 nodes in all. results.name: deg:prop-nondeg4 (a nondegenerate 253-vertex realisation of B' with the same run)
results.statement: B'_nd, obtained from B' of prop:overshoot-small by replacing the edge in slot k of vertex v by a chain of j_{v,k} average vertices delivering the head with probability 1-2^{-7}-2^{-j}, t_0 with 2^{-7} and t_1 with 2^{-j}, for the listed 24 exponents, is a stopping one-player SSG on 253 vertices, nondegenerate (0 of 64 incidences tied), with improvement outmap (12,15,14,13,0,11,10,9,4,3,2,1,8,5,7,6), an AUSO satisfying Holt-Klee of BA height 6, whose all-switches run from sigma_0=(1,1,1,0) is again of length 6 switching {0,3},{0,1,2},{0,1},{1},{2},{3}.
results.argument: Finite exact computation. All 24 gadget first-passage laws verified from the chain description (c_i -> (w,c_{i+1}) for i<j, i != 7; c_7 -> (t_0,c_8); c_j -> (t_1,w)) to equal (1-2^{-7}-2^{-j}, 2^{-7}, 2^{-j}); total chain length 239, so N = 12 + 239 + 2 = 253.
results.verification: bprime.py, bnd_build.py. Built the explicit 253-vertex game; verified stopping by the trap characterisation; certified all 16 val_sigma as fixed points of T_sigma on the explicit game (unique by thm:contraction), so the reduced 12-variable model is faithful; 0 tied incidences; outmap matches the printed one exactly; is a bijection, satisfies the USO condition, is acyclic, passes Holt-Klee on every face, BA height 6, walk 7->14->9->10->8->12->4; run length 6 with the printed switched sets. Also re-verified the B'_7 facts it cites: exactly 10 of 64 incidences tied, ALL at value 0, run length 6 with those switched sets, final val(0) = 34611559809/37019025280 -- all matching prop:overshoot-small. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: deg:prop-zeroties (damping cannot remove a tie at value zero)
results.statement: If G^flat replaces each edge u->w by a damping chain of arbitrary edge-dependent length k_e >= 0, then for every Max strategy sigma the zero set of val^{G^flat}_sigma on V(G) equals the zero set of val^G_sigma, namely the trapping set Z_sigma, which depends on the digraph and sigma alone. Hence every incidence tied at value 0 stays tied, whatever the k_e; in particular no such perturbation makes B' nondegenerate.
results.argument: By lem:trap it suffices to show that the greatest sigma-trap of G^flat meets V(G) in the greatest sigma-trap Z of G. (Superset) U := Z union {chain vertices of edges whose head lies in Z} is a sigma-trap of G^flat: an average chain vertex keeps both successors (the head, in Z, and the next chain vertex, or t_0 which lies in Z); an average v in Z has both G-successors in Z so both chain heads in U; a Max v in Z keeps sigma(v)'s chain head; a Min v in Z keeps some chain head; and t_1 is not in U. (Subset) W := Z^flat meet V(G) is a sigma-trap of G: a chain head in Z^flat is average, so BOTH its successors -- including the head w -- lie in Z^flat, giving both G-successors of an average v in W, and one successor of a controlled v in W. Finally, if both successors of a Max vertex have value 0 then both chain heads have value (1-2^{-k})*0 + 2^{-k}*0 = 0.
results.verification: Proof re-derived line by line; it is correct and holds for arbitrary SSGs with Min vertices present, and uses no probability. The last clause re-measured: B'_7 has exactly the ten ties {(1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(3,1),(3,2),(5,1),(5,2),(6,2),(7,1),(7,2)}, all at value 0, and under 400 random per-edge chain-length assignments in {7,...,13} the SAME ten incidences stay tied in all 400 (bprime.py). VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: allswlower:lem-isolated (no return to an isolated configuration)
results.statement: If S_t is contained in W then sigma_{t'}|_W differs from sigma_t|_W for every t' > t; in particular a vertex that switches alone never switches again, and a sub-game that runs in isolation for one round can never be reset to that local configuration.
results.argument: cor:no-return gives Delta(sigma_t, sigma_{t'}) meet S_t nonempty, and S_t is contained in W, so the two strategies differ somewhere on W. For (i) take W = {v} and use that v has two actions.
results.verification: It IS cor:no-return restated, exactly as the task suspected: the proof is one line and uses nothing else. VERDICT: INTEGRATE, but AS A COROLLARY of cor:no-return with the one-line proof (drafted in the LaTeX), not as a lemma. Its content is the two readings (i) and (ii), which are worth keeping.

results.name: allswlower:cor-selfread (a self-reading vertex switches exactly at its loop value)
results.statement: On a ONE-PLAYER stopping SSG with sigma, p in Vmax, a = sigma(p), b = sigma-bar(p), h = h(b->p) and ell the value of b conditioned on never visiting p: h < 1, val_sigma(b) = h val_sigma(a) + (1-h) ell, p is strictly switchable at sigma iff ell > val_sigma(a), and then val_{sigma[p]}(p) = ell.
results.argument: h < 1 is the second paragraph of thm:impedance's proof (a chain returning to p with probability one is never absorbed) -- so it is a CONCLUSION, not a hypothesis. Conditioning at the first visit to p, with val_sigma(p) = val_sigma(a), gives the decomposition. Since 1-h > 0 the decomposition makes val_sigma(b) > val_sigma(a) equivalent to ell > val_sigma(a). thm:impedance at v = p, where h(p->p)=1, gives val_{sigma[p]}(p) - val_sigma(a) = (val_sigma(b)-val_sigma(a))/(1-h) = ell - val_sigma(a).
results.verification: selfread.py: 1028 (game, sigma, p) triples over random one-player stopping SSGs, all three conclusions exact, 0 failures. REPAIR: the hypothesis 'p is not reachable from a under sigma' is NEVER USED and should be DELETED -- 269 of those 1028 triples VIOLATE it and satisfy all three conclusions. The hypothesis 'h < 1' should likewise move from the hypotheses to the conclusions. VERDICT: INTEGRATE with both hypotheses removed (the statement is strictly stronger, and the remark allswlower:rem-laws that uses it is unaffected).

results.name: las2:thm-two (the degree-two lift is exact at |C| <= 2)
results.statement: The degree-two Lasserre relaxation L_1(G) of las2:def-relax is exact on every stopping SSG with |C| <= 2, with no nondegeneracy hypothesis.
results.argument: Proof re-derived line by line and correct. I re-verified the expansion identity: for M the moment matrix and S := Y - u u^T, the constraint alpha-tilde^{v,0T} M alpha-tilde^{v,1} = 0 is exactly a_{v,0}(u) a_{v,1}(u) + alpha^{v,0T} S alpha^{v,1} = 0; with u in Q-tilde the first summand is >= 0, giving alpha^{v,0T} S alpha^{v,1} <= 0. Writing S as a Gram matrix and using las2:lem-rows (p^{v,i}_v < 1), the sign is that of <x_v - Y_v, x_v - Z_v> with Y_v, Z_v in the convex hull of the other x_j together with x_0 = 0; bilinearity reduces to the vertices. At c = 2 the vertex values at v=1 are A, A-g, A+B-2g with the first and third nonnegative, so A=0 or A<=g or x_1=x_2, and dually at v=2; if A<=g and B<=g then g>0 unless A=B=0, and Cauchy-Schwarz forces A=B=g, i.e. x_1=x_2. In each surviving case (x_1=x_2, x_1=0, x_2=0) the two products are computed to be >= 0, hence 0; then a_{v,0}(u) a_{v,1}(u) = 0 with u in Q-tilde says Tu = u, so u = w*|_C by thm:contraction.
results.verification: Proof checked; corroborated by sampling over exact 2x2 PSD S and admissible rows (las2two.py: 3563 hits at c=1 and 19 at c=2 with all products <= 0, every one of them with BOTH products exactly 0; c=3 random sampling produces 0 hits, which is uninformative and is exactly why las2:rem-c3's engineered configuration is needed). REPAIR OF THE READING: the task's phrasing 'exact iff |C| <= 2' is NOT a theorem and must not be written. Exactness holds at |C| = 3 and 4 on CYC(3,lambda,W) and CYC(4,lambda,W) for every lambda, by las2:thm-cyc(a). What is sharp is the UNIFORM statement: exact on every stopping SSG with |C| <= 2, and false on some stopping SSG with |C| = 3 (thm:lasserre-vacuous). VERDICT: INTEGRATE the theorem; REPAIR the 'iff' reading.

results.name: las2:lem-local (the local criterion) and las2:thm-w10 / las2:thm-w14
results.statement: (a) If (u,Y) in L_1 has u != w*|_C then X := (Y-uu^T) + udot udot^T is PSD, nonzero, and alpha_v^T X beta_v = -gamma_v theta_v with theta_v = s_v alpha_v . udot >= 0, udot = A^{-1}(s .* theta), theta != 0. (b) Conversely, from X > 0 with alpha_v^T X beta_v <= 0 for all v and < 0 for some v one builds (u_t, Y_t) in L_1 with u_t != w*|_C.
results.argument: (a) Using a_{v,sigma(v)}(w*) = 0 one has a_{v,sigma(v)}(u) = alpha_v.udot and a_{v,1-sigma(v)}(u) = s_v gamma_v + beta_v.udot; substituting into the constraint and adding (alpha_v.udot)(beta_v.udot) gives alpha_v^T X beta_v = -(alpha_v.udot) s_v gamma_v = -theta_v gamma_v. (b) tX - t^2 udot udot^T is PSD for t <= (udot^T X^{-1} udot)^{-1}, and the computation of (a) run backwards gives the equalities exactly: the coefficient of t is theta_v gamma_v + f_v = 0.
results.verification: las2w.py: W_10 and W_14 rebuilt from their graphs; w* by brute force = (1/2,1/2,1/4,1/2,1/4,7/16,3/8,1/4) and (1/2,1/2,15/32) on the controlled vertices, exactly as printed; harmonic normal forms exactly as printed; gamma = (1/4,1/16,3/16) on W_10; the printed (u,Y) verified to lie in L_1 exactly (moment matrix PSD by exact LDL, box, Q-tilde, all three equalities exactly 0) with S positive definite. las2:lem-local(a) checked on both witnesses (X PSD, alpha^T X beta = -gamma*theta exactly, theta >= 0 and nonzero, udot = A^{-1}(s.*theta)); (b) checked by rebuilding a fresh witness at t = 1/4 from X on both games. VERDICT: INTEGRATE (these two theorems are already in the paper as thm:lasserre-vacuous; the verification confirms them and the engine).

results.name: las2:thm-cyc (the spectral criterion on CYC) and las2:prop-rlt, las2:prop-cyc-rlt
results.statement: On CYC(c,lambda,W) the degree-two relaxation is exact iff min_k psi_lambda(cos 2pi k/c) >= 0, where psi_lambda(t) = 2 lambda^2 t^2 - 2 lambda t + 1 - lambda^2. Consequently it is exact at c = 3,4 for every lambda and fails for every c >= 6 at lambda = 3/4 and every c >= 5 at lambda = 15/16. One RLT round R(G) is exact on W_10 and NOT on W_14, where max x(v_i) = 25/42, 7/12, 9/16. And for lambda <= lambda_0 = 0.754877... (the root of l^3+l^2=1) the local system of las2:lem-rlt-local is unsolvable on CYC(c,lambda,W) for every c and W, so L_1^+ is exact there.
results.argument: Averaging a witness over the cyclic shift makes X a PSD circulant with X_{i,i} - 2 lambda X_{i,i+1} + lambda^2 X_{i,i+2} = (1/c) sum_k mu_k psi_lambda(cos theta_k); this is the criterion, and E_k + eps I realises it. For prop-cyc-rlt: alpha_v^T X alpha_w = g_{v-w} with g_m = (1/c) sum nu_k cos(m theta_k), nu_k = mu_k G(theta_k) >= 0, G(theta) = |1 - lambda e^{i theta}|^2; Phi = psi_lambda(cos .)/G = Re((1-lambda z)/(1-lambda z-bar)) expands as (1-l^2) - l^3 cos theta + (1-l^2) sum_{n>=2} l^n cos n theta (I re-derived this expansion); the second constraint family says g_m >= 0 for all m, so -gamma theta_0 >= (1-l^2) g_0 - l^3 g_1 >= (1 - l^2 - l^3) g_0 >= 0 using g_1 <= g_0, forcing theta = 0.
results.verification: las2cyc.py, las2w.py, las2rlt.py. CYC verified stopping with w* == W, gamma_i = W(1-lambda), first action optimal. Part (a)'s four psi evaluations are exact identities. The criterion's exact/fail pattern reproduced for c = 3..15 at lambda = 3/4 (exact up to c=5, fails from c=6) and lambda = 15/16 (fails from c=5). EXPLICIT RATIONAL witnesses (u_t, Y_t) built by las2:lem-local(b) and verified to lie in L_1 exactly for CYC(6,3/4,1/2), CYC(7,3/4,1/2), CYC(5,15/16,1/2) and, freshly, CYC(9,3/4,1/2) and CYC(12,3/4,1/4). las2:prop-rlt reproduced by exact two-phase simplex over R(G) with all 4|C| rows and all their pairwise products: W_10 gives (1/2,1/2), (1/2,1/2), (1/4,1/4) -- exact -- and W_14 gives max (25/42, 7/12, 9/16) and min (1/2, 1/2, 15/32), exactly as printed. las2:prop-cyc-rlt corroborated by an exact LP OUTER relaxation (X's PSD constraint dropped, so infeasibility is a proof): infeasible for every c = 3..7 and lambda in {1/2, 3/4, 19/25, 7/8, 15/16, 31/32, 63/64}, including 19/25 > lambda_0. TWO REPAIRS: (b) 'min over [-1,1] of psi_lambda = 1/2 - lambda^2 attained at t = 1/(2 lambda)' holds only for lambda >= 1/2 (at lambda = 1/4 the minimum on [-1,1] is 9/16 at t = 1); the conclusion is unaffected. (c) the printed roots t_pm = 1/(2l) +- sqrt(2l^2-1)/(sqrt2 l) are wrong by a factor sqrt2 -- the discriminant is 4 l^2 (2l^2-1), so t_pm = 1/(2l) +- sqrt(2l^2-1)/(2l); the printed numerical arcs were computed from the CORRECT formula (25.53, 64.47, width 38.94 at l=3/4, matching '25.5, 64.5, 39.0'), except that at l = 15/16 the arc is (3.96 deg, 86.04 deg) of width 82.08, not (3.7, 86.0) of width 82.4. VERDICT: INTEGRATE all four with those two formula repairs.

results.name: cor:prec-characterisation (the escape class, intrinsically)
results.statement: A family carries escape certificates with log_2(1/lambda) >= 1/poly(N) and log_2 kappa = poly(N) if and only if 1 - Lambda(G) >= 1/poly(N), where Lambda = max over the 2^{|C|} profiles of rho(M_pi).
results.argument: (=>) is thm:prec-rate(i) (Collatz-Wielandt). (<=) With Lambda <= 1 - 1/p take lambda := 1 - 1/(3p); then lambda^2 >= 1 - 2/(3p) >= Lambda so rho(A_pi) = rho(M_pi)/lambda <= lambda < 1, and the certificate x = (I-A_pi)^{-1} 1 of thm:prec-rate(ii) has kappa(x) <= ||x||_inf, bounded by Cramer with |det(I-A_pi)| >= (1-lambda)^n (every eigenvalue of A_pi has modulus <= lambda) and Hadamard on the cofactors; the log is polynomial because log_2 1/(1-lambda) = log_2(3p). Then log_2(1/lambda) >= 1/(3p) and thm:escape-class applies.
results.verification: prec3.py: the equivalence 'an escape certificate at rate lambda exists <=> rho(M_pi) < lambda for every profile' tested on 120 random stopping SSGs with three random rational rates each (360 tests), the left side by an exact two-phase simplex over {1 <= x <= 2^40, Sx <= lambda x} and the right by the exact M-matrix criterion. 0 mismatches. ATTRIBUTION (from memory, unchecked against the source): Lambda = max_pi rho(M_pi) is the joint spectral radius of the row-rectangular family {M_pi}, and the identification of the JSR of such a family with the largest spectral radius among its finitely many selections is Blondel-Nesterov; it is also the standard MDP fact that the optimal growth rate of a rectangular nonnegative family is attained by a stationary policy. VERDICT: INTEGRATE with that attribution.

results.name: thm:prec-contract-class (the contracted class) -- REPAIR REQUIRED
results.statement: The two-sided rounded iteration of T-hat returns val on every stopping SSG with C nonempty and stops in O((a + log kappa-hat)/log(1/lambda-hat)) rounds; hence SSG-Value is in P on every family with 1 - Lambda-hat(G) >= 1/poly(N), a class containing the escape class.
results.argument: The route's own width bound is ||u-hat_k - l-hat_k||_inf <= kappa-hat lambda-hat^k + kappa-hat 2^{1-p}/(1-lambda-hat) (which I re-derived in the x-hat-weighted norm and confirm). Its SECOND term is below 4^{-a} only if p >= 2a + log_2 kappa-hat + log_2 1/(1-lambda-hat) + O(1). The stated precision p := Theta(a + log_2 1/(1 - Lambda-hat)) DROPS the factor kappa-hat, so as written the algorithm is not shown to reach width 4^{-a} at all.
results.verification: prec2.py verifies thm:prec-contract (i), (iii), (iv) on 68 random stopping games (T-hat fixes val|_C; rho(R-hat_pi) <= rho(M_pi) for all 2^{|C|} profiles by exact bisection; the bracket holds for 12 rounds). THE REPAIR, stated: since neither kappa-hat nor lambda-hat is available to the algorithm, run the rounded iteration with p = 2, 4, 8, ... , restarting, 2^s rounds at p = 2^s, and stop when the width falls below 4^{-a}. Directed rounding preserves l-hat_k <= val|_C <= u-hat_k at EVERY precision, so the algorithm is correct for every p and the schedule is legitimate; it reaches the correct p within a factor 2 in rounds and O(log p) restarts. With that change the theorem is proved (full proof in the LaTeX). VERDICT: REPAIR then INTEGRATE.

results.name: prop:prec-wedge (the wedge defeats the contraction, at the same rate)
results.statement: For WD(e,j,m) the contracted matrix has R-hat(v_i,a;.) = 0 and R-hat(v_i,b;v_{3-i}) = 1 - 2^{1-j}, so Lambda-hat = 1 - 2^{1-j} exactly, independent of e and m; and the two-sided contracted iteration halts on WD(2j,j,j+4) after 4, 8, 17, 35, 70, 140 rounds for j = 2..7 and after 4 rounds on WD(e,2,6) for every e = 2..7.
results.argument: Under the a-branch the passage from v_i returns to v_i with probability 1 - 2^{-e} and otherwise reaches H, hence a sink, so the row normalisation annihilates it. Under the b-branch, b_i returns to v_i with probability 1/2 and otherwise enters c_{i,1}, from which v_{3-i} is reached with probability 1 - 2^{1-j} and w_1, hence a sink, otherwise; dividing by 1/2 gives the entry. Every R-hat_pi is zero, has one nonzero row, or is antidiagonal with both entries 1 - 2^{1-j}; only the last has nonzero spectral radius.
results.verification: prec.py, prec2.py: the harmonic normal form of WD computed exactly from the graph for j = 2,3,4,5 gives R(v_i,a;.) = (1-2^{-e}) e_i with alpha = 1-2^{-e} and R(v_i,b;.) with alpha = 1/2 and mass (1-2^{1-j})/2 on v_{3-i}, so R-hat is exactly as claimed (1/2, 3/4, 7/8, 15/16). The exact two-sided iteration of T-hat reaches width 0 after 4, 8, 17, 35, 70, 140 rounds for j = 2..7 -- exactly the numbers of prop:wedge -- and, on a FRESH larger instance, 281 at j = 8; and after 4 rounds on WD(e,2,6) for every e = 2..7. VERDICT: INTEGRATE as stated.

results.name: v14:prop-fv-stall (item 6: the few-denominator class DOES contain stalls)
results.statement: For n >= 3, on FV(n) and FV_2(n) of prop:fv-family -- which have D(G) = 3 and are solved by thm:few-denominator in O(N^2) operations -- the slack calculus M2 and its min-plus closure M2T, seeded with Z_0, Z_1 and read in BOTH directions of rem:own-successor at EVERY controlled vertex, never fire, at any round; and the one-shot Z-seeded transport test M4 fires at no controlled vertex either. The value-simulation preorder M1 decides every controlled vertex, and the seeded hybrid M5 decides every controlled vertex at round two or three.
results.argument: Every controlled vertex has two successors of EQUAL value, so direction (ii) can never fire and direction (i) needs an upper bound on a difference that is exactly 0 to ATTAIN 0. Write W(x,y) := w*(x)-w*(y); soundness of the calculus is D >= W implies F(D) >= W, so F(W) >= W. Every entry of F(D) is a minimum of finitely many expressions, each a constant or a max / min / mean / min-plus path sum of entries of D. On D = W + c*Psi with Psi a 0/1 matrix, each expression is piecewise affine in c with breakpoints at (differences of attainable W-combinations)/(differences of attainable Psi-combinations); on FV(n) every value of w* lies in {0,1/3,2/3,1}, so every attainable W-combination is a multiple of 1/6 and every Psi-combination lies in [0,N], hence NO breakpoint lies in (0, 1/(6N)) and F(W + c Psi) = F(W) + c*Theta there, with Theta independent of c. Take K = 14, S := {(x,y) : D_K(x,y) > W(x,y)}, Psi := 1_S, t := min(min_S(D_K - W), 1/(12N)). The three finite exact checks F(W) >= W, Theta >= Psi/2, D_K >= W + t*Psi then give D_{K+j} >= W + t 2^{-j} Psi for every j by induction, so D_k > W on S for ever. At each controlled vertex the two '<= 0' entries lie in S with W = 0 there (hence stay strictly positive) and the two '< 0' entries have W >= 0 (hence are never negative).
results.verification: fv.py (the mechanisms), fvproof2.py (the proof). All three checks pass in exact arithmetic for n = 3,4,5,6 and for both FV and FV_2 and both variants; at n = 2 the check correctly FAILS, matching the measurement that M2 does fire on FV(2) at round 4. Measured alongside: Delta_k(X_0, L_0) = 2^{-floor((k-1)/2)} on FV(3), still 1/549755813888 at k = 60. M1 fires at every controlled vertex on FV(n) and FV_2(n) for n = 2..5 (and its preorder is sound there); M4 with BOTH directions and the Z seed fires at no controlled vertex; M5 fires at round 2 (round 3 at one vertex of FV_2(3)). VERDICT: this is the answer to item (6) and it is the OPPOSITE of the escape class's sentence -- INTEGRATE, together with the remark v14:rem-fewden explaining that all the stalls it supplies are vacuous (no controlled vertex is value-distinguishing) and stating the GAP below.

result.gap: Whether the few-denominator class contains a NON-vacuous stall. Precisely: exhibit a stopping SSG with D(G) = poly(N) carrying a value-distinguishing controlled vertex on which the Z-seeded own-successor test for the transport-slack hybrid of sec:hybrid is silent for superpolynomially many rounds, or prove that none exists. (A small denominator forces every nonzero value gap to be at least 1/D(G) >= 1/poly(N), but that alone bounds nothing: thm:slack-vi-upper converts a gap into a firing round only through the two-sided value-iteration width, whose rate thm:contraction bounds by (1-2^{-a})^{k/N} and which D(G) does not control.)
result.next_steps: 1. Integrate the eleven clean items as they stand (bsr:lem-bias, bsr:prop-selfdual, bsr:prop-normal, bsr:prop-switches, deg:prop-g, deg:prop-g6, deg:prop-hk5, deg:prop-nondeg4, deg:prop-zeroties, las2:thm-cyc/prop-rlt/prop-cyc-rlt, cor:prec-characterisation, prop:prec-wedge). 2. Apply the four repairs before integrating: (a) Q_16's realisation is 'at most 258 vertices' (the count depends on the gadget's leaf order; decreasing-mass order gives 256); (b) delete the hypothesis 'p is not reachable from a under sigma' from allswlower:cor-selfread and move 'h < 1' to its conclusions; (c) fix the two errors in las2:thm-cyc(b) (the minimum formula needs lambda >= 1/2; the roots are 1/(2l) +- sqrt(2l^2-1)/(2l), and the arc at lambda = 15/16 is (3.96 deg, 86.04 deg) of width 82.08) and never write 'exact iff |C| <= 2' -- exactness holds at |C| = 3, 4 on CYC; (d) put the missing log_2 kappa-hat into thm:prec-contract-class's precision and state the doubling schedule that removes the need to know kappa-hat and lambda-hat. 3. Turn allswlower:lem-isolated into a corollary of cor:no-return. 4. Add v14:prop-fv-stall and v14:rem-fewden as the missing sentence for thm:few-denominator, and record the GAP above. 5. Note in rem:flat that the '1,2,4,7,12,21' ceiling is now a verified computation, not just a recorded measurement: g(6) = 21 was confirmed by an independent C search over 3.4e11 nodes, and h*_HK(5) = 11 by an independent completion search with three controls (including a from-scratch re-derivation of prop:auso-census at m = 3). 6. Do NOT integrate prop:prec-Gm(b) (refuted elsewhere); I did not re-examine it.

\begin{lemma}[Same-successor bias]\label{bsr:lem-bias}
Let $v\in\Vmax$ have successors $p\in\Vmax$ and $q\in\Vavg$ with the same
successor pair $\{a,b\}$, as every $v_i$ of the ladder $L_n$ of
\Cref{thm:ladder} has. Then for every Min strategy $\tau$,
$\val^\tau(p)\ge\val^\tau(q)$, with equality if and only if
$\val^\tau(a)=\val^\tau(b)$. Hence the strict variant of \Cref{def:bsi} never
endorses the switch of $v$ from $p$ to $q$, and the non-strict variant
endorses it only when $\val^\tau(a)=\val^\tau(b)$, while the switch from $q$
to $p$ is endorsed whenever it is improving. Moreover the switch $p\to q$ is
$\val_\sigma$-improving at $v$ if and only if $p$ itself is strictly
switchable at $\sigma$. Dually at $\Vmin$ with $\val_\sigma$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\val^\tau$ is the value of the one-player game in which Min is frozen to
$\tau$, so it is the least fixed point of $T^\tau$ and satisfies
$\val^\tau(p)=\max\{\val^\tau(a),\val^\tau(b)\}$ at the Max vertex $p$ and
$\val^\tau(q)=\tfrac12(\val^\tau(a)+\val^\tau(b))$ at the average vertex $q$;
a maximum dominates a mean, with equality only when the two arguments agree.
The veto for $p\to q$ at $v$ reads $\val^\tau(q)\ge\val^\tau(p)$ (resp.\ $>$),
and the veto for $q\to p$ reads $\val^\tau(p)\ge\val^\tau(q)$, which always
holds. For the last claim, $\val_\sigma(p)=\val_\sigma(\sigma(p))$ and
$\val_\sigma(q)=\tfrac12(\val_\sigma(a)+\val_\sigma(b))$ with
$\sigma(p)\in\{a,b\}$, so $\val_\sigma(q)>\val_\sigma(p)$ if and only if
$\val_\sigma(\bar\sigma(p))>\val_\sigma(\sigma(p))$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Self-dual games: BSI is a one-sided rule]\label{bsr:prop-selfdual}
Let $G$ be stopping and \emph{self-dual}: there is an involution $\phi$ of $V$
with $\phi(t_0)=t_1$, $\phi(\Vmax)=\Vmin$, $\phi(\Vavg)=\Vavg$ and
$\phi(x^{(i)})=\phi(x)^{(i)}$ for every non-sink $x$, so that $\phi$ is an
isomorphism of $G$ onto its dual $\bar G$. For a Max strategy $\sigma$ let
$\phi(\sigma)$ be the Min strategy $\phi(v)\mapsto\phi(\sigma(v))$. Then
\[
  \val^{\phi(\sigma)}(x)=1-\val_\sigma(\phi(x))\qquad (x\in V,\ \text{sinks included}),
\]
and from a mirrored pair $(\sigma,\phi(\sigma))$ every BSI round produces a
mirrored pair, with $C_{\min}=\phi(C_{\max})$ and
\[
  C_{\max}=\bigl\{v\in S_\sigma:\ \val_\sigma(\phi(\bar\sigma(v)))\le
  \val_\sigma(\phi(\sigma(v)))\bigr\}
\]
($<$ for the strict variant). So on self-dual games from mirrored starts BSI
is the one-sided rule $\mathrm{MR}\colon\sigma\mapsto\sigma[C_{\max}]$, which
reads $\val_\sigma$ and $\phi$ only; by \Cref{thm:bsi-nostall} it returns a
nonempty subset of $S_\sigma$ whenever $S_\sigma\ne\emptyset$, so it is a
switching rule in the sense of \Cref{def:rule}. It endorses the switch of $v$
to $q$ exactly when Min's best response to $\sigma$ at the mirror vertex
$\phi(v)$ weakly (resp.\ strictly) prefers $\phi(q)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Freezing Min to $\phi(\sigma)$ in $G$ leaves a Max-only stopping game; its
dual is a Min-only stopping game which $\phi$ carries isomorphically onto
$G_\sigma$, the game with Max frozen to $\sigma$. \Cref{lem:duality} gives
$\val^{\phi(\sigma)}=1-\val_\sigma\circ\phi$ off the sinks, and at the sinks
both sides read $1$ at $t_1$ and $0$ at $t_0$ because $\phi$ exchanges them.
Substituting $U=1-L\circ\phi$ with $L=\val_\sigma$ in \Cref{def:bsi}:
$u=\phi(v)$ lies in $S^{\phi(\sigma)}$ iff $U(\phi\bar\sigma(v))<U(\phi\sigma(v))$
iff $L(\bar\sigma(v))>L(\sigma(v))$ iff $v\in S_\sigma$; and the Min veto
$L(\bar\tau(u))\le L(\tau(u))$ reads $L(\phi\bar\sigma(v))\le L(\phi\sigma(v))$,
which is the Max veto $U(\bar\sigma(v))\ge U(\sigma(v))$ at $v$. Hence
$C_{\min}=\phi(C_{\max})$ and $\tau[C_{\min}]=\phi(\sigma[C_{\max}])$, so the
new pair is mirrored again. The last sentence restates the veto:
$L(\phi q)\le L(\phi p)$ says that $\phi(q)$ attains
$\min\{L(\phi p),L(\phi q)\}=L(\phi v)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Normalisation preserves BSI]\label{bsr:prop-normal}
Let $N'(G)$ be the bipartite normal form of \Cref{lem:normalform} and
$\sigma\mapsto\tilde\sigma$, $\tau\mapsto\tilde\tau$ its bijections on the two
strategy sets. Then $\val^{N'(G)}_{\tilde\sigma}=\val^{G}_\sigma$ and
$\val_{N'(G)}^{\tilde\tau}=\val_{G}^{\tau}$ on $V(G)$, both taking at the two
gadget vertices replacing an edge $(v,u)$ the value of $u$; consequently
$S_{\tilde\sigma}=S_\sigma$, $S^{\tilde\tau}=S^\tau$,
$C_{\max}(\tilde\sigma,\tilde\tau)=C_{\max}(\sigma,\tau)$ and
$C_{\min}(\tilde\sigma,\tilde\tau)=C_{\min}(\sigma,\tau)$ for both variants,
so the BSI runs on $(G,\sigma_0,\tau_0)$ and on
$(N'(G),\tilde\sigma_0,\tilde\tau_0)$ have the same length and pass through
corresponding pairs. The same holds for the $k$-blinding normalisation $N_k$
of \Cref{def:kblind}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{lem:normalform}(iii) is the statement for $\val_\sigma$. The gadget
$v\to c_{v,u}$, $c_{v,u}\to(u,d_{v,u})$, $d_{v,u}\to(u,c_{v,u})$ uses only
average vertices and is inserted at exactly the edges whose two endpoints are
controlled, a condition invariant under exchanging the players and the sinks;
hence $N'(\bar G)=\overline{N'(G)}$ under the same vertex naming, and
\Cref{lem:normalform}(iii) applied to $\bar G$, carried back by
\Cref{lem:duality}, is the statement for $\val^\tau$. Each of the four tests
of \Cref{def:bsi} compares two numbers that are therefore unchanged. For
$N_k$ use \Cref{lem:kblind}(ii) in the same way.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The law bound]\label{deg:prop-g}
Let $g(m)$ be the greatest $L$ such that some sequence
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ in $\{0,1\}^{m}$ with
$S_t:=\sigma_t\oplus\sigma_{t+1}\ne\emptyset$ for $t<L$ and $S_L:=\emptyset$
obeys \Cref{cor:no-return}, \Cref{cor:law-b} and \Cref{cor:law-u}. Then
$g(m)=1,2,4,7,12$ for $m=1,\dots,5$ and $g(6)=21$, so that
$h^{\ast}(m)\le g(m)\le f(m)$ with $g(5)=h^{\ast}(5)=12<13=f(5)$ and
$g(6)=21<25=f(6)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
All three laws are invariant under translation of the cube and under
permutation of the coordinates, so $\sigma_0=0$ and $S_0=\{1,\dots,k\}$ may be
assumed. The sequences are built left to right by depth-first search:
choosing $S_t$ requires $(\sigma_u\oplus\sigma_t)\not\subseteq S_t$
(\Cref{cor:law-b}) and $(S_u\bigtriangleup S_t)\cap(\sigma_u\oplus\sigma_t)\ne
\emptyset$ (\Cref{cor:law-u}) for every $u<t$, and setting
$\sigma_{t+1}:=\sigma_t\oplus S_t$ requires
$(\sigma_u\oplus\sigma_{t+1})\cap S_u\ne\emptyset$ for every $u\le t$
(\Cref{cor:no-return}); between them these tests cover every pair the three
laws constrain, since \Cref{cor:law-u} at $t'=L$ is \Cref{cor:no-return}. The
search is exhaustive. $h^{\ast}\le g$ because a bottom-antipodal trace obeys
all three laws (\Cref{lem:auso-laws}, \Cref{cor:law-u}), and $g\le f$ because
\Cref{cor:law-u} is an extra constraint.
\end{proof}
